With a voice sweet and sublime, captivating like the song of the karavīka bird, he proclaims for the hearers the Four Noble Truths, elucidated through a gradual discourse.

64.

64.

Paṭigaṇhiya dhammamādarā

Nijavohāra’nurūpagocaraṃ,

Abhiyāti padakkhiṇena sā

Parisātaṃ sirasā’bhivandiya; () (Pacchābhattakiccaṃ)

Having received the Dhamma with reverence, each according to their own practice and sphere, that assembly, having paid homage with their heads, departs by circumambulating.

66. [O 0.0464]

66.

Varavāraṇakumbhadāraṇo

Migarājāva kudiṭṭhabhañjano,

Atha niṭṭhitadhammagajjano

Muniru’ṭṭhāyu’pavesanā’sanā; ()

Like one who splits the frontal globe of a great elephant, like a king of beasts who crushes wrong views, then, having concluded his thundering of the Dhamma, the Sage rises from his seat.

65.

65.

Kamalaṃ’va kalevaraṃ varaṃ

Vimalaṃ vitarajomalaṃ jino,

Avasiñcitukāmavā sace

Pavisitvāna nahānakoṭṭhakaṃ; ()

The Victor’s excellent body, like a lotus, is immaculate, free from dust and defilement; if he wishes to bathe, he enters the bathing chamber.

67.

67.

Tadūpaṭṭhitikena bhikkhunā

Paṭiyattenudakena viggahe,

Samitotuparissamo muhuṃ

Punarāgamma nivatthacīvaro; ()

With water prepared for his body by the attending monk, his fatigue from the climate is allayed for a moment; having returned, he dons his robe.

68. [O 0.0465]

68.

Sunisajja sina’ssame same

Pariveṇe ṭhapitāsanopari,

Anubhoti muhutta mattanā

Suvimutto’pi vimuttijaṃ sukhaṃ; ()

Having sat down comfortably in his own peaceful hermitage, upon a prepared seat in his cell, though completely liberated, he experiences for a moment the bliss born of liberation.

69.

69.

Tadupaṭṭhitipaccupaṭṭhitā

Abhinikkhammatatotatoyatī,

Mahitañjalipupphamañjarī

Parivārentitilokanāyakaṃ; ()

Then the ascetics, being in attendance and ready, surround the Leader of the Three Worlds as he emerges from that place, honoring him with hands clasped in reverence and with clusters of flowers.

70.

70.

Paṭipattipapūraṇakkamaṃ

Paṭipucchanti vipucchanāni’pi,

Yatayo hi visuṃvisuṃ jinaṃ

Savaṇaṃ dhammakathāya yācare; ()

Indeed, the ascetics, each one separately, ask the Victor questions concerning the method for fulfilling the practice; they also request to hear a Dhamma talk.

71.

71.

Bhagavā karuṇāya codito

Tadadhippāya mavecca buddhiyā,

Abhisādhaya matthamuttamaṃ

Purimaṃ yāmamatikkame iti; () (Purimayāmakiccaṃ)

Urged by compassion, the Blessed One, having understood their intention with his wisdom, accomplishes the supreme purpose; thus he passes the first watch.

72. [O 0.0466]

72.

Bhagavanta manantadassinaṃ

Sirasā tesugatesu bhikkhusu,

Abhivandiya jātikhettato

Labhamānā’vasaraṃ surāsurā; ()

When those bhikkhus had departed, the devas and asuras, obtaining an opportunity from their birth-realm, paid homage with their heads to the Blessed One, the Boundless Seer.

73.

73.

Upagamma tapovanaṅgaṇaṃ

Kurumānā chavivaṇṇapiñjaraṃ,

Maṇimoḷimaricisañcaya-

Paricumbīkaḷitaṃ sirimato; ()

Having approached the courtyard of the hermitage, making it tawny-colored with their radiance, the collection of rays from their jeweled crests touched the Glorious One.

74.

74.

Nakhakesaramaṅgulīdalaṃ

Caraṇambhojayugaṃka pavandiya,

Caturakkharikampi pucchare

Varapañha’ntamaso’hisaṅkhataṃ; ()

Having worshipped his pair of lotus-feet, with their toe-petals and nail-filaments, they ask even a four-syllable question, the supreme question that is said to dispel darkness.

75. [O 0.0467]

75.

Sivado vadataṃanuttaro

Muni vissajjati tabbipucchanaṃ,

Atha vitakathaṅkathi tada-

Bbhanumodanti abhitthavantipi; ()

The Sage, unsurpassed among speakers and giver of peace, answers their questions. Then, their doubt dispelled, they rejoice and also praise him.

76.

76.

Nijadhammapadīpatejasā

Janasammoha tamovidhaṃsano,

Iti majjhimayāma manvahaṃ

Katakicco muni vītināmaye; () (Majjhimayāmakiccaṃ)

With the radiance of the lamp of his own Dhamma, dispelling the darkness of people's delusion, thus the Sage, his duty done, passes the middle watch daily.

77.

77.

Abhibhutasarīrajassamo

Katakiccehi’riyāpathehica,

Atha caṅkamaṇena pacchime

Paṭhamaṃ bhāga matikkame muni; ()

Having overcome the fatigue born of the body through his completed duties and changes of posture, the Sage then passes the first part of the last watch by walking meditation.

78. [O 0.0468]

78.

Paṭivāta’nuvāta vāyita-

Guṇagandhehi sugandhitaṅgimā,

Maṇidīpapabhāsamujjalaṃ

Sugato gandhakuṭiṃka upāgato; ()

His body made fragrant by the multiplied scents wafted against and with the wind, the Sugata approached the fragrant hut, which was shining with the radiance of a jewel-lamp.

79.

79.

Sayanopari sampasārayaṃ

Paṭimārūpasarūpaviggahaṃ,

Sayanaṃ kurute’va kesarī

Dutiyasmiṃ satisampajaññavā; ()

Stretching out his body upon the couch, a form resembling that of an image, he lies down like a lion in the second part of the watch, mindful and clearly comprehending.

80.

80.

Asamiddhakilesamiddhavā

Bhagavā bhaṅgabhavaṅgasattati,

Sunisajja pabujjhito mahā-

Karuṇājhāna mupeticā’sane; ()

The Blessed One, for whom defilements and sloth are unfulfilled, having awakened and being well-seated, enters the meditation of great compassion on his seat.

81. [O 0.0469]

81.

Purimesu bhavesu pāṇino

Yadi vijjanti katādhikārino,

Raviraṃsivikāsanūpaga-

Padumānī’va pabodhanārahā; ()

If there are beings who in former existences have made the necessary preparations, they are worthy of awakening, like lotuses ready to open to the sun’s rays.

82.

82.

Karuṇāya samuṭṭhito tato

Karuṇāsītalamānaso muni,

Abhipassati buddhacakkhunā

Bhuvi te maggaphalopanissaye; ()

Then, having arisen from that meditation on compassion, the Sage, his mind cooled by compassion, surveys with the Buddha-eye those in the world who possess the supporting conditions for the path and its fruit.

83.

83.

Iti pacchimayāma manvahaṃ

Tatiyaṃ bhāga matikkame jino,

Purimoditakiccakārino

Katakiccassa acintiyāguṇā; () (Pacchimayāmakiccaṃ)

Thus daily the Victor passes the third part of the last watch. Immeasurable are the virtues of him, the doer of the duties described before, whose task is accomplished.

84. [O 0.0470]

84.

Pasidanti rūpappa māṇapi buddhe

Pasidanti ghosappamāṇapi buddhe

Pasidanti ḷukhappa māṇapi buddhe

Pasidanti dhammappamāṇapi buddhe ()

Some have faith in the Buddha, taking his form as their measure. Some have faith in the Buddha, taking his voice as their measure. Some have faith in the Buddha, taking his simple living as their measure. Some have faith in the Buddha, taking the Dhamma as their measure.

Iti medhānandābhidhānenayatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santike nidāne pañjavidhabuddhakicca paridīpo aṭṭhārasamoka saggo.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, the 'Illumination of the Fivefold Duties of a Buddha,' in the Proximate Account of the Jinavaṃsadīpa, a source of the gift of joy for the hearts of all poets, composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda.

1. [O 0.0471]

1.

Niravadhibhuvanālavālagabbhe

Sucaritamūlavirūḷhakittivallī,

Navaguṇaniyamotu saṅgamena

Bhagavatamāsiyatheva (pupphitaggā); ()

In the basin of the boundless world, the creeper of the Blessed One's fame, which had grown from the root of good conduct, was, through its connection with the stream of his nine qualities, as if flowered at its very tip.

2.

2.

Suvisadamatimā savāsanehi

Sakala kilesa malehi cārakāyo,

Itipi bhagavato budhābhigīto

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Because he is of exceedingly pure mind and is far from all stains of defilements together with their latent tendencies, for this reason also the Blessed One is praised by the wise, and the sound of his fame as 'Arahant' is renowned in the world.

3.

3.

Gahita nisita maggañāṇa khaggo

Varamati duccaritārayo achindi,

Itipi bhagavato hatārinoyo

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Having grasped the sharp sword of path-knowledge, with supreme wisdom he cut down the foes of misconduct. For this reason also, the Blessed One has slain his foes, and the sound of his fame as 'Arahant' is renowned in the world.

4.

4.

Tibhavarathasamappitaṃ avijjā-

Bhavatasiṇāmayanābhika māsavakkhaṃ,

Vicitupacitakamma sañcāyā’raṃ

Jaṭitajarāmaraṇerunemi vaṭṭiṃ ()

The wheel of the chariot of the three realms has a hub made of ignorance and craving for existence, an axle of taints, spokes from the accumulation of varied and accumulated kamma, and a turning rim of entangled aging and death.

5. [O 0.0473]

5.

Avidita pariyanta kālasīmaṃ

Paribhamitaṃ bhavacakkamatthi tassa,

Thiravīriyapadehi bodhimaṇḍe

Suvimalasīlamahītaleṭhito yo; ()

That revolving wheel of existence, whose end and time-limit are unknown, does not exist for him—for he is one who stands on the perfectly pure ground of virtue at the seat of enlightenment with feet of firm energy.

6.

6.

Hanivihani are visuddhasaddhā-

Karakamalena samādhisāṇapiṭṭhe,

Sunisita masamaṃ nihanti kamma-

Kkhayakarañāṇakuṭhārimādadhāno; ()

Wielding the unequalled, well-sharpened axe of knowledge that destroys kamma, having sharpened it on the whetstone of concentration with the lotus-hand of pure faith, he strikes down and destroys the foes.

7. [O 0.0474]

7.

Hatabhavaratha vibbhamassa magga-

Rathamabhiruyha sivaṃpuraṃ gatassa,

Itipi bhagavato hatārakassa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Because he has destroyed the whirling chariot of existence and, having mounted the chariot of the path, has gone to the city of peace, for this reason also, the Blessed One, who has destroyed the spokes of the wheel, is renowned in the world, and his fame as 'Arahant' is proclaimed.

8.

8.

Avidita pariyanta dukkha vaṭṭaṃ

Athabhavacakkaka mituccate avijjā,

Tahimupahitanābhī mūlakattā

Bhavatijarāmaraṇaṃ tadantanemi; ()

The cycle of suffering, whose end is unknown, is also called the wheel of existence, and ignorance is its name. Because it is the root, ignorance is established as the hub; aging and death are its outer rim.

9.

9.

Ghaṭita tadubhayantarā arāssu

Dasa abhisaṅkharaṇādisesa dhammā,

Kasirasamudaye nirodha magge

Bhavati pajānamajānanaṃ avijjā; ()

Between those two are fixed the spokes: the ten volitional formations and the remaining phenomena. Ignorance is the not-knowing of beings concerning the origin of suffering, its cessation, and the path.

10 [O 0.0475]

10

Bhavati tividhabhumikā avijjā

Catuvidha saccasabhāva chādakā’yaṃ,

Abhivicinana cetanāna maddhā

Vividhanayena bhavattaye nidānaṃ; ()

Ignorance, existing in the three planes, conceals the nature of the four truths. Truly, by not investigating volitions, it becomes, in various ways, the cause for the threefold existence.

11.

11.

Sakasaka paṭisandhicittahetu

Dvaya mabhisaṅkhata kammameva kāme,

Cita kusala marūpa rūpa gāmiṃ

Tadubhayabhupaṭisandhihetu hoti; ()

For each respective rebirth-linking consciousness, the cause is the twofold volitional formation—kamma itself—in the sense-sphere, and the accumulated wholesome kamma leading to the form and formless realms. Both of these become the cause for rebirth in those planes.

12.

12.

Kusalamakusalaṃ tidhā vibhattaṃ

Purimabhavenicitaṃ yathānurūpaṃ,

Nabhavati paṭisandhitoparaṃ kiṃ

Tibhava pavatti vipāka citta hetu; ()

Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is divided threefold and accumulated in a previous existence according to its nature. What comes after rebirth-linking? The resultant consciousness which is the cause for the continuity of the threefold existence.

13. [O 0.0476]

13.

Samudayamaya kāmarūpapākā

Sati paṭisandhi pavattiyaṃ bhavantī,

Saka saka bhavanāma rūpahetu

Vividha nidānavasena cānurūpaṃ, ()

The results pertaining to the sense and form realms, arising from their causes, occur at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence. With the name-and-form of each respective existence as their cause, they arise appropriately by way of various conditions.

14.

14.

Tathariva caturo arūpapākā

Sakasakabhumikanāmapaccayāva,

Samupacita manaṃ asaññasatte

Nabhavatikiṃka bhuvi rūpamattahetu; ()

Likewise, the four formless results are conditioned only by 'name' pertaining to their respective planes. Accumulated mind is not found in non-percipient beings. Why? Because in that plane, form alone is the cause.

15. [O 0.0477]

15.

Tadubhaya mavipāka cittatopi

Pabhavati tīsubhavesu cā’nu rūpaṃ,

Sugati dugatiyaṃ padaṃhi kāme

Bhavati saḷāyatanassa nāma rūpaṃ; ()

That twofold (name-and-form) also arises from non-resultant consciousness, suitably in the three existences. Indeed, in the happy and unhappy destinations of the sense-sphere, name-and-form becomes the basis for the six sense bases.

16.

16.

Bhavati padaka masaññi vajjarūpa-

Bhuvi tividhāyatanassa nāma rūpaṃ,

Havati samudayo bhave arūpe

Sukhuma manāyatanassa nāma mattaṃ; ()

In the form plane, excluding that of the non-percipient beings, name-and-form is the basis for the three sense bases. In the formless existence, there arises only name as the basis for the subtle mind-base.

17.

17.

Iti tividhabhave bhavanti taṃ taṃ-

Bhava pabhavāyatanāti phassahetu,

Tathariva kamato bhavānu rūpaṃ

Tividhabhavesu chaphassavedanejā; ()

Thus, in the threefold existence, those respective existences, origins, and sense bases become the cause for contact. Likewise, in sequence and corresponding to the existence, feelings born of the six kinds of contact arise in the three existences.

18. [O 0.0478]

18.

Vividha bhavagatiṭṭhitīsu taṃ taṃ

Chaṭita jaṭā gahaṇassa hetu hoti,

Punarubhaya bhavassa daḷhagāho,

Bhavati bhavotibhavamhi hetujātyā; ()

In various existences, destinations, and stations, that becomes the cause for grasping the tangle (of craving). The firm grasping of renewed existence becomes the cause for birth in a future existence.

19.

19.

Tividha bhavu’papattijātiresā

Bhavati jarāmaraṇādi dukkha hetu,

Sakalakasirupaddavā’savānaṃ

Samudayahetutatosiyā avijjā; ()

This birth, which is rebirth into the threefold existence, becomes the cause of suffering, such as aging and death. Therefore, ignorance is the cause of the arising of all suffering, calamities, and taints.

20.

20.

Thiragahaṇavasena yohi koci

Sucarita duccaritaṃcareyya tassa,

Sugati dugati gāmi kammamettha

Kathayati kammabhavo’ti kammavādī; ()

Whoever, due to firm grasping, should perform good or bad conduct, their kamma leads to happy or unhappy destinations. An advocate of kamma declares this to be 'kamma-becoming'.

21. [O 0.0479]

21.

Vicitupacita kammasattijātā

Vadatupapatti bhavo’ti pañcakhandhā,

Tadabhijanana māhajāti tesaṃ

Cuticavanaṃ paripākatājarā’ti; ()

The five aggregates, born from the power of variously accumulated kamma, are called 'rebirth-becoming'. Their manifestation is called 'birth'; their decay, 'aging'; and their passing away, 'death'.

22.

22.

Pahavaphalapabandhato ṭhītānaṃ

Sarasagabhīrapaṭicca sambhavānaṃ,

Kayirati visadāya yāya dhamma–

Ṭhitimatināmadhiyā pariggahaṃsā; ()

For those established in the sequence of cause and effect, existing in the subtle and profound dependent origination, may a clear comprehension be made by that wisdom named 'wisdom of the stability of the Dhamma'.

23.

23.

Idhapana caturosiyuṃsamāsā

Purimabhavo’daya moha kammameko,

Bhavatihanabhavacittanāma rūpā-

Yatana cha phassa cha vedanāti ceko; ()

Here, moreover, are four summaries: Delusion and kamma, the arising of past existence, are one group. Existence in the present, consciousness, and name-and-form are one group. The six sense bases, contact, and feeling are also one group.

24. [O 0.0480]

24.

Api bhavati bhavo nikanti gāho

Janana jarāmaraṇaṃ anāgate’ko,

Pabhava phalavasena sambhavānaṃ

Iti catu saṅkhipanaṃ siyātiyaddhaṃ; ()

Moreover, craving, grasping, and becoming are one group; birth, aging, and death in the future are another. Thus, for that which arises by way of cause and effect, this is the fourfold summary across the three time periods.

25.

25.

Idha yathariva’tītahetupañca

Abhiratigāhabhavehi kammamohā,

Tathariva saha mohakammunāpi

Abhiratigāhabhavā idāni hetū; ()

Here, just as there are five causes rooted in the past—delight, grasping, becoming, kamma, and delusion—so too, in the present, delight, grasping, and becoming, along with delusion and kamma, are the causes.

26.

26.

Nabhavati phalapañcakaṃ kimeta-

Rahipaṭisandhika manādipañca dhammā,

Bhavati phakhalamanāgate tatheva

Janana jarāmaraṇādi pañca dhammā; ()

What is the fivefold fruit in the present? It is the five phenomena beginning with consciousness, connected with rebirth-linking. Just so, in the future, the fivefold fruit arises: the five phenomena of birth, aging, death, and so on.

27. [O 0.0481]

27.

Bhavati bhavupapattiya’ntare’ko

Abhirati vedayitāna mantare’ko,

Tathariva citacetanāmanānaṃ

Iti bhavacakkatisandhayo bhavanti; ()

There is one connection between becoming and rebirth; another between delight and feeling; and likewise, between accumulated volitions and consciousness. Thus, these are the three connections of the wheel of existence.

28.

28.

Suvisadamativīsatā’ katāraṃ

Sa’tiparivaṭṭa tisandhikaṃ tiyaddhaṃ,

Tadavagamiyatāya dhātu dhamma-

Ṭṭhitimatiyā catusaṅgahaṃ dvimūlaṃ; ()

This dependent origination—with its more than twenty aspects, three rounds, three connections, and three time periods, its fourfold summary and its twofold root—is to be clearly understood by means of the wisdom of the stability of the Dhamma.

29.

29.

Hanivibhani jagattaye bhavanta-

Bhavaratha cakkasamappitākhilāre,

Itipi bhagavato budhāhigīto

Bhuvi visuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

He has destroyed and dispersed the enemies of defilements; he has broken all the spokes of the wheel of the chariot of existence. For this reason too, the Blessed One is praised by the wise, and his cry of fame, 'Arahant!', is renowned on earth.

30. [O 0.0482]

30.

Bhagavati udite mahānubhāvo

Tamahimaheyya bhusaṃ sadevaloko,

Tadahimahi kadāvi neru matta-

Maṇiratanāvaliyā sahampatīpi; ()

When the Blessed One of great power had arisen, the world with its gods honored him greatly. Then, at one time, even Sahampati honored him with a garland of jewels the size of Mount Meru.

31.

31.

Pacurasuranarā balānurūpaṃ

Yamabhimahiṃsu anātha piṇḍikopi,

Gahapati tamupāsikāvisākhā

Saparisa kosalabimbisārabhūpā; ()

Many asuras and humans honored him according to their ability, as did the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the female lay disciple Visākhā, and the kings of Kosala and Magadha, Bimbisāra, with their retinues.

32.

32.

Bhagavati parinibbute asoka-

Vahayadharaṇīpati dīpacakkavatti,

Dasabalamasamaṃ pariccajitvā

Abhimahi channavutippamāṇakoṭī; ()

When the Blessed One had attained Parinibbāna, the emperor named Asoka, the sorrowless lord of the earth, a wheel-turning monarch of this island, honored the incomparable Ten-Powered One, having given up wealth to the amount of ninety-six crores.

33. [O 0.0483]

33.

Agaṇita vibhavaṃ pariccachitvā

Iharatanāvali cetiyaṃ vidhāya,

Suranarasaraṇassa dhātudehaṃ

Narapatimānayi duṭṭhagāminī’pi; ()

Having given up immeasurable wealth and having built here the Ratanāvali Cetiya, King Duṭṭhagāminī also honored the relic-body of him who is the refuge of gods and humans.

34.

34.

Dasabalamabhipūjayiṃsu pūjā-

Vidhibahumānana bhājanaṃ tadaññe,

Itijana mahanīya cīvarādī-

Catuvidhapaccaya pūjanāka visesaṃ; ()

Others, too, worshipped the Ten-Powered One, who is a worthy vessel for rites of worship and great honor. Thus, people paid special homage with offerings of the four requisites, such as robes, which are held in high esteem.

35.

35.

Guṇajaladhi yadagga dakkhiṇeyyo

Arahati cāhuṇa pāhuṇā rahassa,

Itipi bhagavato kavippa sattho

Bhuvi visuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Because he is an ocean of virtues, the foremost of those worthy of offerings, and is worthy of gifts and hospitality, both public and private. For this reason too, the fame of the Blessed One, the Teacher praised by the wise, is renowned on earth as 'Arahant!'

36. [O 0.0484]

36.

Idhaparamanipaccakāra giddhā

Samaṇaka bhusurakā vibhāvimānī,

Rahasi akusalaṃ silokakāmā

Na kimasilokabhayena sañcinanti; ()

Here, some mere recluses and brahmins, greedy for the highest respect, proud and conceited, and desirous of fame, accumulate unwholesome deeds in secret, while refraining from them publicly only out of fear of disgrace.

37.

37.

Nacakarahaci kiñcideva pāpaṃ

Kayirati resarahopipāpabhīrū,

Itipi bhagavato rahāpagassa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

But he does no evil whatsoever, not even in secret, being averse to wrongdoing. For this reason too, the fame of the Blessed One, who is devoid of secret faults, is renowned on earth as 'Arahant!'

38.

38.

Anupasamita rāgadosa mohā

Thiramanabhāvita kāyacitta paññā,

Ariyapaṭipadāya ye vipannā

Anariya dhammacarā narādhamāte; ()

Those whose passion, hatred, and delusion are unappeased, whose body, mind, and wisdom are not firmly developed, those who have deviated from the Noble Path, practicing the ignoble Dhamma—they are the lowest of humans.

39. [O 0.0485]

39.

Sugahita sugatārahaddhajantā

Jinamanubandhiya santikeka varāpi,

Itipi bhagavato bhavanti dure

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso ()

Though they have well-grasped the banner of the Sugata, the Arahant, the Jina, and follow closely near the most excellent one, yet they are far from the Blessed One. Thus, his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

40.

40.

Tathariva suvidura bhāvamāpa

Munirapitehinihīna puggalehi,

Itipi bhagavato satampa sattho

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso;Ka ()

Likewise, the Sage attained a state of being very far, even amidst those base persons. Thus, the Blessed One, the Teacher of the good, is renowned in the world, his fame proclaimed as the Arahant.

41.

41.

Vihata sakalasaṃkilesa dhammā

Satata subhāvita kāya cittapaññā,

Ariyapaṭipadaṃ papūrakārī

Anariyadhammapathārakāka sudhīrā; ()

Those who have destroyed all defiling qualities, who have constantly well-cultivated body, mind, and wisdom, who are fulfillers of the Noble Path—those very wise ones are far from the path of ignoble things.

42. [O 0.0486]

42.

Satadasasata yojanehi dūre

Yadiviharanti jinassa ārakāte,

Itipi bhagavato na tāva dūre

Bhuvi visuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Though they dwell seventeen hundred leagues away, far from the Victor, yet they are not so far from the Blessed One. Thus, his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

43.

43.

Tathariva avidūra bhāvamāpa

Munirapi sappurisāna mīdisānaṃ,

Itipi bhagavato bhavantagassa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Likewise, the Sage attained a state of being not far in relation to such good persons. Thus, of the Blessed One, who has gone to the end of existence, the sound of renown as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

44. [O 0.0487]

44.

Budha jana rahitabba pāpadhammā

Pavūramanatthakarāka rahāvadanti,

Itipi bhagavato rahā na yassa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kitti ghoso; ()

Wise people call those evil qualities which cause harm 'raha'—things to be abandoned. Thus, for the Blessed One, for whom there is nothing 'raha' (secret or to be abandoned), his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

45.

45.

Garahiya rahitabbatā’riyehi

Paramaputhujjana puggalehi yasmā,

Itipi bhagavato naca’tthi’massa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Because blameworthy things are to be abandoned by the noble ones, and since for this Blessed One there is no such thing, his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

46.

46.

Apica bhagavatā natekadāci

Vigarahiyā rahitabbakā bhavanti,

Itipi bhagavato rahānayassa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

Furthermore, for the Blessed One there are never any blameworthy things to be abandoned. Thus, for the Blessed One, for whom there is no secret evil, his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

47. [O 0.0488]

47.

Gamana miharahoti vuccate taṃ

Tibhavaparibbhamaṇaṃ raho na yassa,

Itipi bhagavato gatassa pāraṃ

Bhuvi visuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

That wandering in the three existences is here called 'raho' (a secret going). For the Blessed One, there is no such secret going. Thus, of the Blessed One, who has gone to the far shore, his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

48.

48.

Niratisaya’dhisīlacittapañño

Parama vimutti vimutti ñāṇalābhī,

Asandisa guṇa bhājanoka anejo

Asamasamo asamo anuttaro’ti; ()

Unexcelled in higher virtue, higher mind, and higher wisdom; attainer of supreme liberation and the knowledge of liberation; a unique, unparalleled receptacle of virtues, unperturbed, equal to the unequalled, unequalled, and unsurpassed.

49. [O 0.0489]

49.

Kusalabala samiddharūpavāti

Vividhaguṇehi siyā pasaṃ siyo yo,

Itipi bhagavato pasaṃsiyassa

Bhuvivisuto arahanti kittighoso; ()

He who is prosperous with wholesome powers and beauty, who is to be praised for his various virtues—thus, of the Blessed One, who is worthy of praise, his fame as the Arahant is widely known throughout the world.

50.

50.

Iminā imināpi kāraṇena

Bhagavā gotama gotta ketubhūto,

Arahaṃ arahanti kittirāvo

Dakatelaṃvatatāna sattaloke; ()

For this and that reason, the Blessed One, the banner of the Gotama clan—his resounding fame as 'Arahant' spread throughout the world of beings like oil on water.

Iti medhānandābhidhānenayatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santike nidāne bhagavato arahantināmapaññattiyāabhidheya paridīpo ekūnavīsatimoka saggo.

Thus the nineteenth chapter, 'A Clarification of the Meaning of the Blessed One's Designation as Arahant,' in the Proximate Introduction of the Jinavaṃsadīpa—a source for the gift of joy to the hearts of all poets, composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda—is concluded.

1. [O 0.0490]

1.

Sammā sāmaṃ sabbadhammāna maddhā

Buddhattā paññānubhāvena tassa,

Sammā sambuddhoti abbhuggatāya

Āsikityā(sālinī) loka dhātu; ()

Because he truly awakened to all phenomena rightly and by himself, through the power of his wisdom, his fame as 'Sammāsambuddha' arose in the world-sphere.

2.

2.

Yo cā bhiññeyye pariññeyya dhamme

Bhāvetabbe sacchikātabba dhamme,

Sammāsāmaṃ bujjhi tasmāsa buddho

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

He who rightly and by himself awakened to the phenomena to be directly known, the phenomena to be fully understood, the phenomena to be developed, and the phenomena to be realized—therefore he is the Buddha, renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

3.

3.

Tatrā’bhiññeyyā catussacca meva

Dukkhaṃ saccaṃ kho pariññeyya dhammā,

Bhāvetabbā magga saccaṃ nirodha-

Saccaṃ tacchaṃ sacchikā tabba dhammā; ()

Therein, the Four Truths themselves are to be directly known. The truth of suffering is indeed the phenomenon to be fully understood; the truth of the path is to be developed; the truth of cessation is truly the phenomenon to be realized.

4. [O 0.0491]

4.

Taṇhāpakkhe sambhavaṃ dhamma jātaṃ

Maggānaṃvajjhaṃka pahātabba dhammā,

Saddhiṃ jātyādīhi dukekhahi pañcu-

Pādānakkhandhā siyā dukkha saccaṃ; ()

That group of phenomena arisen on the side of craving, which are to be abandoned by the paths, are the phenomena to be abandoned. Together with birth and other sufferings, the five clinging-aggregates are the truth of suffering.

5.

5.

Yāyaṃ taṇhā kāma taṇhādibhedā

Dukkhānaṃ sāhetu saccaṃ dvitiyaṃ,

Bandhānaṃ yatrāpya’bhāvo nirodha-

Saccaṃ yañcā gamma taṇhāya cāgo; ()

This craving, with its distinctions of craving for sensual pleasures and so on, is the second truth, the cause of suffering. Wherein there is an absence of bonds, and which is the abandoning of craving—that is the truth of cessation.

6. [O 0.0492]

6.

Sammādiṭṭhādyaṭṭhamaggaṅga dhammā

Nibbānaṃ sampāpakā magga saccaṃ,

Tesaṃ dhammānampi sambujjhinattā

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

The eight path-factor phenomena, beginning with right view, which lead to Nibbāna, are the truth of the path. Because of having rightly awakened to these phenomena as well, he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

7.

7.

Cakkheva’daṃ dukkhaṃ taduppāda hetu

Taṇhā nesānaṃ abhāvo nirodho,

Maggo bodhūpāya paññāti tassa

Evaṃ paccekaṃ padaṃ coddharitvā; ()

'This is suffering'; 'Craving is the cause of its arising'; 'The absence of these is cessation'; 'The path is the means to awakening'—thus having expounded each term individually...

8.

8.

Āropetvā sacca dhammesu sacca-

Sandhātā yo saccadassī sa buddho,

Sammā sāmaṃ tikkhapaññāya bujjhi

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

Having applied them to the phenomena of the truths, he who is the establisher of truth, the seer of truth, that Buddha, awakened rightly and by himself with sharp wisdom; thus he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

9. [O 0.0493]

9.

Channaṃ dvārānañca chārammaṇānaṃ,

Channaṃ cittānañca chabbeda nānaṃ,

Channaṃ saññānaṃ cha sañcetanānaṃ

Channaṃ phassā naṃ vitakkādi kānaṃ; ()

Of the six doors and the six objects, of the six consciousnesses and the six feelings, of the six perceptions and the six volitions, of the six contacts, of thoughts and so on—

10.

10.

Evaṃ channaṃ rūpa taṇhādikānaṃ

Taṇhākāyānaṃ samāropaṇena,

Sammā sāmaṃ bujjhi saccesu tasmā

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

Thus, by applying the six bodies of craving—for forms and so on—to the truths, he awakened rightly and by himself; therefore, he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

11.

11.

Pañcannaṃ khandhāna maṭṭhārasannaṃ

Dhātūnaṃ cakkhādinaṃ bārasannaṃ,

Sammā sāmaṃ bujjhitattā sayambhu

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

Because the Self-Become One awakened rightly and by himself to the five aggregates, the eighteen elements, and the twelve sense bases beginning with the eye, he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

12. [O 0.0494]

12.

Rūpajjhānānaṃ catunnaṃ arūpa-

Jjhānānañcānussatīnaṃ dasannaṃ,

Khatti sākāra’ppamaññāsubhānaṃ

Kammaṭṭhānānaṃ navannaṃ bhavānaṃ; ()

Of the four material jhānas and the four immaterial jhānas, of the ten recollections, of the immeasurables and the perceptions of repulsiveness, of the meditation subjects, and of the nine abodes of beings—

13.

13.

Buddhattā saṃsāra cakke avijjā-

Dyaṅgānaṃ saccesucāropaṇena,

Sammāsāmaṃ esa nissaṅga ñāṇe

Sammā sambuddho vikhyāsi loke; ()

Because he awakened to the wheel of saṃsāra, and by applying the factors beginning with ignorance to the truths, this one, with unattached knowledge, rightly and by himself awakened; thus he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

14.

14.

Paccuppannānāgatātīta dhamme

Nibbānaṃ nissesa paṇṇatti dhamme,

Sāmaṃ abbhaññāsya’naññopa deso

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

Having directly known by himself—not through the instruction of another—the phenomena of the present, future, and past, Nibbāna, and all conceptual phenomena, he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

15.

15.

Sabbaṃñeyyaṃ tassa ñāṇanti kaṃhi

Ñāṇampevaṃ ñeyya dhammantikaṃhi,

Ñeyyantaṭṭhānomañāṇassalābhā

Sammāsambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

All that is knowable is within his knowledge, and his knowledge likewise is within the scope of knowable things. Because his attainment of knowledge stands at the very limit of the knowable, he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

16.

16.

Klesānaṃ yāvāsanāsatatītāya

Saddhiṃyoka sammohaniddāya sammā,

Sāmaṃbuddho magga ñāṇena tasmā

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi loke; ()

He who, with the knowledge of the path, has gone beyond the defilements together with their latent tendencies, and has rightly and by himself awakened from the sleep of delusion—therefore, he is renowned in the world as the 'Perfectly Self-Enlightened One'.

17. [O 0.0496]

17.

Sattādhīso pāramīcoditatto

Pallaṅkenāsajjayo bodhimule,

Ambhojaṃka bhānuppahāka saṅgamena

Sobhaggappattaṃ pabuddhaṃ’va sāmaṃ; ()

The lord of beings, his self urged on by the perfections, who sat cross-legged at the foot of the Bodhi tree, awakened by himself, like a lotus that has attained beauty and blossomed through its meeting with the sun's rays.

18.

18.

Sāmaṃ sammā’nañña sādhāraṇagga-

Maggobhāsenappabuddho samāno,

Sampatto sabbaññutāñāṇa sobhaṃ

Sammā sambuddhoti vikhyāsi tasmā; ()

Having awakened rightly by himself through the radiance of the supreme path not shared by others, he attained the splendor of omniscient knowledge; therefore, he is renowned as the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

19.

19.

Evaṃ sabbesaṃ dhammānaṃ

Sammā sāmaṃ buddhattā so,

Sammā sambuddho buddhoti

Saddo loke abbhuggañji; ()

Thus, having rightly awakened by himself to all phenomena, the name 'Buddha, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One' arose in the world.

Iti medhānandābhidhānenayatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikeka nidāne bhagavato kasammāsambuddhoti nāmapaññattiyā abhidheya paridīpo vīsatimo saggo.

Thus concludes the twentieth chapter, 'A Clarification of the Meaning of the Designation of the Blessed One as the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One,' in the proximate section of the Jinavaṃsadīpa, composed by the monk named Medhānanda, a source of joy for the hearts of all poets.

Taṃ [O 0.0497] kho pana bhavantaṃ

Gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇe kittisaddo abbhuggato

Itipi so bhagavā vijjācaraṇa sampannoti;

Furthermore, concerning that Venerable Gotama, a good report has spread thus: 'That Blessed One is indeed accomplished in knowledge and conduct.'

1.

1.

Sampannavijjācaraṇe avijjā-

Ghaṇandhakāraṃ bhiduro pavīro,

Rāja vijjācaraṇubbhavāya

Uḷārakittissiriyā kathaṃ taṃ; ()

For one accomplished in knowledge and conduct, a great hero who shatters the thick darkness of ignorance, how could there not be vast glory and splendor for him, who is born of that very knowledge and conduct?

2.

2.

Asaṅkhakappepi nivutthakhandhe

Peyyālapāḷiṃ viya ñāṇagatyā,

Kaṇṭhiravassu’ppatanaṃ yatheva

Saṅkippa khippaṃ visayāvalambaṃ; (1)

Even concerning the aggregates lived through in countless aeons, with the speed of knowledge—like the Peyyāla recitation, like the springing of a lion—it briefly and swiftly takes hold of its object.

3. [O 0.0498]

3.

Saro’tisūro sarabhaṅgaka satthu-

Khitto saravyamhi virajjhate kiṃ

Evaṃ atitesu bhavantaresu

Asajjamānaṃ avirajjhamānaṃ; ()

Does the very heroic arrow, shot by the Teacher Sarabhaṅga, fail to hit the target? Even so, in past existences, he proceeded without attachment and without failure.

4.

4.

Yathicchitaṭṭhāna matitakhandha-

Saṅkhāta māhacca pavattamānaṃ,

Pubbenivāsānugatañhi ñāṇaṃ

Anaññasādhāraṇamāsi yassa; ()

The knowledge of recalling past lives, which proceeded having reached the desired state among the past aggregates, was indeed a knowledge not shared by others.

5.

5.

Pahīṇa’vijjānusayo jino so

Vijjāyu’peto paṭhamāya tāya,

Iccassa daṇḍāhatakaṃsapāti-

Saddova sampatthari kittisaddo; ()

That Conqueror, having abandoned the underlying tendency to ignorance, was endowed with that first knowledge; thus his fame spread like the sound of a bronze bowl struck with a stick.

6. [O 0.0499]

6.

Hanīnappaṇītādi pabheda vatte

Uppajjamāne ca nirujjhamāne,

Satte yathākammu’page gatīsu

Pasādacakkhā’visaye ca rūpe; ()

Beings fare according to their kamma to various destinations—low and exalted, arising and ceasing—in the round of existence, and in forms that are beyond the range of the eye of faith.

7.

7.

Anañña sādhāraṇa dibbacakkhu-

Saṅkhātañāṇena pahassarena,

Dibbena cā’loka pariggahena

Yenā’hijānāti jino anejo; ()

By means of the radiant knowledge known as the divine eye, which is not shared by others, and with its encompassing divine light, the passionless Conqueror directly knows.

8.

8.

Cutupapātabbisayāya satthā

Vijjāyu’peto dutiyāya tāya,

Iccassa sampatthari hema ghaṇṭā-

Ṭaṅkāraghosoriva kittighoso; ()

The Teacher, endowed with that second knowledge concerning the passing away and reappearance of beings—thus his fame spread like the ringing sound of a golden bell.

9.

9.

Dukkhañca dukkhappabhavo nirodho

Maggo ca dukkhassa nirodhako’ti,

Cattāri saccāni yathāsabhāvaṃ

Pavedi ñāṇena sayambhu yena; ()

By which knowledge the Self-Awakened One proclaimed the Four Truths according to their true nature: suffering, the origin of suffering, its cessation, and the path that brings about the cessation of suffering.

10. [O 0.0500]

10.

Yecā’savā āsavasambhavo yo

Tesaṃ khayo yavā’savanāsupāyo,

Taṃ sabbamaññāsi sayambhu ñāṇa-

Balena yenā’sava vippamutto; ()

The taints, the origin of the taints, their destruction, and the means for the destruction of the taints—all this the Self-Awakened One understood with the power of wisdom, by which he was freed from the taints.

11.

11.

Khīṇa’ti jātī vusita’nti seṭṭha-

Cariyaṃ kataṃ’tī karaṇiya maddhā,

Nacā’parantye’va manantañāṇo

Ñāṇena’bhiññāya vihāsi yena; ()

By which knowledge the one of infinite knowledge abided, having directly known: 'Birth is destroyed, the noble life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.'

12. [O 0.0501]

12.

Sayambhu sabbāsava saṅkhayāya

Vijjāyupeto tatiyāya tāya,

Iccassa vipphāragahīrateri-

Rāvo’va sampatthari kittirāvo; ()

The Self-Awakened One, endowed with that third knowledge for the destruction of all taints—thus his fame spread like a deep and pervasive roar.

13.

13.

Vijjāhiheṭṭhā gaditāhi tīhi

Samaṅakgi bhutassa tathāgatassa,

Tadubbhavaṃ kitti sarīra bimbaṃ

Sataṃmanodappaṇagaṃ vibhāti; ()

Of the Tathāgata, endowed with the three knowledges previously declared, the fame arisen therefrom shines like a bodily reflection in the mirror of the minds of the good.

14.

14.

Cātummahābhūtikarūpiko yaṃ

Mātāpitunnaṃ karajamhi jāto,

Yo bhattakummāsahatopi kāyo

Aniccaviddhaṃsanabheda dhammo; ()

This body, which is formed from the four great elements, born from the physical substance of mother and father, and sustained by rice and gruel, is of a nature to be impermanent, destroyed, and broken up.

15.

15.

Parittakāmāvacaramhi bhuto-

Pādāya bhedamhi tadattabhāve,

Yaṃ nissitaṃ vedayitatta saññā-

Saṅkhāra viññāṇa pabhedanāmaṃ; ()

Dependent on that self-existence, which has arisen in the limited sense-sphere and is subject to breaking up, is what is called 'name,' with its divisions of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.

16. [O 0.0502]

16.

Yo vippasanno maṇivaṃsa vaṇṇo

Tatrāvutaṃ suttamivakkhimā taṃ,

Ñāṇakkhinārūpa mavekkhi yena

Sacakkhumā tatrasitañca nāmaṃ; ()

He who is perfectly clear, with the hue of a bamboo-gem, beheld form with the eye of wisdom, and also name, which is dependent on it, just as a thread is passed through the eye of a needle.

17.

17.

Sītādinā ruppaṇalakkhaṇanti

Rūpañca nāmaṃ natilakkhaṇanti,

Taduttariṃ vedakakārako vā

Attāttabhāvī paramatthato na; ()

Form has the characteristic of being afflicted by cold and so forth, and name has the characteristic of inclining. Beyond these, in an ultimate sense, there is no experiencer or doer, no self or what belongs to a self.

18.

18.

Aññoññasambandhavasena yantī

Nāpaṅgulandhā puthageva yanti,

Tathā’ññamañño’panidhāya nāma-

Rūpāni vattanti’ha novisunti; ()

They proceed by way of mutual connection; they do not proceed separately, like a cripple and a blind man. Thus, depending on each other, name and form continue here; they are not separate.

19. [O 0.0503]

19.

Vavatthayantassi’ti nāmarūpaṃ

Nissattanijjivasabhāva massa,

Yā diṭṭhi duddiṭṭhivisodhanena

Samuṭṭhitā diṭṭhi visuddhisaṅkhā; ()

For one who thus discerns that name-and-form is by nature without a being and without life, the view that arises through the purification of wrong view is known as the purification of view.

20.

20.

Avijju’pādānanikantikamma-

Hetubbhavaṃ rūpamarūpamādo,

Pakavattiyaṃ hetucatūhi rūpaṃ

Vatthādihetuppabhava’nti nāmaṃ; ()

At the outset, form and the formless arise from the causes of ignorance, clinging, craving, and kamma. In the course of existence, form arises from four causes, and name arises from causes such as its physical basis.

21.

21.

Sabbattha sabbesu sadā samo na

Nā’hetukaṃ tena naniccahetu,

Evaṃ taduppādaka paccayānaṃ

Pariggahaṃ yāya dhiyā akāsi; ()

It is not always the same in all respects everywhere; it is not without a cause, and therefore it does not have a permanent cause. Thus, with that wisdom, he comprehended the conditions that produce it.

22. [O 0.0504]

22.

Ahaṃ nu kho’siṃ nanukho ahosiṃ

Iccā’dya’tītādipabheda bhutā,

Kaṅkhā’ssa kaṅkhātaraṇabbisuddhi-

Saṅkhātapaññāya vigañchi yāya; ()

His doubt—divided into past and so forth, beginning with 'Was I in the past? Was I not?'—was dispelled by the wisdom known as the purification by crossing over doubt.

23.

23.

Khandhā atītādi pabhedavanto

Parikkhayaṭṭhena anicca dhammā,

Bhayāvahaṭṭhena dukhā anattā

Asārakaṭṭheni’ti sammasanto; ()

Reflecting thus: 'The aggregates, divided into past and so forth, are impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of being fearful, and non-self in the sense of being without essence.'

24.

24.

Tāḷisadhā lakkhaṇapāṭavatthaṃ

Khandhāna mesaṃ navadhā’tha nātho,

Tikkhindriyo so bhaya sattakānaṃ

Vasena sammadditanāmarūpo; ()

For the purpose of skill in the forty kinds of characteristics of these aggregates, and in nine other ways, the Lord, he of sharp faculties, thoroughly subdued name-and-form by means of the seven kinds of fear.

25. [O 0.0505]

25.

Paññāsadhā bandhudayabbayānaṃ

Pariggahaṃ yāyadhiyā akāsi,

Yadā’ssa tāruññavipassanāya

Upakkilesā dasa pātubhūtā; ()

When the ten imperfections appeared to him during his tender insight, he, with that wisdom, comprehended the fifty aspects of the arising and passing away of phenomena.

26.

26.

Ñāṇakkhiṇā yena tilakkhaṇaṃ so

Addakkhi dhammesu tadā’pi tesu,

Jahāsu’pakelasapaduṭṭhamaggaṃ

Vipassanā sodhitamaggagāmi; ()

With the eye of wisdom, he saw the three characteristics in those phenomena, even then. He abandoned the path defiled by imperfections, being a traveler on the path purified by insight.

27. [O 0.0506]

27.

Vavatthapetvāna pathāpathe’vaṃ

Vipassanāvīthi manokkamitvā,

Yā magga’maggikkha visuddhi nāma

Samubbhavā tīraṇatikkha buddhi; ()

Having thus determined the path and the non-path, and having entered upon the avenue of insight, there arose a sharp, penetrating wisdom, namely, the Purity of Knowledge and Vision of the Path and Not-Path.

28.

28.

Anantaraṃ tīraṇuṇapāraṃ

Patto pariññāya parikkhayāya,

Nipphattiyā yo navañāṇupetaṃ

Visuddhi mākaṅkhi visuddhikāmo;

Immediately thereafter, having reached the further shore of the knowledge of discernment, for the sake of full understanding and destruction, he who desired purity longed for the Purity Endowed with the Nine Knowledges for its accomplishment.

29.

29.

Pabandhato ce’riyato ghanena

Channesu dhammesva’nupaṭṭhahanne,

Tilakkhaṇe yenu’dayabbayena

Punāpi so sammasi nāmarūpaṃ;

By means of continuous, sustained exertion, when phenomena were concealed and did not appear, he again comprehended name-and-form through their arising and passing away, in terms of the three characteristics.

30. [O 0.0507]

30.

Uppādabhaṅgaṭṭhitito yadā’ssa

Vivaṭṭayitvāna vipassato yaṃ,

Saṅkhārabhaṅge’va pavatta maṭṭha-

Vidhānisaṃsaṃbhavi bhaṅgañāṇaṃ; ()

When for him, practicing insight and turning away from arising, presence, and dissolution, his mind was set upon the breaking up of formations alone, the knowledge of dissolution arose, yielding eight kinds of benefits.

31.

31.

Vipassato bhaṅgamahiṇhamassa

Hutvā bhayaṃ vāḷamigādayo’va,

Upaṭṭhitā’tītabhavādibheda-

Bhavattayaṃ yaṃ bhayañāṇamāsi; ()

For him, constantly contemplating dissolution, the threefold existence, distinguished as past and so on, appeared as a terror, like wild beasts. This was the knowledge of fear.

32.

32.

Atha’ssa khandhāyatanādhi dhammā

Ukkhittakhaggā madhakādayo’va,

Upaddavādīnavato vibhutā

Patvā yadādīnavañāṇa māsuṃ; ()

Then for him, the phenomena—the aggregates, sense bases, and so on—appeared as perilous and disadvantageous, like executioners with upraised swords. Thus they quickly became the knowledge of disadvantage.

33. [O 0.0508]

33.

Suvaṇṇahaṃsādi’va pañjaresu

Bhavesu diṭṭhādinavesu tīsu,

Nibbinditatto bhuvanekanetto

Yaṃ nibbidāñāṇa malattha tibbaṃ; ()

Having seen the disadvantages in the three existences, like golden swans in cages, he, the one eye of the world, his mind filled with disenchantment, attained the intense knowledge of disenchantment.

34.

34.

Pāsādito pāsagate’va sattā

Vimuttikāmassa bhavehi tīhi,

Nissesasaṅkhāra vimokkha kāmaṃ

Babhuva yaṃ muñcitukāma ñāṇaṃ; ()

Like beings escaping from a fortress, for him, who longed for liberation from the three existences, there arose the knowledge of the desire for deliverance, which is the wish for complete release from all formations.

35.

35.

Aniccadukkhā’subhato ca khandhe

Anattato bhāvayato abhiṇhaṃ,

Tassā’si saṅkhāravimokkhūpāya-

Sampādakaṃ yaṃ paṭisaṅkhañāṇaṃ; ()

For him, who constantly contemplated the aggregates as impermanent, suffering, foul, and not-self, there arose the knowledge of reflection, which provides the means for liberation from formations.

36. [O 0.0509]

36.

Attena vā attaniyena suñño

Dvidhātya’yaṃ saṅkhata dhammapuñjo,

Evaṃ catuddhā bahudhā chadhā’pi

Vipassato buddhimato abhiṇhaṃ; ()

This heap of conditioned phenomena is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; thus, the wise one who constantly practices insight sees it as empty in two ways, and also in four ways, six ways, and in many ways.

37.

37.

Yā kho sikhāppattavipassanākhyā

Vuṭṭhānagāmīnica sānulomā,

Sāmuddakākīriva kūpayaṭṭhiṃ

Tilakkhaṇalambanikā babhūva; ()

Indeed, that which is called insight that has reached its climax, which leads to emergence and is the conformity knowledge, became dependent on the three characteristics, like a sea-crow on the mast of a ship.

38.

38.

Nahārudaddūlla mivaggipattaṃ

Saṅkhāradhammaṃ paṭiliyamānaṃ,

Vissaṭṭhadāraṃ’va upekkhakassa

Saṅkhārupekkhā’si mahesinoyā; ()

Contemplating conditioned phenomena as they dissolve—like a sinew shriveled by fire—and being indifferent, like a man who has divorced his wife, such was the great sage’s equanimity towards formations.

39. [O 0.0510]

39.

Āgrotrabhuñāṇa masesakhandhe

Tilakkhaṇa’ropaṇa ninnapoṇaṃ,

Vipassanāñāṇa manekabhedaṃ

Yade’ttha saṅkhepanayena vuttaṃ; ()

The knowledge of insight, of manifold kinds, which inclines and slopes towards the application of the three characteristics to all the aggregates, and the change-of-lineage knowledge—this is what has been stated here in brief.

40.

40.

Vijjāya so māraji tāya tāya

Vipassanāñāṇagatāyu’peto,

Iccassa saṃvaḍḍhita kittivalli

Lokālavālamhi vikāsa māpa; ()

By means of this and that knowledge, he, the conqueror of Māra, endowed with a life rooted in insight-knowledge—thus the flourishing vine of his fame came to blossom in the basin of the world.

41.

41.

Muñjā isikaṃ asikosiyā’siṃ

Yathā karaṇḍā phaṇi muddhareyya,

Sabbaṅga paccaṅgika mindriyaggaṃ;

Manomayaṃ rūpimito sarīrā; ()

Like drawing a reed from its sheath, a sword from its scabbard, or a snake from a basket, so he drew forth from this body a mind-made form, complete with all major and minor limbs, its faculties perfected.

42. [O 0.0511]

42.

Aññaṃ sarīraṃ abhinimmiṇitvā

Mahiddhimā iddhimatānu rūpaṃ,

Cetovasipakpattavasippadhāno

Yvākāsi veneyyajanānamatthaṃ; ()

Having created another body, he of great psychic power, in a manner befitting one with such power, foremost among masters who have attained mastery over the mind, worked for the welfare of those who were to be trained.

43.

43.

Mahiddhiko tāyamanomayiddhi-

Saṅkhāta vijjāya samanvito so,

Iccassa abbhuggatakittirāvo

Nissesalokaṃ badhirīkarittha; ()

He, great in psychic power, endowed with that knowledge called the mind-made potency—thus the resounding roar of his fame deafened the entire world.

44.

44.

Ekopihutvā bahudhāca hoti

Yo hotice’ko bahudhāpi hutvā,

Kare tirobhāva mathāvibhāvaṃ

Mahiddhiko iddhimataṃ cariṭṭho; ()

Having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one. He makes himself appear and disappear. Great in power, he is foremost among those with psychic power.

45. [O 0.0512]

45.

Yathā nirālambanabhotalamhi

Yo iddhimā viṇṇavasi vasindo,

Vaje tiropabbata gehabhitti-

Pākāra macchidda masajjamāno; ()

He with psychic power, a master of consciousness, goes unhindered through walls, ramparts, and mountains, as if through empty air.

46.

46.

Karoti ummujjanimujjaniddhiṃ

Yo vāripiṭṭheriva bhumipiṭṭhe,

Abhejjamāno salile salīlaṃ

Padappito yāti yathā pathavyā; ()

He performs the feat of emerging and submerging in the earth as if in water. He walks on water without parting it, as if on solid ground; he goes playfully, established on his feet.

47.

47.

Pakkhī’va yo saṅkamate nabhamhi

Pallaṅka mābhujja mahānubhāvaṃ,

Mahiddhimantaṃ ravicandabimbaṃ

Sapāṇiphuṭṭho parimajjate yo; ()

He travels through the sky cross-legged, like a winged bird. He, of great power and psychic might, touches and strokes with his hand the orbs of the sun and moon.

48. [O 0.0513]

48.

Ābrahmalokāpi kalebarena

Vasaṃ pavatteti mahiddhimā yo,

Suvaṇṇakāroviya yaṃyadeva

Icchānurupābharaṇabbisesaṃ; ()

He, of great psychic power, wields mastery with his body even up to the Brahma world. Like a goldsmith, he fashions whatever kind of ornament he wishes.

49.

49.

Yathicchitaṃ paccanubhoti jātu

Nānāvidhaṃ iddhividhaṃ jino yo,

So tāya vijjāyapi saṅgato’ti

Abbhuggato tassa yasopabandho; ()

The Victor experiences at will the manifold kinds of psychic power. Because he is endowed with that knowledge, his stream of fame arose and spread.

50.

50.

Sotappasādabbisayaṃ yatheva

Addhānamaggaṃ paṭipannaposo,

Visuṃvisuṃ kāhaḷasaṅkhabheri-

Vīṇādisaddaṃ vividhaṃ suṇeyya; ()

Just as a person traveling along a road might hear, separately and distinctly, various sounds such as those of trumpets, conches, drums, and lutes;

51.

51.

Dūrantike mānusake ca dibbe

Ubhopisadde sukhume uḷāre,

Visuddhanimmānusaketa yena

So dibbasotena suṇāti nātho; ()

So with the divine ear, which is purified and surpasses the human, the Lord hears both kinds of sounds, divine and human, whether far or near.

52. [O 0.0514]

52.

Samaṅgibhūtoti sadibbasota-

Saṅkhātavijjāya jitāri tāya,

Abbhuggato tassa kavībhigīta-

Silokasaddo’va silokasaddo; ()

Endowed with that knowledge called the divine ear, he, the conqueror of foes, his fame arose like the sound of a verse sung by poets.

53.

53.

Sarāgacittampi virāgacittaṃ

Sadosacittampi adosacittaṃ,

Samohacittampi vimoha cittaṃ

Saṃkhittavikkhittagatampi cittaṃ; ()

A mind with lust and a mind without lust; a mind with hate and a mind without hate; a mind with delusion and a mind without delusion; a contracted mind and a distracted mind;

54. [O 0.0515]

54.

Mahaggatampī amahaggatampī

Sottaraṃ citta manuttarampi,

Samāhitampī asamāhitampi

Vimuttacittampya’vimuttacittaṃ; ()

An exalted mind and an unexalted mind; a surpassable mind and an unsurpassable mind; a concentrated mind and an unconcentrated mind; a liberated mind and an unliberated mind—

55.

55.

Sakaṃ mukhaṅkaṃviya dappaṇamhi

Acchodake maṇḍanajātiko yo,

Paricca ceto parapuggalānaṃ

Yenā’bhijanāti vimuttaceto; ()

Just as a person fond of adornment might see their own facial features in a clear, clean mirror, so he, with his mind liberated, encompasses with his mind the minds of other beings and knows them.

56.

56.

So tāya cetopariyābhidhāna-

Vijjāyu’petoti dayānidhāno,

Tilokagabbhe’ka vitānasobhā

Tatāna tassu’bbhavasetakitti; ()

Endowed with that knowledge called the penetration of minds, he, a treasury of compassion—his pure white fame, with the splendor of a unique canopy, spread throughout the womb of the three worlds.

57. [O 0.0516]

57.

Vijjāttayena’ṭṭhavidhāhi’māhi-

Vijjāhu’peta’ssa tathāgatassa,

Veneyya kundākaracandikābhaṃ

Vibhāti yāvajja yasosarīraṃ; ()

Endowed with these eight kinds of knowledge and the threefold knowledge, the Tathāgata's body of fame shines even today, like moonlight upon a bed of jasmine for those to be trained.

58.

58.

Sumaṇḍito saṃvutapātimokkha-

Saṅkhātasīlābharaṇena yena,

Irīyate yo karuṇa nidhāno

Tapodhano sīlavataṃ padhāno ()

Well adorned with the ornament of virtue known as the Pātimokkha restraint, he who is a treasury of compassion, rich in austerity, and foremost among the virtuous, moves about.

59.

59.

Veḷupakpadānadivasena cāṭu-

Kamyena duteyyapahenakena,

So pāribhaṭyenapi muggasūpya-

Samena saccālikabhāsaṇena; ()

By giving gifts of bamboo and fruit, by flattery, by acting as a messenger or envoy, by servile attendance, and by speech that is a mixture of truth and falsehood, like lentil soup.

60. [O 0.0517]

60.

Agocaraṭṭhāna mupāsanena

Vikopaye kimpana pātimokkhaṃ,

Hitvā anācāramagocaraṃ taṃ

Care sadācārasugocaraṃ so; ()

How could he violate the Pātimokkha by frequenting unsuitable resorts? Having abandoned that unseemly conduct and unsuitable resort, he ever fares in seemly conduct and suitable resorts.

61.

61.

Anuppamāṇesupi sabbadassi

Sāvajjadhammesu bhayānupassi,

Laddhaggamaggapaphalasiddhasīla-

Sikkhāya sikkhāgaru sikkhate so; ()

The all-seeing one, he sees danger even in the slightest blameworthy things. Respectful of the training, he trains himself in the training in morality, which is perfected by the attainment of the highest path and fruition.

62. [O 0.0518]

62.

Khemaṃ disaṃ sañcaratī’ti pāti-

Mokkhādhisikkhācaraṇena tena,

Abbhuggato taccaraṇanu bandho

Ādiccabandhussa yasopabandho; ()

By that practice of the higher training in the Pātimokkha, 'he fares in a safe direction.' Thus, the stream of fame of the Kinsman of the Sun, the result of that conduct, has become exalted.

63.

63.

Kantampirūpāyatanādi chakkaṃ

Cakkhādinā so visayīkaritvā,

Nimitta’nubyañjanagāhi nātho

Nahoti yeni’ndriyasaṃvarena; ()

Having perceived with the eye and other senses the six sense-bases, such as forms, even when they are pleasing, the Guide, by means of that sense-restraint, does not grasp at their signs or features.

64.

64.

Cakkhādichadvāra masaṃvaritvā

Rāgādidhammā viharanta menaṃ,

Atvāssa veyyuṃ satisaṃvarena

Tassaṃvaratthaṃ paṭipajji yena; ()

Lust and other such states would assail one who dwells without restraining the six sense-doors beginning with the eye. For this reason, he undertook the practice for the sake of their restraint by means of the restraint of mindfulness.

65. [O 0.0519]

65.

Khemaṃdisaṃ so caraṇena tena

Jitindriyo indriyasaṃvarena,

Abbhuggato saṃcaratīti tassa

Tilokanāthassa siloka saddo; ()

By that practice of sense-restraint, he, with senses conquered, 'fares in a safe direction.' Thus has the sound of fame of that Lord of the Three Worlds arisen.

66.

66.

Ye lābhasakkārasilokakāmā

Pāpicchake’cchāpakatāsamānā,

Kevi’dhaloke catupaccayānaṃ

Paṭikkhipitvā paṭisevanena; ()

Those who desire gain, honor, and fame, being of evil wishes and overcome by desire—some here in the world, by means of rejecting the proper use of the four requisites and partaking of them improperly;

67.

67.

Sāmantajappāya catubbidhassa

Iriyāpathassā’ṭhapanādināca,

Kuhāyanenā’lapanādināca

Saccaṃ hiyā’nuppiya bhāsanena; ()

By hinting, by not maintaining the four postures, and so on, by deceit, by coaxing, and so on, and by abandoning truth for pleasant speech;

68. [O 0.0520]

68.

Attā’vacaṭṭhānu’paropaṇena

Muggassa sūpyenava pāribhaṭyā,

Nemitta kattādivasena micchā-

Jīvena dujjīvika mācarantī; ()

By imposing oneself and disparaging others, by servility like lentil soup, and by means of being a fortune-teller and the like, they lead a bad life through wrong livelihood.

69.

69.

Yatheva te no bhagavā kadāci

Kohaññavutyā’lapanādināca,

Nemitta nippesikatāya kiñci

Lāhena lābhaṃka nijigiṃsa nena; ()

Unlike them, the Blessed One never at any time, by means of hypocrisy, coaxing, and the like, nor by hinting or pressing, sought to obtain some gain by means of another gain.

70.

70.

Nimittasatthā’dipakāsanena

Ājīvasīlaṃ avikopayitvā,

Namaṇḍanatthaṃ na vibhusaṇatthaṃ

Davāya vā neva madāya neva; ()

Without corrupting his virtue of livelihood by proclaiming the science of signs and so on, [he partook of requisites] not for embellishment, not for adornment, nor for sport, nor for intoxication;

71. [O 0.0521]

71.

Anuppabandhaṭṭhitiyā imassa

Kāyassa cā’bādha nisedhanatthaṃ,

Pavattiyā paggahanāya seṭṭha-

Cariyassa porāṇa khudāpanetuṃ; ()

But for the sustained maintenance of this body, for the prevention of affliction, for the support and continuation of the noble practice, and to dispel old feelings of hunger;

72.

72.

Nūppādanatthañca navaṃ jighacchaṃ

Yātrāya kāyassa’navajjatāya,

Sukhaṃ vihārāya ca bhojanamhi

Mattaññuko bhuñjati piṇḍapātaṃ; ()

And not to create new feelings of hunger, for the sustenance of the body, for blamelessness, and for dwelling in comfort, being moderate in eating, he partakes of almsfood.

73. [O 0.0522]

73.

Tilokanātho caraṇena tena

Mattaññubhāvena hi bhojanamhi,

Khemaṃ disaṃ sañcaratīti loke

Abbhuggato tassa siloka saddo; ()

The Lord of the Three Worlds, by that practice—indeed, by being moderate in food—'fares in a safe direction in the world.' Thus has his sound of fame arisen.

74.

74.

Divā nisajjāya ca caṅka mena

Tathā rajanyā’varaṇīya dhammā,

Suddhantaro dvīhi’riyāpathehi

Sapacchimevā paṭhamamhi yāme; ()

By day, through sitting and walking, and likewise in the first and last watches of the night, he purifies his mind from obstructive states with these two postures;

75.

75.

Vuṭṭhānasañño satisampajañño

Sa’majjhimasmiṃ muni dakkhiṇena,

Passena kappeti ca sīha seyyaṃ

Pāde padaṃ thokaka matibbidhāya; ()

In the middle watch, the sage lies down in the lion's posture on his right side, placing one foot slightly over the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, with his perception set on rising.

76. [O 0.0523]

76.

Aṅgīraso jāgariyānuyoga-

Dhammena sammācaraṇena tena,

Khemaṃdisaṃ sañcaratīti tassa

Abbhuggato abbhutakitti ghoso; ()

Aṅgīrasa, by that right practice, the principle of devotion to wakefulness, 'fares in a safe direction.' Thus has his wondrous sound of fame arisen.

77.

77.

Sambodhiyā saddahanā samiddha-

Visuddhasaddhācaraṇena tena,

Iti medhānandābhidhānenayatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santike nidāne bhagavato vijjācaraṇa sampannoti nāmapaññattiyāabhidheya paridīpo ekavīsatimo saggo.

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, the Illumination of the Meaning of the Designation 'Endowed with Knowledge and Conduct,' in the Jinavaṃsadīpa, the source of joy to the hearts of all poets, composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda, in the Proximate Chronicle of the Blessed One.

Sobhanagamanattā sugatoti.

By reason of his beautiful going, he is the Sugata (Well-Gone One).
