Gadita matthagataṃ ubhayatthadaṃ

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

Always knowing the meaning of the words of what is to be known, he speaks for the welfare of people, removing what is unbeneficial; his speech is meaningful, bringing benefit in both ways. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

55. [O 0.0546]

55.

Sakalasaṅkhatadhammavimuttiyā

Gadati damma masaṅkhadhātuyā,

Ariyamaggaphalehi’pi nissitaṃ

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

He speaks the Dhamma for liberation from all conditioned things, the Dhamma concerning the unconditioned element, which is based upon the fruits of the Noble Path. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

56.

56.

Vinayavādi vineyyajane yato

Vinayanattha manattanayatvitaṃ,

Vinayanissitakaṃ gadate kathaṃ

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

Since he is a speaker of discipline to those who can be trained, endowed with the aim of discipline and the way of self-control, he speaks words based on discipline. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

57.

57.

Hadayakosanidhānavatiṃ sadā

Sadupamaṃ pariyantavatiṃ kathaṃ,

Gadati mañjugado vadanaṃ varo

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

The noble one, sweet-voiced, always speaks words possessing a treasure-store in the heart, with good similes, and well-defined. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

58. [O 0.0547]

58.

Muni rasaṅkuvitānanapaṅkajo

Purimameva giraṃ parisantare,

Gadati aṭṭhavidhaṅgikaka māsabhiṃ

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

The Sage, whose lotus-like face is stainless, speaks the profound eightfold path as his very first utterance in the assembly. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

59.

59.

Avitathaṃ vitathampi niratthaka-

Mapi kathaṃ suṇataṃ piya mappiyaṃ,

Nahivadanti kadāci tathāgatā

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

The Tathāgatas speak what is true; they never speak what is false, meaningless, or speech that is merely pleasing or unpleasing to the listeners. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

60. [O 0.0548]

60.

Avitthaṃ suṇataṃ pakiya mappiyaṃ

Abhivadantī sadatthasitaṃ kathaṃ,

Ya’dahivoharaṇe samayaññuno

Itipi so sugato sugato siyā; ()

Knowing the right time for speaking, they speak words that are true and connected to real benefit, whether pleasing or unpleasing to the listeners. Thus indeed is he the Sugata, the Well-Gone One.

61.

61.

Tāya tāya’bhisāvayaṃ janataṃ sakāya niruttiyā

Ehisāgatavādi gotamagottaketu tathāgato,

Mūlamāgadhibhāsayā gadate sabhaṃ kaparitosayaṃ

Tena so bhuvanattaye sugato siyāti suvissuto; ()

Instructing people in their own respective dialects, the Tathāgata—the banner of the Gotama lineage, who says, 'Come, welcome!'—speaks in the original Māgadhī language, delighting the assembly. Therefore, he is well-known as the Sugata throughout the three worlds.

62. [O 0.0549]

62.

Lokaṃ lokappabhavaṃ

Lokanirodhañca lokamokkhūpāyaṃ,

Catubhī abhisamayehi

Nātho sammā gato tato so sugato; ()

The world, the origin of the world, the cessation of the world, and the way to release from the world—the Protector has rightly gone by fully comprehending these four. Therefore, he is the Sugata.

Iti medhānandābhidhānena yatināna viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikeka nidāne bhagavato sutagoti paññattiyā abhidheya paridīpo. Bāvīsatimo saggo.

Thus, in the Jinavaṃsadīpa—the source of delight for the hearts of all poets, composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda—this is the exposition of the meaning of the Blessed One's designation 'Sugata', in the section on the Proximate Origin. The Twenty-second Chapter.

Taṃkho pana [O 0.0550] bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato. Itipiso bhagavā lokavidūti.

Furthermore, this good report concerning the venerable Gotama has spread: 'That Blessed One is... a Knower of the World.'

1.

1.

Tassa sa (dodhaka) lakkhaṇacāru-

Cakkavara’ṅkitapādatalassa,

Lokavidū’tipi yāva bhavaggā

Ekasilokaravo udapādi; ()

Of him whose foot-soles are marked with the beautiful and excellent wheel of auspicious signs, a single cry of praise, 'Knower of the World,' arose, reaching to the highest state of existence.

2.

2.

Lakkhaṇamūlanirodhanirodho-

Pāyavasena paki lokakamasesaṃ,

Yo paṭivijjhi tilokahito kagho

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

He who, for the benefit of the three worlds, the taintless one, fully penetrated the entire world by way of its characteristic, its origin, its cessation, and the path to its cessation, is therefore called the Knower of the World.

3.

3.

Lokamidheva kalebaramatte

Lokanidānanirodhamavedi,

Lokanirodhakaraṃka paṭipattiṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

He knew the world in this very body, the origin of the world, the cessation of the world, and the practice leading to the cessation of the world; therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

4. [O 0.0551]

4.

Lokamahambudhipāragu satta-

Saṅkhatabhājanalokapabhedaṃ,

So bhagavā’navasesamavedi

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

The Blessed One, who has gone to the far shore of the great ocean of the world, knew without remainder the distinctions of the world of beings, the conditioned world, and the container world; therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

5.

5.

So hi bhavābhavadaṭṭhisabhāva-

Ñāṇanulomikakhantipabhedaṃ,

Āsayadhamma mabujjhi pajānaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

He indeed understood the nature of views on being and non-being, the distinctions of knowledge, conformity, and acceptance, and the dispositions and natures of beings; therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

6. [O 0.0552]

6.

Pātubhavaṃ sati kāraṇalābhe

Sattavidhānusayampi janānaṃ,

So paṭivijjhi vicaṭṭitaloko

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

He fully penetrated the seven kinds of latent tendencies of beings and their manifestation when a cause is present, and the world in its full extent; therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

7.

7.

Rajjanadussanamuyhanasaddhā-

Buddhivitakkavimissavasena,

So caritaṃ paṭivijjhi pajānaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā, ()

He fully penetrated the temperament of beings, by way of its being mixed with lust, aversion, delusion, faith, intelligence, and discursive thought; therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

8.

8.

Hīnapaṇīta’dhimuttivasena

Dubbidhameva’dhimutti mavedi,

Lokaniruttivido janatāya

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

He, the knower of the world's expressions, knew the twofold disposition of people, by way of their inclination towards the inferior and the superior; therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

9. [O 0.0553]

9.

Apparajakkha manussadapāpaṃ

Ussadapāpa muḷārarajakkhaṃ,

Dubbidhalokamabujjhi yatoso

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he understood the twofold world—that of beings with little dust and little evil, and that of beings with abundant evil and great dust—therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

10.

10.

Indriyapubbaparopariyatti-

Ñāṇapabho tikhiṇindriyalokaṃ,

So paṭivijjhika mudindriyalokaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he, endowed with the radiant knowledge of the prior and subsequent states of the faculties, penetrated the world of those with keen faculties and the world of those with dull faculties, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

11.

11.

Vaṭṭavivaṭṭapatiṭṭha masādhu-

Sādhusabhāvagataṃ bhagavā so,

Dvāktike’taraloka mavedi

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because that Blessed One, established in the round of existence and its cessation, understood the nature of the unwholesome and the wholesome, and knew the twofold world—this and the other—therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

12. [O 0.0554]

12.

Sādhupasatthasadattaniyāmaṃ

Ñāpayituṃ sukarāsukarampi,

Sattanikāyamavedi yato so

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he knew the aggregate of beings, what is easy and what is difficult to teach, and the fixed nature of the true doctrine praised by the good, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

13.

13.

Kammakilesavipākavibandha-

Muttyavimuttigate paṭivijjhi,

Bhabbajaneya mabhabbajane so

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he penetrated the bondage of action, defilement, and result, and the paths to liberation and non-liberation, and because he discerned those who were capable and those who were incapable, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

14.

14.

Nipphalatāya navuttamananta-

Sattapamāṇa manāvaraṇena,

Ñāṇabalena sayaṃ viditaṃhi

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because the measure of endless beings—which is not declared due to its fruitlessness—was indeed known by himself with unobstructed power of knowledge, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

15. [O 0.0555]

15.

Vuttanayeni’ha so muni satta-

Lokamanekavidhaṃ paṭivijjhi

Sattanikāyasarojavane’ṇo

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because that Sage, by the method here described, penetrated the manifold world of beings, being subtle in his understanding of the lotus-grove of the hosts of beings, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

16.

16.

Paccayasaṇṭhitikaṃ paṭivijjhi

Saṅkhatalokamasaṅkhatadassi,

Ekavidhampyavaropitaloko

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because, as the seer of the unconditioned, he penetrated the conditioned world as that which is established by conditions, and because he had dismantled even the one-fold world, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

17.

17.

Ruppaṇalakkhaṇato’khilarūpaṃ

Nāmasalakkhaṇato catunāmaṃ,

Dubbidhaloka mavedi munindo

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because the Lord of Sages knew the twofold world—all form by its characteristic of being afflicted, and the fourfold name by its characteristic of inclining—therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

18. [O 0.0556]

18.

Lokahito sukhadukkhamupekkhā-

Vedayitattikato suvibhattaṃ,

So bhagavā kapaṭivijjhi tilokaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because that Blessed One, the benefactor of the world, penetrated the three worlds as well-distinguished by the triad of pleasant, painful, and neutral feelings, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

19.

19.

Pañcavidhaṃka muni bandhavasenā-

Hāravasena catubbidhalokaṃ,

Lokapadīpanibho paṭivijjhi

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because the Sage, who is like a lamp for the world, penetrated the fivefold world by way of the hindrances and the fourfold world by way of nutriment, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

20.

20.

Advayavādi saḷāyatanākhya-

Chabbidhalokamavedi jino so,

Sattavidhampi manaṭṭhitilokaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because that Victor, the speaker of non-duality, knew the sixfold world called the six sense-bases, and also the sevenfold world of the stations of consciousness, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

21. [O 0.0557]

21.

Lābhapabhutika maṭṭhavidhampi

Lokasabhāvamavedi yato so,

Sakyamunī navasantanivāse

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because that Sakyan Sage knew the eightfold nature of the world beginning with gain, and the nine abodes of beings, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

22.

22.

So dasabārasadhā’yatanānaṃ

Bhedavasena tilokapadīpo,

Lokamavedi tilakkhaṇavedī

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he, the lamp of the three worlds and the knower of the three characteristics, knew the world by way of the division of the ten and twelve sense-bases, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

23.

23.

Dhātuvasena yato suvibhattaṃ

Loka matha’ṭṭhadasapparimāṇaṃ,

Saṅkhatalokabhido paṭivijjhi

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he, the distinguisher of the conditioned world, penetrated it, having well-divided the world by way of the elements into its eighteen kinds, therefore, he is called the Knower of the World.

24. [O 0.0558]

24.

So maṇikañcanarūpiyamuttā-

Saṅkhapavālasilākaṭhalādiṃ,

Lokamavedi atindriyabaddhaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he knew the world of gems, gold, silver, pearls, conch shells, corals, stones, gravel, and the like, which is bound to that which is beyond the senses, therefore he is called the Knower of the World.

25.

25.

Rukkhalatāphalapallavapatta-

Pupphapakarāgapabhedavasena,

So sukhumantaralokamavedi

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because he knew the subtle, inner world by way of the distinctions among trees, vines, fruits, shoots, leaves, flowers, and their manifold colors, therefore he is called the Knower of the World.

26.

26.

Yattakamevu’tujaṭṭhakalāpa-

Rapagataṃ ihabhājanaloke,

Vijjati tampaṭivijjhi asesaṃ

Lokavidūti pavuccati tasmā; ()

Because whatever eightfold material aggregates born of season exist here in this container-world, he penetrated all of them without remainder, therefore he is called the Knower of the World.

27. [O 0.0559]

27.

So bhagavā himavatta pamāṇaṃ

Aṭṭhamahānirayādi pamāṇaṃ,

Nāgasupaṇṇavimāna pamāṇaṃ

Brahmasurāsuraloka pamāṇaṃ; ()

That Blessed One knew the measure of the Himālaya, the measure of the eight great hells and so forth, the measure of the abodes of nāgas and supaṇṇas, and the measure of the worlds of Brahmās, devas, and asuras.

28.

28.

Paṃsujalānilabhumi pamāṇaṃ

Dīpasavantisamudda pamāṇaṃ,

Merumahidharakūṭa pamāṇaṃ

Kappatarūravicanda pamāṇaṃ; ()

He knew the measure of dust, water, wind, and earth; the measure of islands, rivers, and oceans; the measure of Meru, mountains, and their peaks; and the measure of celestial trees, the sun, and the moon.

29.

29.

Paccayasaṅkhatadhammasamuhaṃ

Bhājanalokagataṃ sakalampi,

Uddhamadhotiriyaṃpaṭivijjhi

Lokavidūti pavuccatitasmā; ()

Because he penetrated the entire collection of causally conditioned phenomena, and all that is comprised in the container-world—above, below, and across—therefore he is called the Knower of the World.

30. [O 0.0560]

30.

Lokālokakaro tilokatilakoso sattalokaṃ imaṃ

Bujjhitthā’nusayāsayādividhinā saṅkhāralokaṃ tathā,

Āhārādipamāṇatādividhinā okāsalokaṃ yato

Tasmā lokavidūti vuccati jino saṅkhāraloka’ntago; ()

Because he, the illuminator of the world, the crest-jewel of the three worlds, understood this world of beings by way of latent tendencies, dispositions, and so forth, and likewise the world of formations, and the world of location by way of the measure of nutriment and so forth, therefore the Victor, who has gone to the end of the world of formations, is called the Knower of the World.

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikenidāne bhagavatolokavidūti nāmapaññattiyā abhidheyaparidīpo tevīsatimosaggo.

Thus ends the twenty-third section, the elucidation of the meaning of the designation 'The Blessed One, the Knower of the World,' in the Santikenidāna of the Jinavaṃsadīpa, which was composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda, a source of delight for the hearts of all poets.

Taṃkho pana [O 0.0561] bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato itipi so bhagavā anuttaro purisadammasārathīti.

Furthermore, this excellent report has spread concerning the venerable Gotama: 'That Blessed One is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.'

1.

1.

Abhāvato paramatarassa kassaci

Janassa sagguṇavisarehi attanā,

Samāsanibbacananayena so muni

Anuttaro sasi (rucirā)’nanambujo; ()

Because there is no person superior to himself in the range of good qualities, that sage is, by way of concise explanation, unsurpassed, like the moon with its lovely lotus-face.

2.

2.

Tathāhi so narahari sīlasampadā-

Guṇeni’maṃ abhibhavate sadevakaṃ,

Samādhinā varamatiyā vimuttiyā

Vimuttidassanaguṇasampadāyapi; ()

For indeed, that lion among men overcomes this world with its devas by the quality of his accomplishment in virtue, by concentration, by supreme wisdom, by liberation, and also by the accomplishment in the quality of the knowledge and vision of liberation.

3.

3.

Yato navijjati adhisīlasampadā-

Samādhidhipabhutiguṇehi tassamo,

Kutonu vijjati’ha taduttarītaro

Siyā tatopya’ya masamo mahāmuti; ()

Since no one equal to him is found in the qualities of accomplishment in higher virtue, higher concentration, higher wisdom, and so forth, how then could one superior to him be found here? Therefore, this great sage is unequalled.

4. [O 0.0562]

4.

Nirūpamo asamamunīhi somuni

Yato samo asamasamo siyā tato,

Tathāgatassi’ha dutiyassa kassaci

Abhāvato adutiyako tathāgato; ()

That sage is incomparable, unequalled by other sages. Since he is the equal of the unequalled, therefore he is unequalled. Because there is no second to the Tathāgata here, the Tathāgata is without a second.

5.

5.

Yato navijjati paṭimāpi tassamā

Samo tadā’samatanusampadāyapi,

Sahāyako nahi paṭividdhabodhiyā

Tato yamappaṭima’sahāyako muni; ()

Since no likeness equal to him is found, nor an equal in the accomplishment of his unequalled body, and since he has no companion in penetrating awakening, therefore this sage is without peer and without companion.

6.

6.

Kalebarenapi abhirūpahārinā

Guṇehi tappaṭisamapuggalo nahi,

Nacatthi pāvacanavibhāgakapakpane

Sayaṃ vinā bhuvi paṭibhāgapuggalo; ()

There is no person equal to him in qualities, nor even in his body, which is exceedingly beautiful and charming. Nor is there on earth, apart from himself, a comparable person in the analysis and exposition of the teaching.

7. [O 0.0563]

7.

Anaññagocaravarabodhisiddhiyā

Sa’haṃ sayambhuti paṭipuggalonahi,

Paṭiññamappayitu malaṃ sayaṃ vinā,

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

By his attainment of supreme awakening, a domain inaccessible to others, he is self-arisen and without a peer. He is able to make his proclamation himself, without another. Thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

8.

8.

Sudantapuggaladamitabbapuggale

Dameti sārayati adantapuggale,

Yato jino vinayanupāyakovido

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Because the Victor, skilled in the means of training, tames and guides the untamed, those to be tamed, and the well-tamed, he is therefore the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

9. [O 0.0564]

9.

Yathā haye mudukaguṇekhana sārathi

Tathāgato sugatikathāya dhammiyā,

Dameti sārayati tathā tathāgate

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Just as a charioteer trains horses with gentle means, so the Tathāgata, with righteous discourse leading to a good destination, tames and guides beings in that way; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

10.

10.

Yathā haye pharusaguṇena sārathi

Apāyatajjanavidhinā tathāgato,

Dameti sārayati tathā tathāgate

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Just as a charioteer trains horses with harsh means, so the Tathāgata, by the method of warning about woeful states, tames and guides beings in that way; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

11.

11.

Adammiye mudupharusena sārathi

Yathā’bhimārayati tathā tathāgato,

Jahātya’novadiya nacānusāsiya

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Just as a charioteer deals with an untamable horse with gentle and harsh means, so the Tathāgata does not abandon anyone without first admonishing and instructing them; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

12. [O 0.0565]

12.

Karī’bhidhāvati damakena sārito

Puratthimādisu disameva kevalaṃ,

Anuttarena hi naradammasārathi-

Jinena sāritapurisānatādisā; ()

An elephant, when guided by its tamer, runs only in the directions, east and so forth. But persons guided by the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed, the Victor, are not like that.

13.

13.

Nisajja katthaci sayanāsanamhi te

Disāsu aṭṭhasu atisaṅgacārino,

Vidhāvare turitamanuttaraṃ disaṃ

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Those who, sitting or lying down anywhere, wander with excessive attachment in the eight directions—he swiftly leads them to the unsurpassed direction; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

14.

14.

Patiṭṭhite muni’radhisīlasikkhayā

Vasī’nusāsiya adhicittasikkhayā,

Yathārahaṃ damayati bhabbapuggale

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

The sage, established in the training in higher virtue and instructing with mastery in the training in higher mind, tames suitable persons according to their capacity; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

15. [O 0.0566]

15.

Samāhite muni radhicittasikkhayā

Vipassanāya’pi samaṇe’nusāsiya,

Yathārahaṃ damayati bodhanārahe

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

The sage, concentrated through the training in higher mind, and having instructed ascetics in insight, tames those who are ready for awakening according to their capacity; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

16.

16.

Tathuparūpari paṭivedhapattiyā

Yathākkamaṃ anariyasekkhapuggale,

Dameti so vinayati lokanāyako

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi ()

That leader of the world, through the attainment of successively higher penetrations, tames and trains ignoble persons and learners in due order; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

17. [O 0.0567]

17.

Vineyyabandhavamanakundacandimā

Vinesi kosalamagadhādhipādayo,

Anekakhattiyapurise vināyako

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

He, a moon to the lotus-like minds of those kinsmen to be trained, trained the rulers of Kosala and Magadha and others; the guide trained many Khattiya men; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

18.

18.

Kudiṭṭhikuñjarahari kūṭadantabhu

Surādibhūsurapurise vibhāvino

Jināsabho vinayi yato’nusāsiya

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Because the bull among conquerors—a lion to the elephants of wrong views—trained by instructing prominent men who were deceitful and arrogant, brahmins, and others, he is therefore the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

19.

19.

Upālināmikapamukhe durāsade

Vināyako gahapatipaṇḍite puthu

Vinesi so upanayanakkhame yato

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Because that guide trained many wise householders difficult to approach, headed by the one named Upāli, and he trained those who were capable of being guided, he is therefore the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

20. [O 0.0568]

20.

Asaccadiṭṭhikamapi saccakavhayaṃ

Anaññavenayikanigaṇṭhanāyakaṃ

Vinesi tappabhutidigambare jino

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Because the Victor trained even the one named Saccaka, who held false views, and the Nigaṇṭha leaders who were not to be trained by others, as well as the Digambaras and others like them, he is therefore the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

21.

21.

Jināsabho sabhiyasubhaddasaññino

Tappassino timisabhido sadhammiyā

Kathāyi’tobahi samaṇepi sikkhayi

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

The bull among conquerors, with discourse on the good Dhamma, instructed the ascetics known as Sabhiya and Subhadda, who were seekers and dispellers of darkness; beyond these, he also trained other ascetics; thus he is the unsurpassed guide for persons to be tamed.

22.

22.

Damesi somuni uruvelakassapa-

Gayādikassapajaṭilādike yato,

Jaṭādhare vijaṭitajālinījaṭo

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Because that sage tamed Uruvela Kassapa, Gayā Kassapa, and other matted-hair ascetics, and he, whose net-like matted hair of defilements was disentangled, tamed those who wore matted hair, he is therefore the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

23. [O 0.0569]

23.

Pahāṇasaṃvaravinayuttaro muni

Anekakhattiyasamaṇepi sāsane,

Vinesi sārathiriva uttaruttariṃ

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

The sage, supreme in abandoning, restraint, and discipline, trained many Khattiya ascetics in the Dispensation, ever higher and higher like a charioteer; therefore, he is the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

24.

24.

Manussasoṇitapisitāsanehi so

Vinesi pīvarajaṭharaṃ nisācaraṃ,

Sughoramānavaka manekarakkhase

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi, ()

He trained the night-roaming ogre with a bulging belly who feeds on human blood and flesh, the very dreadful Āḷavaka, and many other ogres; therefore, he is the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

25.

25.

Vināyako suvinayi rāhunāmikaṃ

Mahattabhāvika masurādhipaṃ yato,

Surādhipappabhutisure tathā’sure

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Since the Guide well-tamed the one named Rāhu, the mighty lord of asuras, and likewise the gods headed by their lord and the asuras, he is therefore the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

26. [O 0.0570]

26.

Pajāpatiṃ nikhilapajānukampako

Bakābhidhānikampi tucchaladdhikaṃ,

Vinesi so naditaranīrajāsane

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

He, compassionate toward all beings, tamed Pajāpati, and also the one named Baka, who held a futile view; therefore, he is the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

27.

27.

Kasaṅkusehi’pi avineyyake yato

Tiracchajātikapurise narāsabho,

Vinesi so tisaraṇasilasaṃvare

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Since the bull among men trained, in the three refuges and moral restraint, those men of animal nature who were untrainable even with whips and goads, he is therefore the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

28.

28.

Kapolasecanamadakaṇṇacāmaraṃ

Hutāsanāsanirivabhiṃsanaṃ yato,

Damesi māraji dhanapālakuñjaraṃ

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

Since the Conqueror of Māra tamed the elephant Dhanapāla—which had ichor streaming from its temples, ears like whisks, and was terrifying like fire and a thunderbolt—he is therefore the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

29. [O 0.0571]

29.

Vinesi somuni himavantavāsinaṃ

Patāpapajjala mapalālabhoginaṃ,

Kharaṃ bhayaṅkara maravālabhoginaṃ

Anuttaro’tipi naradammasārathi; ()

That sage tamed the one dwelling in the Himalayas, blazing with majesty and feeding on raw flesh, and the fierce, terrifying serpent Aravāla; therefore, he is the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

30.

30.

Nando’panandu’ragapatiṃ mahodara-

Cūlodaroragapamukhe ca nibbise,

Dhumassikhā’nalasikhabhogīno akā

Tenā’pyanuttaranaradammasārathi; ()

He rendered harmless the serpent lords Nanda and Upananda, and other chief serpents such as Mahodara and Cūlodara—serpents with crests of smoke, flame, and fire. Therefore, he is also the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

31.

31.

Damanupāyakovido hi bodhaneyyabandhave

Ariyamaggavīthibhāsuraṃ varaṃ sivamapakuraṃ,

Paṭipadārathena sārayi yatheva sārathi

Purisadammasārathiti vuccate anuttaro; ()

Indeed, skilled in the means of taming, he guided his kinsmen who were fit to be awakened with the chariot of the practice, just as a charioteer does, along the shining avenue of the Noble Path—excellent, auspicious, and banishing evil. Thus is he called the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed.

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā varacite sakalakavijana hadayānanda dānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikenidāne bhagavato anuttaro purisadammasārathīti nāma paññattiyā abhidheya paridīpo catubbīsatimosaggo.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the Jinavaṃsadīpa—a work composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda, a source of delight for the hearts of all poets—in the section of the Santike Nidāna, being the elucidation of the meaning of the designation: 'The Blessed One is the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed'.

Taṃkho pana [O 0.0573] bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇekitti saddo abbhuggato itipi sobhagavā satthā devamanussānaṃti.

Furthermore, concerning the venerable Gotama, this good report of his fame has spread: 'That Blessed One is the Teacher of gods and humans.'

1.

1.

Kantāraṃ kharatakkaraṃ nirudakaṃ kattāramotārimaṃ

Kantāraṃ migarājakuñjaramahā (saddulavikkīḷitaṃ),

Kantāraṃ avatārabhurijanataṃ yo satthavāho sudhi

Tāretvā nayate dayāparavaso khemantabhumiṃ yathā; ()

Just as a wise caravan leader, overcome by compassion, leads across and guides to the land of safety the many folk who have entered a wilderness—a wilderness harsh and stony, waterless, a precipice difficult to descend, where lions, elephants, and great tigers roam;

2.

2.

Iccevaṃkaruṇānidhānahadayo saṃsāradukkhāture

Satte jātijarāvikāramaraṇassokādikantārato,

Tāretvā dasasaṃkilesagahanā pāpesi khemaṃpuraṃ

Tasmā satthupasatthakittivisaro satthā’ti sampattharī; ()

Even so, he whose heart is a treasury of compassion, having led beings afflicted by the suffering of saṃsāra across the wilderness of birth, aging, disease, death, sorrow, and the like, and across the thicket of the ten defilements, brought them to the city of safety. Therefore, his widespread and lauded fame as 'Teacher' has spread abroad.

3. [O 0.0574]

3.

Atthā’natthavicāraṇā’ticaturo lokuttaratthena’pi

Yasmā sāsati lokiyena ubhayena’tthenalokaṃ imaṃ,

Sabrahmaṃ sanarāmaraṃ sasamaṇaṃ sabrāhmaṇaṃ yohi so

Satthā’tveva pasatthakittinikaro satthāramabbhuggato; ()

Since he, exceedingly skilled in discerning the beneficial and the unbeneficial, instructs this world with its Brahmās, its humans and devas, its ascetics and brahmins, by means of both worldly and supramundane benefit, a chorus of lauded fame has therefore arisen for him as 'Teacher'.

4.

4.

Bhītiṃ jātijarārujādikasiraṃ nissāya jātaṃhi yo

Satthā satthadharorivā’rivisaraṃ nikkhittasattho sadā,

Sattānaṃ tasasate vihiṃsati dhiyā siddhatthasāro tato

So satthā’ti yasosarīrasurabhī lokattayaṃ vyāpayī; ()

He, the Teacher, having always laid down the weapon, with his wisdom destroys the fear born from birth, aging, sickness, and the like—just as a swordsman destroys a host of foes. He whose essential purpose is accomplished does not harm trembling beings. Therefore, the fragrance of the body of his fame as 'Teacher' pervades the three worlds.

5.

5.

Lokatthābhirato anatthavirato jātyādikantārato

Uttāretica satthavāhasadiso yo atthadhammenavā,

Satte sāsati hiṃsatī’ti janatāsantānajātaṃ bhayaṃ

Vuttā’nvatthavasena sohibhagavā satthāti vaṇṇīyate; ()

Delighting in the world's welfare, averse to what is harmful, he, like a caravan leader, leads beings across the wilderness of birth and so on. He instructs beings with the beneficial teaching. By the true etymological meaning of the word, the fear born in the minds of people that 'he harms' is allayed. Therefore, the Blessed One is praised as 'Teacher'.

Taṃkho panabhavantaṃ [O 0.0575] gotamaṃ evaṃkalyāṇe kittisaddo abbhuggato itipiso bhagavā buddhoti.

Furthermore, concerning the venerable Gotama, this good report of his fame has spread: 'That Blessed One is the Buddha, the Awakened One.'

6.

6.

Yo saṅkhāravikāralakkhaṇaparosaṅkhārapaññattisu

Ñeyyatthesva’nanussutesu purimaṃ cattāri saccāni’pi,

Bujjhitvā’cariyopadesarahito tattheva sabbaññutaṃ

Patto ñāṇabalesu pāpuṇi vasībhāvaṃ sayamabhuka sayaṃ; ()

He who, without a teacher's instruction, by himself first understood the Four Truths concerning things knowable but previously unheard of—the characteristics of conditioned phenomena and their alterations, and concepts beyond the conditioned—thereby attained omniscience and achieved mastery over the powers of knowledge, being self-become.

7. [O 0.0576]

7.

Bodhetā’ti pajāya nibbacanato saccāni so bujjhitā

Saccānīti’pi saccavādi bhagavāka nissesañeyyassapi,

Matyā bujjhanasattiyā mahatiyā yasmā samaṅakgī tato

Buddho nāmasiyāti kittivisaro tambuddhamabbhuggato; ()

He is the Awakener of beings, having understood the truths by severing their craving. Because the Blessed One speaks the truth about the truths, and because he, by his wisdom, comprehends all knowable things without remainder, and is endowed with a great power of understanding, therefore he is named 'Buddha'. Thus has widespread fame for that Buddha arisen.

8.

8.

Yesaṃja bodhanavasattiyā sumatiyā cā’naññaneyyo sayaṃ

Buddhattā ca yathāvikāsapadumaṃ so bujjhanaṭṭhenapi,

Nānābuddhaguṇassa vissavanato buddhoti suddhodanī

Abbhuggañchi tibuddhakhettabhavane taṃkittigītassaro; ()

And because, by the power of his mastery over awakening and by his great wisdom, he is not led by another; and because, by his very Buddhahood, he has 'blossomed' like a lotus, he is 'Buddha' in the sense of awakening. From the renown of his manifold Buddha-qualities, the son of Suddhodana is called 'Buddha'. The sound of that song of his fame arose in the realms of the three Buddha-fields.

9. [O 0.0577]

9.

Rāgassādhigataggamaggamatiyā dosassa mohassapi

Chinnattā ca samulaghātamakhilakelasārivaggassapi,

So khīṇāsavatāya copadhipariccāgena buddhotyayaṃ

Uccāriyati cārikittiracanā viññūhi yāvajjapi; ()

Because passion, hatred, and delusion have been cut off by the wisdom that has attained the supreme path, and because the entire host of enemies, the defilements, has been destroyed down to the root; and because of the destruction of his taints and the relinquishing of all substrates of existence, he is called 'Buddha'. This beautiful composition of his fame is proclaimed by the wise even to this day.

10.

10.

Dhammassāmi yathā pabuddhapuriso okkantaniddakkhayā

Nājjho’tiṇṇakilesamiddhavidhamā bodhāpito kenaci,

Buddhambhojatibhānano hī bhagavā sāmaṃ pabuddho yato

Buddhonāmasiyāti tabbhavayasoghoso vibhusāyate; ()

Just as a person, once awakened, has destroyed the tendency to sleep and is not overcome by the oppressive defilement of sloth and torpor, so the Lord of the Dhamma was not awakened by anyone else. Indeed, since the Blessed One, whose face shines like a lotus, is self-awakened, he is named 'Buddha'. Thus the resounding fame of his state is glorified.

11.

11.

Gatyatthāvagamatthadhātusamatāsabbhāvato vā gato

Yenekāyanamaggamuggamatimā eko, hīsambujjhīso,

Sambodhiṃ jayabodhimūlamupago sattuttaro’nuttaraṃ

Buddhotī’dha jagattaye nijayaso yāvajja vijjumbhate; ()

Or, from the very nature of the verbal root having the equivalent meanings of 'to go' and 'to understand', he has 'gone' to the end of the one-way path. He, the one of keen wisdom, awakened by himself. Having approached supreme, unsurpassed enlightenment at the root of the tree of victory, he is the highest of beings. Thus, his own fame as 'Buddha' radiates in the triple world even today.

12. [O 0.0578]

12.

Khīṇattā paramāya maggamatiyā dubbuddhiyā buddhiyā

Laddhattāpi kaanuttaruttaraguṇālaṅakkārasāmaggiyā,

So sambodhiparāyaṇo sirighaṇo buddhoti suddhodanī

Lokambhodhimalaṅkari nijayasokallolamālāhi’maṃ; ()

Because wrong views were destroyed by the supreme path-wisdom, and because he had obtained the full array of adornments of supreme and unsurpassed virtues, he, the son of Suddhodana, intent on supreme enlightenment, a mass of glory, the Buddha, adorned this ocean of the world with garlands of the waves of his own fame.

13.

13.

Sambuddho’ti’mināpadena munino saccāvabodhāvahaṃ

Ñāṇaṃ tappaṭivedhañāṇa managhaṃ nā’ññehisādhāraṇaṃ,

Buddho’tī’dha padena satthu karuṇāpubbaṅgamaṃ desanā-

Ñāṇaṃ ñeyyapadatthabodhanakaraṃ ñāṇañca dassiyate; ()

By this term 'Sambuddha' is indicated the sage's knowledge which brings realization of the truths—that faultless knowledge of penetration not shared by others. By the term 'Buddha' is shown the Teacher's knowledge of instruction, which is preceded by compassion, and the knowledge which brings understanding of knowable subjects and their meanings.

14. [O 0.0579]

14.

Taṃ sabbaññutañāṇathomanavasā sammādisambuddhi’ti-

Saddassā’riyamaggakittanavasā buddhotisaddassaca,

Yogo’pe’tthakato’tya’bhāsi vibudho so dhamma pālābhidho

Buddhānussativaṇṇanāvivaraṇe viññātasatthāgamo; ()

'Here a connection is made between the word 'Sammāsambuddha', by way of praising the knowledge of omniscience, and the word 'Buddha', by way of proclaiming the Noble Path.' Thus spoke the wise one named Dhammapāla, who was learned in the Teacher's tradition, in his subcommentary on the exposition of the Recollection of the Buddha.

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikenidāne satthādevamanussānaṃ buddhoti nāmapaññattīnaṃ abhidheya paridīpo pañcavīsatimo saggo.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter in the Jinavaṃsadīpa—a work composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda, a source of delight for the hearts of all poets—in the section of the Santike Nidāna, being the elucidation of the meaning of the designations 'Teacher of gods and humans' and 'Buddha'.

Taṃkho pana [O 0.0580] bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇe kittisaddo abbhuggato itipi sobhagavā bhagavāti.

Furthermore, concerning the venerable Gotama, this good report of his fame has spread: 'That Blessed One is indeed the Blessed One.'

1.

1.

Kavibhāratipaddhatichandasi ta-

Gguṇathomana (toṭaka) vutya’bhavi,

Bhagavā’ti vibhattapadatthavatī

Madhurā suṇataṃ surataṃ madhurā; ()

In the prosody that is the way of the poet's art, the praise of his virtues has been composed in the Toṭaka meter. The word 'Bhagavā', meaningful in its component parts, is sweet to hear, delightful, and pleasant.

2.

2.

Adhisīlasamādhimatippabhuti-

Guṇarāsivisiṭṭhatarassa tato,

Bhagavā’ti sadevamanussapajā-

Pavarassa sagāravanāma’midaṃ; ()

Therefore, for him who is most distinguished by the mass of virtues beginning with higher morality, concentration, and wisdom, this is the revered name 'Bhagavā' for the supreme one among the populace of gods and humans.

3.

3.

Bhagavāvacanena pavuccati yo

Saniruttinayo vacanatthavaro,

Sa’hi gāravaseṭṭhavisiṭṭhataro

Bhagavāti nimittakanāmamidaṃ; ()

He who is proclaimed by the word 'Bhagavā', who is supreme in the method of etymology and meaning of words—indeed, he is most distinguished by supreme reverence. This is the indicative name 'Bhagavā'.

4. [O 0.0581]

4.

Paripācitasañcitapāramitā-

Mitabhāgya manuttariyu’ttariyaṃ,

Yadi vijjati’massa anaññasamaṃ

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

If there exists for him an unsurpassed and supreme immeasurable fortune of accumulated and matured perfections, and if there exists none equal to him, that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

5.

5.

Yadi mārabalaṃ pabalaṃ sakalaṃ

Kadalī dviradoriva tālavanaṃ,

Asanī’va kilesamabhañji tato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he shattered the entire powerful army of Māra, as an elephant shatters a banana plant and a palm grove, and shattered the mass of defilements like a thunderbolt, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

6.

6.

Yadi bhaggamakā’khilalobhamapā-

Khiladosamapā’khilamohamapi,

Viparītamanokaṇañca tato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he broke all greed, all hatred, and all delusion, as well as perverse thoughts, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

7. [O 0.0582]

7.

Yadi kodhu’panāha musuyanama-

Cchariyaṃ ahirikkanirottapanaṃ,

Api makkhapalāsa mabhañji bhavā-

Bhavadiṭṭhi manajjava’maddavataṃ; ()

Since he broke anger, malice, envy, stinginess, shamelessness, and lack of fear of wrongdoing, and also broke hypocrisy, disparagement, views of existence and non-existence, lack of straightforwardness, and lack of gentleness, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

8.

8.

Kharaphārusatā karaṇuttariyaṃ

Yadi māna’bhimāna’pamādamadaṃ,

Saṭhaphārusatā karaṇuttariyaṃ

Saṭhamāyamabhañji’ti mohajaṭaṃ

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he broke harshness, roughness, the causing of superiority, conceit, pride, heedlessness, and intoxication, as well as deceit, harshness, trickery, and the tangle of delusion, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

9. [O 0.0583]

9.

Tividhā’kusalaṃ tividhabbisamaṃ

Tivitakkatimūlatisaññamapi,

Timalaṃ tipapañca mabhañji tato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he broke the threefold unwholesome actions, the threefold wrong conduct, the threefold thoughts, the three roots, and the threefold perceptions, as well as the three stains and the threefold proliferations, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

10. [O 0.0584]

10.

Caturogha catubbidhayoga catu-

Bbidhagantha catubbidhagāha mapi,

Caturāsavadhamma mabhañjitato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he broke the four floods, the four yokes, the four bonds, the four kinds of grasping, and also the four taints, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

11.

11.

Vinibaddha manokhīla nīvaraṇā-

Nya’bhīnandanamaccariyāni tato,

Yadi pañcavidhāni’pi bhaggamakā

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he broke the five kinds of defilements—the bonds, the mind's stakes, the hindrances, delight, and stinginess—therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

12. [O 0.0585]

12.

Chavivādapadāni’pi sattavidhā-

Nusayehi kusitakavatthu’mato,

Ya mabhañji’tarāti’pi aṭṭhavidhaṃ

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he broke the six grounds for dispute, the seven underlying tendencies, the eight grounds for indolence, and also the eight kinds of wrongness, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

13. [O 0.0586]

13.

Navadhā’layamula mabhañji tathā

Dasadhā’kusalaṃ dasakammapathaṃ,

Sakalāni kudiṭṭhigatāni tato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he shattered the ninefold roots of attachment, likewise the ten unwholesome courses of action and all wrong views, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

14. [O 0.0587]

14.

Pariḷāhadaraṃ vividha’ddhasataṃ

Bhavakanettivicāra mahañji tato,

Satamattasahassakilesagataṃ

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he shattered the one hundred and eight kinds of burning anguish, the discursive thoughts concerning the guide to becoming, and the hundred thousand states of defilement, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

15.

15.

Aṇimā laghimā mahimā vasitā-

Pabhuti’ssariya’ṭṭhabhagehi yato,

Subhagehi samaṅakgībbhūva tato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since he became endowed with the eight auspicious qualities of mastery, beginning with minuteness, lightness, greatness, and control, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

16.

16.

Aṇuno nanuno’ nanunokaraṇaṃ

Karaṇaṃ lahuno’lahuno aṇimā,

Laghimā mahimā mahimākaraṇaṃ

Karaṇaṃ vasitā vasitāya tahiṃ; ()

Minuteness (aṇimā) is the making of oneself minute or not minute; lightness (laghimā), the making of oneself light or not light; greatness (mahimā) is the making of greatness; mastery (vasitā) is for exercising control therein.

17. [O 0.0588]

17.

Saya micchitaṭhāna mupāgamanaṃ

Lahu vicchitakāriyasādhanatā,

Abhipatti pakamya masesavasī-

Karaṇe’sikatā paramissaratā; ()

Going to any desired place by oneself is attainment (patti); the swift accomplishment of a wished-for task is irresistible will (pākāmya); sovereignty (īsitā) is mastery in making everything subject to one's will; and there is supreme lordship (paramissaratā).

18.

18.

Nabhasā padasā gamanādivasā

Vajato pariniṭṭhitakāriyatā,

Nijakāma’vasāyikatātiyahiṃ-

Paramissariyākhyabhagā’ṭṭhavidhā; ()

Mastery over going through the sky or on water, the accomplishment of tasks while traveling, and control over one's own desires—these are the eightfold qualities known as supreme masteries.

19.

19.

Catumagga catupphalasantipadā-

Riyadhammasamuhabhagehi yuto,

Vinalīkatapāpamalehi tato

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Because he is endowed with the qualities of the four paths, the four fruits, the attainment of peace, and the collection of noble principles, and is rid of the stains of evil, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

20. [O 0.0589]

20.

Caraṇadiguṇa’tisayādhigatā-

Samakittisarīrabhageta yuto,

Bhuvanattayavipphuritena tato

Bhagavāti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Having attained the surpassing virtues beginning with conduct, endowed with a quality of unequalled fame and a body radiant throughout the three worlds, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

21.

21.

Janalocananīharaṇāya nirū-

Pama rūpasarīragatāya tato,

Nikhilāvayavassiriyā sabito

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

For delighting the eyes of people, being one who possesses an incomparable physical form, and being endowed with the splendor of all his limbs, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

22.

22.

Abhipatthita micchita mattahitaṃ

Parasattahitampi samijjhati yaṃ,

Iti tādisakāmabhagena yuto

Bhagavā’ti pavuccati so bhagavā; ()

Since that which is longed for and wished for—one's own welfare and the welfare of other beings—is accomplished, and since he is thus endowed with such a quality of will, therefore that Blessed One is called 'Bhagavā'.

Tathāhi’ssa paññattasikkhāpadāni

Navītikkamante samuddo’va velaṃ; ()

Even giving up their lives, his disciples firmly worship the Victor with Dhamma offerings. Indeed, his enacted precepts are not transgressed, like the ocean its shore.

86.

86.

Pavuccanti bhāgāti dhammassabhāva-

Vibhāgā hi te khandhadhātvādinā’pi,

Atītādirūpādibhedehi tepi

Anekappabhedā vibhattā bhavantī; ()

They are called “portions” (bhāgā), for they are divisions of the nature of Dhamma, by way of aggregates, elements, and so on; and also by distinctions of past, etc., and form, etc., they are divided into many kinds.

87. [O 0.0614]

87.

Papañcattayaṃ sabbasaṃyojanāni

Jino ganthayogā’savo’gho’padhīca,

Samucchijja maggena nibbānadhātvā-

Mataṃ so pibanto vamī te ca bhāge; ()

The three proliferations, all fetters, the knots, the yokes, the taints, the floods, and the substrata—the Victor, having cut them off by the path, drinking the deathless element of Nibbāna, vomited those portions.

88.

88.

Chacakkhādivatthuni jā’rammaṇāni

Chacittāni chabbedanā phassachakkaṃ,

Chasaññā chataṇhā chasañcetanā cha-

Bbitakke vicāre cha bhāge vamīti; ()

The six bases beginning with the eye and their objects, the six consciousnesses, six feelings, the sixfold contact, six perceptions, six cravings, six volitions, and six kinds of thoughts and reflections—these portions he vomited.

89.

89.

Yamā’nanda cattañca vantaṃ vimuttaṃ

Pahīṇaṃ vinissaṭṭha maṅgīrasassa,

Na taṃ jātu paccessatītyā’bha satthā

Yathāvuttabhāge vamītvevameva; ()

“Whatever, Ānanda, has been given up, vomited forth, freed from, abandoned, and relinquished by Aṅgīrasa, that will never return,” declared the Teacher, having thus vomited forth the portions as described.

90. [O 0.0615]

90.

Jino kaṇhasukkeca vajjānavajje

Nihīnappaṇite adhamme ca dhamme,

Asādhāraṇena’ ggamaggā’nanena

Apaccāgamaṃ pāpayī uggirīti; ()

The Victor, regarding the dark and the bright, the faulty and the faultless, the inferior and the sublime, the unwholesome and the wholesome dhammas, by means of the supreme path and unique knowledge, brought them to a state of non-return; he vomited them forth.

91.

91.

Paresañca saṃsāranirākaramhā

Samullumpanatthāya kullūpamaṃ so,

Yathājjhāsayaṃ desayitvāna dhammaṃ

Pamāpesi tehā’pi bhāge’ti sabbe; ()

And for the sake of rescuing others from the round of existence, he, having taught the Dhamma, which is like a raft, according to their inclinations, caused all those portions to be dispelled from them as well.

92.

92.

Pure pūrayaṃ pāramīdhammajātaṃ

Mahābodhisatto samāno bhagābyaṃ,

Siriṃ issarattaṃ yasohatthasāraṃ

Vamī chaḍḍhanīyaṃ yathākheḷapiṇḍaṃ; ()

Previously, while fulfilling the collection of perfections, being the Great Bodhisatta, he vomited forth glory, sovereignty, fame, and essential wealth, which are to be discarded like a lump of phlegm.

93. [O 0.0616]

93.

Tathāhi’ssa laddhaṃ pure somanassa-

Vhayo temiyo’yogharo hatthipālo,

Kumārosamāno’bhinikkhamma gehā

Siriṃ devarajjassiriṃ uggiri so, ()

Indeed, in the past, as Somanassa, Temiya, Ayoghara, and Hatthipāla, being a prince and having gone forth from home, he vomited forth glory and the splendor of divine kingship.

94.

94.

Anekāsu jātīsu sampannabhogo

Bhāge laddhabhoge’vamevu’ggiritvā,

Sakaṃ hatthagaṃ pacchime attabhāve

Anomassiriṃ cakkavattissirimpi; ()

In many births, endowed with abundant wealth, having thus vomited forth the portions of wealth gained, in his final existence he also vomited forth the incomparable glory that was in his hand, even the glory of a universal monarch.

95.

95.

Catuddīpikaṃ devarajjā’dhipacca-

Samānādhipaccaṃ yathābhucca muccaṃ,

Yasañcā’pi tatnissayaṃ pañcakāme

Alaggo tiṇaggāya’pā maññamāno; ()

The dominion over the four continents, a supremacy equal to that of a divine king, truly supreme; and also the fame dependent on that, and the five strands of sensual pleasure—unattached, he regarded them as worth less than the tip of a blade of grass.

96. [O 0.0617]

96.

Pahāyā’ bhigantvābhisambodhirajje

Patiṭṭhāya saddhammarājā babhuva,

Asāre tusāre’va saṃsārasāre

Suvuttappakāre bhage so vamīti; ()

Having abandoned them, and having attained the kingdom of supreme enlightenment, being established therein, he became the King of the True Dhamma. Regarding the essence of saṃsāra as essenceless, like chaff, he thus vomited forth those well-described portions.

97.

97.

Pavattanti nakkhattarūpehi bhehi

Samaṃ cakkavāḷāvakāsesu yātā,

Tikuṭaddi kuṭaddi canda’kka neru-

Vimānādisobhā bhagā nāma honti; ()

The splendors of the constellations and forms which, together with their lights, move through the spaces of the world-spheres; the splendors of the Tikuṭa and Kūṭa mountains, the moon, the sun, Meru, celestial mansions, and so forth—these are called 'portions' (bhagā).

98.

98.

Jino tassamaṅgī janokāsaloke

Have chandarāgappahāṇena yena,

Mahābodhimaṇḍe nisinnosamāno

Vibhūtāvibhūte bhāge te vamīti; ()

The Victor, indeed, in this world of beings, by means of abandoning desire and lust, while seated at the Great Bodhi-maṇḍala, thus vomited forth those portions, both manifest and unmanifest.

99. [O 0.0618]

99.

Sobhāgavā’ti bhatavā’ti bhagevanī’ti

Bhāgevanī’ti abhipatthayi bhattavā’ti,

Bhāgevamī’ti tibhavesu bhagevamī’ti

Anvatthato hi bhagavā bhagavā samañño; ()

'Possessing fortune,' 'having analyzed,' 'vanquisher of portions,' 'possessor of portions,' 'one who aspired,' 'one who partook,' 'one who vomited portions,' 'one who vomited portions in the three existences'—indeed, in accordance with its meaning is the designation 'Bhagavā'.

100.

100.

Icceva’massa arahādiguṇappabandha-

Pubbācalu’bbhavayasovisarosadhīso,

Pajjañca sajjanamanokumudāni’ve’daṃ

Cittāni bodhayati kiṃ purisādhamānaṃ; ()

Thus, this continuous stream of his qualities, beginning with Arahantship—like the moon with its spreading splendor arising from the eastern mountain—and this verse awaken the minds of the good, which are like water lilies; what then of the minds of vile persons?

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānanda dānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikenidāne bhagavā’tināmapaññattiyā abhidheyaparidīpo chabbīsatimo saggo.

Here ends the twenty-sixth chapter, "The Exposition of the Meaning of the Designation 'Bhagavā'," in the Jinavaṃsadīpa, a source providing joy to the hearts of all poets, composed by the monk named Medhānanda, in the Santikenidāna.

1. [O 0.0620]

1.

Ettha’ttahisampattiparahitapaṭipattito

Nissīmāpi dvidhā buddhaguṇā saṅgahitā kathaṃ; ()

Here, how are the Buddha's qualities, though boundless, summarized in two ways, namely, through the attainment of his own welfare and the practice for the welfare of others?

2.

2.

Tāsva’ttahitasampattisaddhammacakkavattino;

Pahāṇasampadāñāṇasampadābhedato dvidhā; ()

Among those, the attainment of his own welfare, for the Wheel-turning Monarch of the True Dhamma, is twofold, distinguished as the perfection of abandoning and the perfection of knowledge.

3.

3.

Rūpakāyā’nubhāvāsuṃ tatthe’va’ntogadhā dvidhā,

Paratthapaṭipattī’pi payogāsayabhedato; ()

The powers of the form-body are included therein. The practice for the benefit of others is also twofold, distinguished by application and intention.

4.

4.

Payogo lābhasakkārasilokanirapekkhino,

Dukkhū’pasamaṇatthāya nīyyāniko’padesanā; ()

The application, on the part of one who is indifferent to gain, honor, and fame, is the teaching that leads to liberation for the sake of the stilling of suffering.

5.

5.

Āsayo devadattādipaccāmittajanesupi,

Hitajjhāsayatā niccaṃ mettākantāya bhattuno; ()

The intention is the constant disposition for the welfare even of hostile persons such as Devadatta, through the Master's cherished loving-kindness.

6. [O 0.0621]

6.

Indriyā’paripakkānaṃbodhaneyyāna manvahaṃ,

Paññindriyādisampākasamayā’vagamādito; ()

Daily, for those to be awakened whose faculties are unripe, from the understanding of the time of the ripening of the wisdom faculty and others;

7.

7.

Deyyadhammapaṭiggāhappabhutīhā’ nukampiya,

Parahitapaṭipatyā’si paresaṃ hitasādhanaṃ; ()

Out of compassion, by means of accepting offered requisites and so forth, the welfare of others was accomplished through the practice for the benefit of others.

8.

8.

Tesaṃ guṇaviseyānaṃ vibhāvanavasenapi,

Pāḷiyaṃ arahantyādipadānaṃ gahaṇaṃ kathaṃ; ()

And for the purpose of explaining those specific qualities, how are the terms such as 'Arahant' and so forth taken up in the Pāli text?

9.

9.

Tatthā’rahanti iminā padena paridīpitā,

Pahāṇasampadānāma attano hitasampadā, ()

Therein, by this word 'Arahant', is indicated the perfection of abandoning, namely, the attainment of one's own welfare.

10.

10.

Padehi sammāsambuddho lokavidūti attano,

Ñāṇasampattisaṅkhātā nahitasampatti dīpitā; ()

By the terms 'Sammāsambuddho' and 'Lokavidū', the attainment of his own welfare, which is designated the perfection of knowledge, is declared.

11.

11.

Vijjācaraṇasampanno’ti’minā dassitā’ttano,

Vijjācaraṇappabhuti sabbā’pi hitasampadā; ()

By this term, 'Vijjācaraṇasampanno', is shown the entirety of his own attainment of welfare, which begins with knowledge and conduct.

12. [O 0.0622]

12.

Sugato’ti’minā vuttā paṭṭhāyapaṇidhānato,

Attanohitasampatti paratthapaṭipattica; ()

By this term 'Sugato', is stated, beginning from his aspiration, the attainment of his own welfare and the practice for the welfare of others.

13.

13.

Satthā devamanussānaṃ purisadammasārathī,

Paratthapaṭipatye’va padañcayehi dīpitā; ()

By the pair of terms, 'Satthā devamanussānaṃ' and 'Purisadammasārathī', the practice for the benefit of others is itself declared.

14.

14.

Padañcayena buddhoti bhagavāti vibhāvitā,

Yāva’ttahitasampatti parahitapaṭipatti ca; ()

By the pair of terms, 'Buddha' and 'Bhagavā', both the attainment of his own welfare and the practice for the welfare of others are made known.

15.

15.

Tidhā buddhaguṇā hetuphakhalasatto’pakārato,

Saṃkhittā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’ti padehica; ()

The Buddha's qualities are summarized in three ways—with respect to cause, fruit, and helpfulness to beings—by the terms 'Arahant' and 'Sammāsambuddho'.

16.

16.

Vijjācaraṇasampanno lokavidū’ti’mehi ca,

Catūhi phakhalasampattisaṅkhātā kittitā guṇā; ()

And by these four terms—'Arahant', 'Sammāsambuddho', 'Vijjācaraṇasampanno', and 'Lokavidū'—the qualities designated as the attainment of fruition are extolled.

17. [O 0.0623]

17.

Purisadammasārathi satthā dvīhipadehi tu,

Sattopakārasampattivasena gaditā guṇā; ()

But by the two terms, 'Purisadammasārathī' and 'Satthā', the qualities are described by way of the attainment of helpfulness to beings.

18.

18.

Phalasamapattisattopakārasamapattibhedato,

Ubho buddhaguṇā buddho’ti’minā paridīpitā; ()

By way of the distinction between the attainment of fruition and the attainment of helpfulness to beings, both sets of the Buddha's qualities are declared by this term, 'Buddha'.

19.

19.

Sugato bhagavā dvīhi padehā’diccabandhuno,

Vibhāvitā hetu phalasatto’pakārasampadā; ()

By the two terms, 'Sugata' and 'Bhagavā,' the Kinsman of the Sun is revealed as endowed with the perfections of cause, result, and benefiting beings.

20.

20.

Thīrasārataro’dāruttuṅga sagguṇamerunā,

Girirājā’pi nīcattaṃ jagāma jinarājino; ()

By the Meru of his good qualities, more stable in essence and exceedingly lofty, even the King of Mountains was brought to lowliness before the King of Conquerors.

21.

21.

Tassā’nupubbagambhīrasampuṇṇaguṇasāgare,

Sāgaro’yaṃ paricchinno bindumattaṃ’va khāyati; ()

In that ocean of his virtues, successively deep and completely full, this finite ocean appears as but a drop.

22.

22.

Thāvarā’calapatthiṇṇapatiṭṭhāguṇabhumiyā,

Nopeti paṃsupathavī kalabhāgampi satthuno; ()

The dusty earth does not equal even a fraction of the Teacher's ground of virtues, which is steadfast, unmoving, widespread, and well-established.

23. [O 0.0624]

23.

Cakkavāḷasahassāni sambādhikaḷitāni’va,

Guṇalesānubhāvena dissanteravibandhuno; ()

By the power of a mere trace of the virtues of the Kinsman of the Sun, thousands of world-systems appear as if crowded together.

24.

24.

Anantāpariyantena guṇākāyena satthuno,

Ākāso’mananto’pi antabhuto’va gamyate; ()

Evaṃ buddhaguṇānantāpariyantā acintiyā,

Avāciyā’nopameyyā ahoacchariyabbhutā; ()

By the infinite and boundless body of virtues of the Teacher, even the endless sky is perceived as if it were finite. Thus, the Buddha's virtues are infinite, boundless, inconceivable, inexpressible, and incomparable—oh, how wonderful and amazing!

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikenidāte navannamarahādiguṇānaṃ saṅkhepanayaparidīpo

Thus ends the concise elucidation of the nine qualities beginning with 'Araham,' in the Santika Nidāna of the Jinavaṃsadīpa—a source of joy for the hearts of all wise people—composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda.

Sattavīsatimosaggo.

The Twenty-seventh Chapter.

1. [O 0.0625]

1.

Dhutanijjharacāmarānilena

Sisire kūṭabhujehi gijjhakūṭe,

Haribhudharahāridehadhāri

Viharanto karuṇākaro kadāci; ()

Sometimes the Compassionate One, bearing a body as charming as a golden mountain, dwelt on the cool Vulture Peak with its craggy slopes, fanned by a breeze from its streams that was like a shaken whisk.

2.

2.

Vasamāna masesabhikkhusaṅghaṃ

Iha rājaggahanāmarājadhānyā,

Varamaṇḍalamāla mānayassu

Munirānandayanindamiccavoca; ()

The Sage, dwelling here in the royal city named Rājagaha, delighting the king, spoke thus: 'Lead the entire assembly of monks to the excellent assembly hall.'

3.

3.

Yati sampati sannipātayitvā

Yatisaṅghaṃ yatirājamabruvī so,

Rucirañjalipūjitaṅghikañjo

Samayaṃ maññatha yassadāni bhante; ()

That ascetic, having now convened the assembly of ascetics, addressed the King of Ascetics, whose beautiful lotus-feet were worshipped with reverently cupped hands: 'Reverend Sir, you may now deem the time to be right.'

4. [O 0.0626]

4.

Atha kho sugato tato’higantvā

Navasañjhāghanaraṃsivippakiṇṇo,

Varamaṇḍalamāḷa motarittha

Ravi mandāramivodayā’calamhā; ()

Then the Sugata, having gone from there, scattering dense rays like the new evening twilight, descended to the excellent assembly hall, like the sun from the dawn mountain upon Mount Mandara.

5.

5.

Tahi māsanamatthake nisinno

Migarājāriva kañcanācalagge,

Parisāsu visārado abhāsi

Munirājā’parihāniyeca dhamme; ()

Seated there at the head of the seats, like a lion-king on a golden mountain peak, the King of Sages, fearless among the assemblies, spoke on the principles of non-decline.

6.

6.

Abhinkhamiya’mbalaṭṭhikāyaṃ

Viharanto bhagavā tato puramhā,

Navapallavamaṇḍitambasākhī

Riva’nubyañjanacārurūpakāso; ()

Having gone forth from that city, the Blessed One dwelt at Ambālaṭṭhikā; his form, radiant and beautiful with the minor marks, was like a mango branch adorned with new shoots.

7. [O 0.0627]

7.

Itisīlapabhāvito samādhi

Saphalo cittapabhāvitā ca paññā,

Saphalā’ti pavattadhammacakko

Atha nālandamupāgamī sasaṅgho; ()

'Thus, concentration developed by virtue is fruitful, and wisdom developed by the mind is fruitful.' Having thus set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion, he then approached Nālandā with the Sangha.

8.

8.

Tahi mambavane yathābhirantaṃ

Viharantaṃ tamupecca theranāgo,

Makahītañjalimañjarika sirena

Caraṇacanda mavandi sāriputto; ()

There in the mango grove, the elder Nāga, Sāriputta, approached him who was dwelling as he pleased. With his clasped hands like a flower bud placed upon his head, he paid homage to the moon-like feet of the Teacher.

9.

9.

Sunisajja asajjamānañāṇaṃ

Bhagavantaṃ pacuraṃ abhitthavanto,

Nadi sihanibho abhītavācaṃ

Bhagavā ca’bbhanumodi bhāsitaṃ taṃ; ()

Having sat down well, Sāriputta, roaring like a lion with fearless speech, abundantly praised the Blessed One, whose knowledge is unattached. And the Blessed One approved of that speech.

10.

10.

Kathayaṃ adhisīlacattapaññā-

Paṭisaññuttakathaṃ tahiṃ vasitvā,

Yatisaṅghapurakkhato tato so

Agamā pāṭaligāmamuggadhīmā; ()

Having dwelt there, discussing the talk connected with higher virtue, higher mind, and higher wisdom, that one of great wisdom, escorted by the assembly of ascetics, then went from there to Pāṭaligāma.

11. [O 0.0628]

11.

Muni pāṭaligāmupāsakānaṃ

Anukampāya sumāpite nivāse,

Nivasaṃ savaṇañjalīhi peyyaṃ

Vadhuraṃ dhammasudhārasaṃ adāsi; ()

The Sage, out of compassion for the lay devotees of Pāṭaligāma, dwelt in a residence they had well constructed, and gave the sweet nectar of the Dhamma, to be received with listening ears and reverent, cupped hands.

12.

12.

Acirāpagatesu’pāsakesu

Bhagavā pāṭaligāmikesu tesu,

Janasuññaniketanaṃ anañño

Pavisitvāna akāsi sīhaseyyaṃ; ()

When those lay followers of Pāṭaligāma had not long departed, the Blessed One, alone, entered the dwelling now empty of people and assumed the lion's posture.

13.

13.

Magadhādhipatissa bhupatissa

Nagaraṃ tatra sunidhavassakārā,

Sacivā tidasehi mantayitvā

Viya tasmiṃsamaye sumāpayanti; ()

At that very time, the ministers Sunidha and Vassakāra were having a city built there for the king, the lord of Magadha, as if they had consulted with the Thirty-three gods.

14. [O 0.0629]

14.

Abhipassiya dibbacakkhunā taṃ

Bhagavā’nanda mavoca hessate’daṃ,

Ariyā’yatanaṃ vaṇippatho’ti

Nagaraṃ pāṭaliputtanāma maggaṃ; ()

Having perceived this with the divine eye, the Blessed One said to Ānanda: 'This will become a foremost city named Pāṭaliputta, a dwelling for noble ones and a center of trade.'

15.

15.

Mithubhedavasena aggitovā

Dakato pāṭaliputtasaññino kho,

Nagarassa kadāci antarāyā

Muni vedehamuniṃ tayo’tya’voca; ()

The Sage then said to the sage of Videha: 'Indeed, for the city known as Pāṭaliputta, there will be three dangers: from internal dissension, from fire, and from water.'

16.

16.

Tadahe’vupasaṅkamiṃsu yena

Bhagavā tena sunīdhavassakārā,

Jinapādakirīṭaphuṭṭhasīsā

Abhisitte’va khaṇaṃ lasiṃsu’ ho te; ()

On that very day, Sunidha and Vassakāra approached where the Blessed One was. With their heads touched by the Victor's feet, they shone for a moment, ah, as if newly consecrated!

17.

17.

Thirasāraguṇena dhammarañño

Dhanudaṇḍeva ṭhitā nataṅakgayaṭṭhi,

Tadubho savivā nimantayiṃsu

Sugataṃ ajjatanāya bhojanena; ()

With bodies bent like bow-staves, standing in awe of the steadfast, essential virtue of the King of Dhamma, those two, with their retinues, invited the Sugata for that day's meal.

18. [O 0.0630]

18.

Adhivāsana massa te vidatvā

Paṭiyattehi paṇītabhojanehi,

Bhagavanta matappayuṃ sasaṅgaṃ

Kamalāvāsanivāsagaṃ sahatthā; ()

Having understood his acceptance, they, with their own hands, satisfied the Blessed One—the dweller in the lotus-abode—together with the Sangha, with fine foods that had been prepared.

19.

19.

Bhagavā’tha sunīdhavassakāre

Paribhutto apanītapattapāṇī,

Anumodi nipīya dhammapānaṃ

Pacuraṃ pītiphuṭantarā’bhavuṃ te; ()

Then the Blessed One, having finished his meal provided by Sunīdha and Vassakāra and having withdrawn his hand from the bowl, gave his blessing. Having drunk the nectar of the Dhamma, they were inwardly pervaded with abundant joy.

20.

20.

Anuyantajanehi dhammarañño

Vajato bhikkhupūrakkhatassa tamhā,

Puthuloratalena yaṃ visālaṃ

Nagaradvāra manantaribabhuva; ()

As the King of Dhamma departed from there, escorted by the assembly of monks and followed by the people, that broad and wide city gate became immediately renowned.

21. [O 0.0631]

21.

Iti gotamabuddhapādaphuṭṭhaṃ

Tadidaṃ dvāra mahosī gotamākhyaṃ,

Tahi motari yattha kākakapeyyā

Muni gaṅgākhyasavanti tuṅgavīci; ()

Thus this gate, touched by the feet of the Buddha Gotama, became known as the Gotama Gate. The Sage then went down to where the river named Ganges flowed, with its high waves, full enough for crows to drink from its banks.

22.

22.

Bahaḷā’nilabhaṅgavīcimālā-

Lulitāyā’ti gabhīraninnagāya,

Ya manaṅgapabhaṅguro tarittha

Tayidaṃ gotamatitthanāma māsi; ()

The place where the Crusher of Māra crossed that very deep river—agitated by strong winds and garlands of breaking waves—that place became known as Gotama's Ford.

23.

23.

Sugato paratīrago’ghatiṇṇo

Janataṃ passiya sāvakehi saddhiṃ,

Taraṇattha mulumpakullanāvā

Pariyesanta mudānagātha māha; ()

The Well-Gone One, having reached the far shore and crossed the flood, seeing the people together with his disciples, while seeking rafts, floats, and boats for the purpose of crossing, spoke this verse of inspiration.

24. [O 0.0632]

24.

Narasārathi yena bhumikantā-

Makuṭākārakuṭīhi nāvakāso,

Upasaṅkami tena koṭigāmo

Uditambhoru hu’pāhanappitaṅghī; ()

The Guide of Men approached Koṭigāma by that way where, on the surface of the earth, there was no space even for crown-shaped huts; his feet were placed on shoes like rising lotuses.

25.

25.

Ahamasmi pabuddhasaccadhammo

Punaruppatti nacatthi me’ti vatvā;

Tahi movadi vāsago tisikkhā-

Paṭisaṃyuttakathāya bhikkhusaṅghaṃ; ()

Having said, 'I am awakened to the true Dhamma; there is no further rebirth for me,' there the Master exhorted the community of monks with a talk connected with the three trainings.

26.

26.

Muni nātikanāmagāmayāto

Kathitānandayatindapuṭṭhapañho,

Paridīpayi dhammadappaṇākhyaṃ

Pariyāyaṃ gatipaccavekkhaṇāya; ()

The Sage, having gone to the village named Nātikā, being asked a question by the ascetic Ānanda, expounded the discourse called the Mirror of the Dhamma, for the purpose of reviewing one's destiny.

27. [O 0.0633]

27.

Arahādiguṇakaroka mahesi

Viharaṃ tatrapi giñjakānivāse,

Piṭakattayasaṅgahaṃ vasinaṃ

Adhisīlādikathaṃ kathesi bhīyyo; ()

The Great Seer, possessor of qualities beginning with Arahantship, while dwelling there in the Brick Hall, spoke further to the masters of themselves a discourse concerning higher virtue and so forth, which is a compendium of the three Piṭakas.

28.

28.

Sugato pagato sabhikkhusaṅgho

Atha vesālipuriṃ purīnamaggaṃ,

Tahi mambavane vasaṃ vasinaṃ

Satipaññāparamaṃ abhāsi dhammaṃ; ()

Then the Well-Gone One, together with the community of monks, proceeded to Vesālī, the foremost of cities. Dwelling there in the mango grove, he taught the masters of themselves the Dhamma that is supreme in mindfulness and wisdom.

29.

29.

Jinagandhagajo mama’mbapāli-

Gaṇikā ambavane’ni’dāni sutvā,

Abhiruyha payāsi bhaddayānaṃ

Kucabhārātisamiddhabhattibhārā; ()

The courtesan Ambapālī, hearing that the Victor, the fragrant elephant, was now in her mango grove, mounted a splendid carriage and departed, heavy with the weight of her breasts and exceedingly rich with the burden of devotion.

30.

30.

Gaṇikā’tha katañjalinisinnā

Ghanapīnatthanabhārarumbhīteva,

Karavikavirāvamañjughoso

Madhuraṃ dhamma mabhāsi tāya satthā; ()

Then the courtesan, seated with hands clasped in reverence, as though impeded by the weight of her dense and plump breasts, was addressed by the Teacher, whose voice is as lovely as the call of the Karavīka bird, who spoke the sweet Dhamma to her.

31. [O 0.0634]

31.

Katabhattanimantanā pasādaṃ

Rasanādāmasarehi vāharanti,

Pavidhāya padakkhiṇaṃ munindaṃ

Agamā haṃsavadhuva mandiraṃ sā; ()

Having made the invitation for a meal, expressing her faith with the sounds from the strings of her tongue, and having circumambulated the Lord of Sages, she went to her residence like a female swan.

32.

32.

Ahatāhatanīlapītaratta-

Sitamañjiṭṭhavirāgasāṭakehi,

Sunivatthasupārutā’bhirūḷhā

Suraputtāriva bhaddabhaddayānaṃ; ()

The Licchavis, well-dressed and well-covered in garments new and worn, blue, yellow, red, white, madder-dyed, and plain, ascended their auspicious and excellent carriages, like sons of the gods.

33.

33.

Atha licchavirājarājaputtā

Upasaṅkamma paṇamma dhammarañño,

Nakharaṃsipabandhasindhutīre

Samayuṃ maggaparissamaṃ nisinnā; ()

Then the Licchavi kings and royal princes, having approached and paid homage to the King of Dhamma, sat down and relieved the weariness of their journey.

34. [O 0.0635]

34.

Vilasiṃsu kiriṭabhiṅgamālā-

Viraḷā licchavikañjakosarāsi,

Ravibandhavadhammabhākarena

Phuṭitā’dhaṭṭhitasilagandhasāli; ()

The assembly of Licchavis shone like a lotus pond, sparsely adorned with crowns like garlands of bees. Touched by the Kinsman of the Sun, the dispenser of the Dhamma, they blossomed, established in virtue, fragrant and noble.

35.

35.

Saphalīkatadullabhantabhāvā

Viphalībhutanimantānā janā te,

Virajaṅghirajopisaṅgamoḷī

Pura mārūḷharathā tato payāsuṃ; ()

Those people, whose rare final existence was made fruitful, yet whose invitations had become fruitless, departed thence for the city, having mounted their chariots, with feet free from dust but crowns touched by dust.

36.

36.

Janalocanatoraṇākarāḷaṃ

Avatiṇṇo vimalañjasaṃ sasaṅgho,

Gaṇikāya gharaṃ mahesi pāto

Caraṇakkantathalambujo jagāma; ()

In the morning, the Great Seer, together with the Sangha, entered upon the stainless path, which was a grand sight for the eyes of the people. He went to the courtesan’s house, his feet like lotuses treading upon the ground.

37. [O 0.0636]

37.

Katabhojanasaṅgabhāvasāne

Gaṇikā pañjalikā nisajja dhammaṃ,

Sunisamma sasāvakassa’dāsi

Sugatassa’mbavanaṃ samiddhasaddhā; ()

When the partaking of the meal was concluded, the courtesan, with abundant faith, sat with hands clasped in reverence. Having listened well to the Dhamma, she gave the mango grove to the Well-Gone One and his disciples.

38.

38.

Muni rambavanaṃ paṭiggahetvā

Viharitvātahimeta deva dhammaṃ,

Kathayaṃ adhisīlacittapaññā-

Paramaṃ beḷuvagāmakaṃ jagāma; ()

The Sage, having accepted the mango grove and having dwelt there, speaking on that same Dhamma which is supreme in higher virtue, higher mind, and higher wisdom, then journeyed to the village of Beluva.

39.

39.

Ahamettha vasāmi bhikkhave’ko

Samaṇhe’ttasahāyakehi tumhe,

Upagacchatha vassa massamesu

Muni vesālisamanatatotya’bhāsi; ()

From the vicinity of Vesālī, the Sage spoke thus: 'Monks, I will dwell here alone. You should enter upon the rains retreat in hermitages, with your friends and companions.'

40. [O 0.0637]

40.

Jitamārabalasasa beḷuvasmiṃ

Atha vassupagatassa ghorarogo,

Udapādi ca māraṇantikā’suṃ

Kaṭukā kāyikavedanā’tibāḷhā; ()

Then in Beluva, as he who had conquered the forces of Māra entered the rains retreat, a severe illness arose, and sharp, exceedingly strong bodily feelings, leading to death, occurred.

41.

41.

Adhivāsanakhantipārago so

Sukhadukkhesu tulāsamo tadāni,

Bhagavā avihaññamānarūpo

Adhivāsesi sato ca sampajāno; ()

That Blessed One, who had perfected endurance and patience, and was then like a balance in pleasure and pain, with his physical form undisturbed, endured mindfully and with clear comprehension.

42.

42.

Anapekkhiya tāva bhikkhusaṅghaṃ

Idhu’paṭṭhākanivedanaṃ akatvā,

Analanti mamā’nupādisesa-

Parinibbānapadaṃ sace labheyyaṃ; ()

It would not be proper for me, were I to attain the state of final Nibbāna without residue without first addressing the community of monks and without making a declaration to my attendants.

43. [O 0.0638]

43.

Vīriyena paṭippaṇāmayitvā

Balavā’bādha malabbhayāpanīyaṃ,

Paṭisaṅkharaṇārahaṃ visesaṃ

Samadhiṭṭhāya sajīvitindriyassa; ()

Having suppressed the powerful illness with energy, he made a firm resolve upon the life faculty and maintained it.

44.

44.

Bhagavā’tha samādhi mappayitvā

Paṭipassambhiya dukkhavedanaṃ so,

Pavihāsi mahāvipassanāya

Nahi vikkhamhita vedanā punāsuṃ; ()

Then that Blessed One, having applied his concentration and calmed the painful feelings, dwelt by means of great insight; the suppressed feelings did not arise again.

45.

45.

Ravibandhu vihārato’higantvā

Bahichāyāeraṇaṅgaṇappadese,

Sunisajji susajajitā sanamhi

Pariyuṭṭhāya lahuṃ gilānabhāvā; ()

The Kinsman of the Sun, having come out from his dwelling, sat down on a well-prepared seat in a shaded spot in the outer courtyard, having quickly recovered from his state of illness.

46.

46.

Jitajātijarārujo nisīdi

Yahimānandatapodhano’ pagamma,

Tahi mañjaliko mayā sudiṭṭhaṃ

Khamanīyaṃ tava sāta miccavoca; ()

Where the Conqueror of birth, aging, and disease was seated, the ascetic Ānanda approached. There, with hands clasped in reverence, he said: 'It is good to see you, venerable sir. Is your body bearable? Is it comfortable?'

47. [O 0.0639]

47.

Tava bāḷhagilānatāya bhante

Mama patthaṅghano viya’ttabhāvo,

Sakalāpi disā’nupaṭṭhahanti

Napi dhammā paṭibhanti manti vatvā; ()

He said: 'Venerable sir, because of your grave illness, my own body felt as if it were paralyzed, all the directions became unclear to me, and the teachings were no longer manifest in my mind.'

48.

48.

Apicā’si mame’sa sāvakānaṃ

Hadayassā’salavo nakiñcivatvā,

Bhagavā napanā’nupādisesa-

Parinibbāna padaṃ bhaje’ti bhante; ()

And yet, venerable sir, I had this one consolation: 'The Blessed One will not enter final Nibbāna without having said something concerning the community of disciples.'

49.

49.

Yamanantarabāhiraṃ karitvā

Nanu cā’nandapakāsito hi dhammo,

Gurumuṭṭhi tathāgatesu natthi

Vada kiṃ patthayate mame’sa saṅgho; ()

Indeed, Ānanda, the Dhamma has been taught by me without making any distinction between esoteric and exoteric doctrine. There is no 'teacher's closed fist' in the Tathāgatas. What more, then, does this community of monks expect of me?

50. [O 0.0640]

50.

Adhunā’ha masīti vassikosmi

Parijiṇṇosmi tathāgatassa kāyo,

Sakaṭaṃviya jajjaraṃ jarāya

Bhiduro vattati vekhamissakena; ()

Now I am old, eighty years of age. The Tathāgata’s body is worn out. Like a decrepit cart, it is held together with straps and keeps going only with difficulty.

51.

51.

Sanimittakavedanānirodhā

Upasampajja vimuttijaṃ samādhiṃ,

Vihareyya yadā tadāttabhāvo

Vayadhammopi atīvaphāsuhoti; ()

When a Tathāgata attains and dwells in the concentration born of liberation, through the cessation of feelings connected with signs, then his body, though subject to decay, becomes exceedingly comfortable.

52.

52.

Adhunāga miva’ttadhammadīpā

Bhavathā’naññaparāyaṇāttha tumhe,

Bhagavāvadi te’va sattamā’ti

Samaṇā bhāvitakāya cittapaññā; ()

Now, be islands unto yourselves, with the Dhamma as your island, having no other resort. Thus spoke the Blessed One to those seven ascetics who had cultivated body, mind, and wisdom.

53. [O 0.0641]

53.

Punarāgami tattha vutthavasso

Bhagavā jetavanaṃ mahāvihāraṃ,

Upagamma tadāni dhammasenā-

Pati satthāra mavandi sāriputto; ()

Having spent the rains-retreat there, the Blessed One returned to Jetavana, the great monastery. Then Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma, approached the Teacher and paid homage.

54.

54.

Vividhiddhivikubbaṇaṃ vidhāya

Yatināgo muninā katāvakāso,

Tava pacchimadassananti vatvā

Nivuto pañcasatehi satthukappo; ()

Having performed various psychic transformations, the Nāga among ascetics, having been given leave by the Muni, said, 'This is my last sight of you.' He, who was like the Teacher, was surrounded by five hundred disciples.

55.

55.

Abhinamma padakkhiṇaṃ karitvā

Bhagavantaṃ samupecca mātugehaṃ,

Janito’varake nipajjaka mañce

Parinibbāyi tadā’si bhūmicālo; ()

Having reverently circumambulated the Blessed One, he then approached his mother’s house. Lying down on the bed prepared in a private chamber, he attained Parinibbāna—and then the earth shook.

56. [O 0.0642]

56.

Atha kolitanāmatheranāgo

Parinibbāyi tathā katāvakāso,

Puna dhātusarīra mappayitvā

Munikārāpayi cetiyāni tesaṃ; ()

Then the elder Nāga named Kolita attained Parinibbāna, having been given leave in the same way. Then, having apportioned the bodily relics, the Muni had cetiyas built for them.

57.

57.

Janalocanapīyamānarūpo

Muni vesālipuraṃ kamena patvā,

Sunivatthasupāruto kulesu

Cari piṇḍāya karī’va sericārī; ()

The Muni, with a form pleasing to the eyes of the people, having gradually reached the city of Vesāli, well-robed and well-covered, wandered for alms among the families, like an elephant roaming at will.

58.

58.

Bhagavā paribhuttapātarāso

Bhavatā’nandadivāvihārakāmo,

Atha gaṇha nisīdananti vatvā

Gami cāpālasamaññacetiyaṃhi; ()

The Blessed One, having partaken of the morning meal and desiring to spend the day in seclusion, then said, “Ānanda, take the sitting mat,” and went to the Cāpāla Shrine.

59. [O 0.0643]

59.

Atha kho bhagavā nisidi yena

Tadupaṭṭhākavaro’pagamma tena,

Katapañjaliko nisidi vatvā

Ramaṇīyaṃti udenacetiyampi; ()

Then the Blessed One sat down. His excellent attendant approached, and with hands clasped in reverence, sat down at one side. The Blessed One then said: 'Lovely, too, is the Udena Shrine.'

60.

60.

Sugatassa panī’ddhipādadhammā

Caturo bhikkhu subhāvitā suciṇṇā,

Bahulīkaḷitā’ti cāha bhīyyo

Muni tiṭṭheyya sace khameyya kappaṃ; ()

And the Muni said further: 'Bhikkhu, the four bases of psychic power have been well-developed, well-practiced, and made abundant by the Sugata. Should he so wish, the Sugata could remain for an aeon.'

61.

61.

Karuṇāparibhāvitāsayena

Jitamārena tivāra mattamevaṃ,

Ujukaṃ muninā karīyamāne

Vipulobhāsanimittajappanamhi; ()

Although a clear and open hint was thus made as many as three times by the Muni, the Conqueror of Māra, whose mind was imbued with compassion...

62.

62.

Pariyuṭṭhitamānaso riva’ñño

Kharamārena pamuṭṭhamānaso so,

Na ca taṃ paṭivijjhi neva yāci

Bhagavā tiṭṭhatu yāvatā’yukappaṃ; ()

His mind was overwhelmed as if by another, his mind bewildered by the harsh Māra. He did not comprehend that hint, nor did he request, “May the Blessed One remain for the lifespan of an aeon.”

63. [O 0.0644]

63.

Vaja kaṅkhasi yassadānikālaṃ

Pahitā’nandatapodhano’tivatvā,

Vasavattivasikato muhuttaṃ

Avidūramhi nisīdi rukkhamūle; ()

Having said, 'Go, Ānanda, you may do what you think it is now time for,' and sent him away, the great ascetic, for a moment like one who has attained mastery, sat down not far away at the foot of a tree.

64.

64.

Upagañchiya bodhaneyya bandhu

Bhagavā yena pamatta bandhu tena,

Bhujagoriva bhuttanaṅgalena

Abhimānena anonataṅgayaṭṭhi; ()

Then the kinsman of the heedless approached the Blessed One, his pride unbroken and his staff-like body unbowed.

65.

65.

Ajapālasamaññino kadāci

Uruvelāya vaṭaddumassa mūle,

Katakicca? Tayā katā paṭiññā

Likhitā vattati cittapotthake me; ()

He said: 'At the foot of the Goatherd's Banyan tree in Uruvelā, you once made a promise. Is your task now complete? It is written on the tablet of my mind.'

66. [O 0.0645]

66.

Samaṇā tava sāsanā’va tiṇṇā

Adhunā dhammadharā’nudhammacārī,

Paṭipattiratā bahussutā ca

Suviyattā suvisāradā vinītā; ()

The monastics of your dispensation have indeed crossed over; they are now bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, delighting in the practice, very learned, skillful, confident, and disciplined.

67.

67.

Paṭisiddhaparappavādivādā

Sahadhammena sapāṭihāriyaṃ te,

Kathayanti kathāpayanti dhammaṃ

Parinibbātu tato bhavantya voca, ()

Having refuted the arguments of other schools with reason, they teach the Dhamma with its wonders; they teach and cause the Dhamma to be taught. Therefore, let the Blessed One attain Parinibbāna,” he said.

68.

68.

Pariniṭṭhitasabbabuddhakicco

Munirevaṃ samudirite tivāraṃ,

Analanti nirālayo bhavesu

Tadū’(pacchandasikaṃ) nisedhanāya; ()

When this had been urged three times, the Muni, for whom all the tasks of a Buddha were now complete, said, 'Enough!' in order to reject that persuasive speech, being without attachment to existences.

69. [O 0.0646]

69.

Appossukko samāno viharatu kalimā ho timāsaccayena

Saccālokappakāso durita tamahido pañcatāḷisavassaṃ;

Sammā khīṇassineho tibhuvanabhavane dhammarājappadīpo

Nibbāyissatya’bhāsi tadahani vijahañcā’yu saṅkhāravegaṃ ()

He spoke, and on that day relinquished the force of his life-formation: 'Be untroubled, Māra.
