After three months, the lamp of the King of Dhamma in the three worlds—who for forty-five years has been the light of truth dispelling the darkness of evil, his attachments rightly destroyed—will be extinguished.'

70.

70.

Cāpāle cetiye’vaṃ vijahati satiyā sampajaññenavāyu-

Saṅkāre bhūmicālo bhavi paṭupaṭahārāva gambhiraghoso,

Gajjiṃsu vijjurājibhujasatapahaṭā sukkhajimūtabheri

Loko sokandhakāre paripati janito bhiṃsano lomahaṃso; ()

At the Cāpāla Shrine, when he thus relinquished the life-formation with mindfulness and clear comprehension, the earth shook with a deep roar like the sound of a great drum. Lightning flashed, and the drums of dry clouds thundered as if struck by a hundred arms. The world fell into the darkness of sorrow, and a terrible, hair-raising fear arose.

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santike nidāne bhagavato āyusaṅkhārossajjana pavatti paridīpo aṭṭhavīsatimo saggo.

Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter in the Jinavaṃsadīpa—composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda, a source of delight for the hearts of all poets—the chapter which illuminates the account of the Blessed One's relinquishing of the life-formation, in the section on the Proximate Account.

1. [O 0.0648]

1.

Yenā’nando vasati bhagavā tena gantvā nisinno

Pādambhoje sumahiya suhebaddhamuddhāñjalihi,

Bhante sukkhāsati ca elitā hiṃsano lomahaṃso

Jāto kasmā vasumativadhū sampavedhītya’pucchi; ()

Ānanda went to where the Blessed One was staying. Having paid great reverence to his lotus feet with hands joined above his head, he sat down and asked: 'Venerable Sir, I am ill at ease, and a terrible, hair-raising fear has arisen. Why has the earth, our bride, trembled so violently?'

2.

2.

Heṭṭhā’kāse balavapavane vāyamāne kadāci

Vātaṭṭhā yā salilapathavī taṭṭhitā paṃsubhumi,

Saṅkampante yatharivatari lola kallolamāli-

Majjhotiṇṇā pathavicalanaṭṭhāna mānanda ce’taṃ; ()

Sometimes, when a strong wind blows in the space below, the earth, which rests on water, which in turn rests on wind, trembles, just as a boat trembles when tossed amidst a garland of swaying waves. Ānanda, this is one cause of an earthquake.

3.

3.

Appekacce samaṇa samaṇabrāhmaṇā appamāṇā

Āposaññā sukhumapathavi bhāvitā santi yesaṃ,

Pattābhiññā paricitavasī te samāpattilābhī

Kampentīmaṃ tadapi bhavate bhūmicālassa ṭhānaṃ; ()

Some ascetics and brahmins, who have attained supernormal powers, are skilled in mastery, and gain meditative attainments, have developed the subtle perception of earth and the immeasurable perception of water. They can cause this earth to tremble; that too is a cause of an earthquake.

4. [O 0.0649]

4.

Gabbhokkanto bhacati ca yadā sampajāno satova

Gabbhasmā nikkhamati carime attabhāve tadāpi,

Sambodhiṃ vā purisanisaho bujjhate kampate’yā

Ete dhammā samaṇa mahato bhumicālassa hetu; ()

When the Bodhisatta, mindful and clearly comprehending, descends into his mother's womb; when he emerges from the womb in his final existence; or when the bull among men awakens to perfect enlightenment, this earth trembles. These, O ascetic, are causes of a great earthquake.

5.

5.

Buddho hutvā bhuvananayano dhammacakkaṃ pajānaṃ

Saṃvattetī vijahati yadā cā’yusaṅkhāravegaṃ,

Kampatye’sāpathavi phusate khandhanibbānadhātuṃ

Ānande’te mahatipathavikampanatthāya hetu; ()

When, having become the Buddha, the Eye of the World, he turns the Wheel of Dhamma for all beings; when he relinquishes the force of his life-formation; and when he attains the element of Parinibbāna where the aggregates cease—this earth trembles. Ānanda, these are the causes for the great trembling of the earth.

6. [O 0.0650]

6.

Tabyāsenabbigatahadayā’nandamānandatheraṃ

Assāsetvā uparupari so desanaṃ vaḍḍhayitvā,

Ānandā’haṃ karahacivasiṃ yassa nerañjarāya

Najjā tire jitajalamucassā’japālassa mūle; ()

Having consoled the Elder Ānanda, whose heartfelt joy was overcome by distress, the Blessed One elaborated upon the teaching again and again, saying: 'Ānanda, I once dwelt on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, at the foot of the Ajapāla banyan tree.'

7.

7.

Tatrā’gantvā phusatu bhagavā khandha nibbānadhātuṃ

Issāmāyāmalinahadayo pāpimā iccavoca,

Laddhokāso punarapi kamamaṃ evamevā’bhiyāci

Ajjā’sīnaṃ paramarucire pya’tra cāpālacetye; ()

The Evil One, with a heart stained by envy and deceit, came there and spoke thus: 'May the Blessed One attain the Nibbāna-element of the aggregates.' Having obtained the opportunity again, he importuned me in the very same way today, as I was seated here in the most delightful Cāpāla Shrine.

8.

8.

Apposasukekā tvamiha kalimā hohi māsehi tīhi

Khandhānaṃ nibbuti bhagavato hessatī’ccetamatthaṃ,

Ārocentena hi kasatimatā samapajaññena bhikkhu

Ossaṭṭho me jitanamucinā cā’yusaṅkhāradhammo; ()

'Be untroubled, Māra. In three months the Blessed One's aggregates will be extinguished.' Announcing this matter, mindful and clearly comprehending, I, the conqueror of Namuci, relinquished my life-formation.

9. [O 0.0651]

9.

Evaṃ vutte caraṇakamalacanda mānandathero

Natvā bhante bahujanahitatthāya tiṭṭhā’yukappaṃ,

Vatatikkhattuṃ paramakaruṇācodito yācidāni

Nā’yaṃ kālo bhavati sugataṃ yāvanāyi’cca’voca; ()

When this was said, the Elder Ānanda bowed to the Buddha's moon-like lotus feet and said: 'Venerable Sir, for the welfare and happiness of many, please remain for an aeon!' He pleaded thus three times, prompted by great compassion. But the Buddha replied: 'This is not the time to entreat the Sugata.'

10.

10.

Sambodhiṃ tvaṃ yadi bhagavato saddahanto’si kasmā

Nippīḷesī dasabala manullaṅghanīyā’bhilāpaṃ,

Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sati bhagavatā ka yamāne nimitte

Tumheve’taṃ viya kalimatā dukkatañcā’paraddhaṃ; ()

If you have faith in the enlightenment of the Tathāgata, why then do you vex the Ten-Powered One, whose word is not to be transgressed? When on each occasion a clear hint was being made by the Blessed One, it was you who, as if bewildered, did wrong and offended.

11.

11.

Yāceyyāsi yadi dasabalaṃ ce paṭikkhippa vācā

Satthā’datte tava tatiyakaṃ vippayogo piyehi,

Naṇvā’kkhāto samaṇa paṭigacceva me saṅkhataṃ yaṃ

Jātaṃ bhūtaṃ avipariṇataṃ taṃ kuto’ pe’ttha labbhā; ()

If you had begged the Ten-Powered One, though he might have rejected your words twice, the Teacher would have accepted your third request. O monk, has it not been declared by me from the very beginning that there is separation from all that is dear? That which is born, come into being, and conditioned—how could it possibly be that it should not be subject to change?

12. [O 0.0652]

12.

Ekaṃsenā’vitathavacasā saccasandhena cāyu-

Saṅkhāro’ hīyati bhagavatā vyākatā’nanda bhikkhu,

Yāsā vācā yathariva chiyāmuttakhāṇo tathā taṃ

Paccāgacche napunavacanaṃ jīvitārakkhahetu; ()

With speech that is certain and truthful, and bound by truth, O monk Ānanda, it has been declared by the Blessed One that the life-formation is relinquished. That word, like a broken axle-pin cast away, does not return again, even for the sake of preserving life.

13.

13.

Evaṃ vatvā sapadi sugato gandhanāgindagāmī

Yenāraññaṃ vipulamalakāsāravesāliyaṃ so,

Kūṭāgāraṃ tadavasariyā’nandatherena saddhiṃ

Iccābhāsī samaṇaparisaṃ sannipātehi sīghaṃ; ()

Having spoken thus, the Sugata, majestic as a lordly fragrant elephant, swiftly went to the great forest near Vesālī. There, having entered the Peaked Hall with the Elder Ānanda, he spoke thus: 'Quickly convene the assembly of monks!'

14. [O 0.0653]

14.

Evaṃ bhante lapitavacano sokasallena viddho

Sohā’yasmā vasigaṇa mupaṭṭhānasāḷāya māsuṃ,

Rāsikatvā mahitacaraṇo’pāhano tassa kālaṃ

Ārocesi gamiya bhagavā pīṭhikāyaṃ nisajja; ()

Having said, 'So be it, venerable sir,' that venerable one, pierced by the dart of sorrow, quickly gathered the assembly of monks in the attendance hall. Having approached the Blessed One and paid homage to his honored feet, he announced that it was time. The Blessed One then took his seat.

15.

15.

Āmantetvā samaṇaparisaṃ bodhipakakkhe bhavā me

Yete dhammā sayamadhigatā desitā sādhukaṃ vo,

Uggaṇhitvā yathariva siyā sāsanañcaddhanīyaṃ

Bhāvetabbā suparihariyā sevitabbā’ti vatvā; ()

Having addressed the assembly of monks, he said: 'These doctrines that are factors of enlightenment, realized by myself and well taught to you, should be thoroughly learned, developed, practiced, and cultivated, so that this holy life may long endure.'

16.

16.

Nibbāyissatya’vaca bhagavā accayenā’cirena

Temāsānaṃ bhuvanabhavanu’jjotapajjotarūpo;

Tumhe sampādayatha samaṇā appamādena sabbe

Saṅkhārā yaṃ samudayamayā lakkhaṇabbhāhatā’ti; ()

The Blessed One said: 'Before long, after the passing of three months, he whose form is a lamp illuminating the world-abode will attain final Nibbāna. Strive on with diligence, all you monks! All conditioned things are marked by the characteristic of arising and passing away.'

17. [O 0.0654]

17.

Pubbaṇhe so karakisalayā’dhāna’viṭṭhānapatto

Patto satthā pacuracaraṇo cīvaracchannaganto,

Gattobhāsāruṇitaparikhāvīthipākāracakkaṃ

Cakkaṅkeha’ṅkitapadatalassālivesālināmaṃ; () (Yamakabandhanaṃ)

In the early morning, the Teacher—his body covered by his robe, holding his bowl in hands like tender sprouts, his soles marked with wheel-marks—entered the city named Vesālī, the radiance of his body reddening the complex of moats, avenues, and ramparts.

18.

18.

Āhiṇḍitvā tahi manugharaṃ piṇḍa manvesamāno

Pacchābhattaṃ bhuvananayano locanindīvarehi,

Taṃ vesāliṃ dviradagatimā’nanda nāgāpalokaṃ

Oloketvā ida mavaca me pacchimaṃ dassana’nti; ()

Wandering there from house to house seeking alms, after the meal, the Eye of the World, with eyes like blue lotuses and the gait of an elephant, looked upon that Vesālī with a Nāga-gaze and said to Ānanda: 'This is my last sight of it.'

19. [O 0.0655]

19.

Tambhāṭhānā nayanasubhagaṃ sevito sāvakehi

Bhaṇḍaggāmāṭavi mavasaṭo diṭṭhivādībhasīho,

Nicchāretvā sarasamadhuraṃ dhammagambhīraghosaṃ

Taṇhākhīṇā mamapunabhavo bhikkhave natthya’bhāsi; ()

From that place, pleasing to the eye, attended by his disciples, he, a lion to the elephants that are holders of wrong views, went to the Bhaṇḍa village. And having uttered the deep, sweet, and tasteful sound of the Dhamma, he declared: 'Monks, for me, whose craving is destroyed, there is no further becoming.'

20.

20.

Tisso sikkhā pariharatha vo sādhukaṃ bhikkhave’ti

Evaṃ vatvā matibhagavatibhattubhūto sayambhu,

Tamhāgāmā punarupagamī hatthigāma’mbagāmaṃ

Jambuggāmaṃ vamitagamano hatthivikkantigantā; ()

'Practice well the three trainings, O monks.' Having said this, the Self-Existent One, who is the support of those endowed with wisdom, went forth again from that village to Hatthigāma, Ambagāma, and Jambugāma, journeying on with the powerful stride of an elephant.

21. [O 0.0656]

21.

Patvā bhogāyatana manaso bhoganāmaṃ subhikkhaṃ

Nibbhogo so nagaramaparaṃ bhāratibhatturūpo,

Cittābhogaṃ kurutha samaṇā sādhukaṃtaṃ suṇātha

Desissāmī’tya’vadi caturo vo uḷārāpadese; ()

He who, having attained the mind's sphere of enjoyment, a prosperity named 'bhoga', yet without enjoyment goes to another city in the guise of a supplicant, said: 'Monks, apply your minds and listen carefully. I will teach you the four great references.'

22.

22.

Eso dhammo bhavati vinayo sāsanaṃ satthu cedaṃ

Abbhaññātaṃ vata bhagavato sammukhā me sutanti,

Sakkhīkatvā yadi vadati maṃ bhikkhave koci bhikkhu

Nādatabbaṃ tadadhivacanaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ; ()

If, monks, any bhikkhu, bearing witness, should say: 'This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher's instruction; this I have heard in the presence of the Blessed One,' his statement should neither be accepted nor rejected.

23.

23.

Pakkhittānaṃ mama tipiṭake tappadabyañjanānaṃ

Yaṃyaṃṭhānaṃ avatarati saṃdissate niddhamettha,

Gantabbaṃ vo sugahitamidaṃ bhāsitaṃ bhikkhunoti

If those words and phrases, when set down in my Tipiṭaka, are seen to be in accord with the Dhamma at every point, then you should conclude: 'This statement by the bhikkhu is well-grasped.'

Chaḍḍetabbaṃ kavacanamitaraṃ duggahītanti no ce;()

If not, that statement should be discarded as poorly grasped.

24. [O 0.0657]

24.

Āvāse yo viharati mahābhikkhusaṅgo amutra

Therā bhikkhū tipiṭakadharā theravaṃsaddhajā ye,

Yvābhiññāto paṭibalataro bhikkhu vā sammukhā me

Tesaṃ tesaṃ idamavagataṃ suggahītatti vutte; ()

Whether from a great community of monks dwelling in a monastery with elders who are bearers of the Tipiṭaka and banners of the elders' lineage, or from a single renowned and capable bhikkhu, or from my own presence—if it is said that from them 'this was understood and well-grasped'...

25.

25.

Otāretvā tadapi vinaye satthu suttābhidhamme

Saṃsandantaṃ yadipana paṭiggaṇhitabbaṃkata na noce,

Cattāro me itivibhajite nippadesāpadese

Dhāreyyātha’bruvi muni ranādhānagāhī sadā vo; ()

The Sage, ever averse to conflict, declared to you: 'Having compared that with the Teacher's Vinaya, Sutta, and Abhidhamma, if it harmonizes, it should be accepted; if not, it should not. Thus you should bear in mind these four complete and exhaustive great references.'

26. [O 0.0658]

26.

Patvā pāvāpuravara matho’ropitakkhandhabhāro

Ambāraññe viharati mamaṃ dhammarājāti sutvā,

Tibbacchando javanamatino dassanassādanamhi

Cundo gantvā caraṇakamalaṃ vandi kammāraputto; ()

Having heard that the King of Dhamma, after reaching the excellent city of Pāvā and laying down the burden of the aggregates, was dwelling in the mango grove, Cunda the smith's son, with intense desire and a swift mind for the delight of seeing him, went and worshipped his lotus feet.

27.

27.

Sammādhammassavaṇapasuto ekamantaṃ nisinno

Sotāpanno paṭhamadivase dassanenevasatthu,

Buddhaṃ paññābhagavatipatiṃ svatanāyā’bhiyācaṃ

Cando pubbācalamiva gharaṃ pāvisi cundanāmo; ()

Intent on hearing the true Dhamma, having sat to one side, he became a Stream-enterer on the very first day by the mere sight of the Teacher. Having invited the Buddha, the Lord endowed with wisdom, for the morrow, Cunda by name entered his house like the moon entering the eastern mountain.

28.

28.

Sampādetvāgahapati bahuṃ tāyaratyā’vasāne

Khajjaṃ bhojjaṃ sumadhutaraṃ sūkaraṃ maddavampi,

Pakkhittojaṃ pacuravibhavo ñāpayī dhammarañño

Kālo bhante’tarahi bhagavā niṭṭhitaṃ bhojananti; ()

At the end of that night, the householder, a man of great means, having prepared abundant hard and soft food, very sweet, and also sūkaramaddava infused with nutritive essence, informed the King of Dhamma: 'Venerable sir, it is time. The meal is ready.'

29. [O 0.0659]

29.

Sālakkhandhāyatabhujayugo muggavaṇṇaṃ gahetvā

Pattaṃ pattatthavikapihitaṃ pakkanigrodhavaṇṇaṃ,

Acchādetvā parivutavasi cīvaraṃ paṃsukūlaṃ

Pāsādabbhantara mabhiruhī tassa sovaṇṇavaṇṇo; ()

He of golden hue, whose arms were long like the trunks of sāla trees, having taken his bowl the color of green gram and covered by its stand, and having donned his refuse-rag robe the color of a ripe banyan fruit, surrounded by his retinue of self-controlled ones, ascended into that one's dwelling.

30.

30.

Bālādiccori’va dasabalo tāva pubbācalagge

Paññattasmiṃ ratanakhavite bhaddapīṭhe nisajja,

Āmantetvā jitadhanapatiṃ cundamādiccabandhu

Satthāraṃ tvaṃ parivisiminā maddavenātya’bhāsi; ()

Having reached the prosperous city named Bhoganagara, he who is without worldly enjoyment, the master of speech, said: 'Monks, apply your minds and listen well. I will teach you the four Great References.'

31. [O 0.0660]

31.

Santappetvā sugatapamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sahatthā

Maṃsaṃ sobbhe nikhaṇiya tato satthubhuttāvasesaṃ,

Bhatyā dhammassavaṇanirataṃ bodhayitvāpayāsi

Pūro paṅkeruhamiva jino cundakammāraputtaṃ; ()

If, monks, a certain monk should say: 'This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher's Dispensation; this I have heard and learned in the presence of the Blessed One himself,' that monk's statement should neither be approved nor rejected.

32.

32.

Bāḷhābādho balavakaṭukā vedanā tassa bhattaṃ

Bhuttāvissā’bhavi bhagavato rattapakkhandikā’si,

Vikkhambhetvā tamapi satimā sampajāno’vidūre

Maggotiṇṇo muni rupagamīrukkhamūlaṃ kilanto; ()

Those words and phrases should be laid alongside the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya. If they are found to conform, you may conclude: 'This is indeed the word of the Blessed One; this has been well-grasped by the monk.'

33.

33.

Paññāpetvā catuguṇamupaṭṭhākathero adāsi

Yaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ narahari tahiṃ vissamatto nisajja,

Gantvā’nandā’hara sarabhasaṃ tvaṃ pipāsāturassa

Pānīyyaṃ me nikhiladarathā nibbutassetya’bhāsī; ()

If they do not conform, you may conclude: 'This is not the word of the Blessed One; this has been poorly grasped by the monk,' and you should discard it.

34. [O 0.0661]

34.

Yasmā bhatte sakaṭasatasañcārasambhinnamaggā

Gorūpānaṃ vigaḷitaṭī siṅgasaṅghaṭṭaṇena,

Cakkacchinnā kalalakalusībhutasantattavāri

Nālaṃ pātuṃ salilamadhunā kunnadi sandate’dha; ()

This same principle applies if a monk claims to have heard a teaching from a community of monks with elders in a certain residence, from a number of elder monks, or from a single elder monk.

35.

35.

Accāsanne kakudhaviṭapīmūlasaṃsaṭṭhakulā

Vātakkhittā’malajalakaṇā sātasitodapuṇṇā,

Sakkā bhante savati kakudhāsindhu gattāni sīkiṃ

Kātuṃ pātuṃ dharaṇiramaṇi baddhahārābhirāmā; ()

Having compared that also with the Suttas and Vinaya, if it harmonizes, it should be accepted; if not, it should not. 'These four Great References of mine, thus completely analyzed, you should always bear in mind,' thus spoke the Sage to you, he who takes up no strife.

36. [O 0.0662]

36.

Evaṃ vutte puna bhagavatā codito pattahattho

Patvā’nando kalalavisamaṃ kunnadītitthamāsuṃ,

Netvā sitodaka malulitaṃ nimmalaṃ sandamānaṃ

Ñato bhante pivatu bhagavā’tyā’ha buddhānubhāvo; ()

Then, having reached the excellent city of Pāvā, he who has laid down the burden of the aggregates was dwelling in the mango grove. Hearing, 'The King of Dhamma is here,' Cunda the smith's son, with intense desire and a swift mind for the joy of seeing him, went and worshipped his lotus-like feet.

37.

37.

Tasmiṃkāle samitatasiṇaṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ

Naṃ disvāna’ṅkusanisitadhī pukkuso kamallaputto,

Pabyākāsika paṭutarasamāpattiyākittanena

Āḷārassā’dhikavupasame attano’bhippasādaṃ; ()

Devoted to listening to the true Dhamma and sitting to one side, he became a Stream-enterer on the very first day by the mere sight of the Teacher. Having invited the Buddha, the Lord of Blessed Wisdom, for the following day, Cunda by name entered his house like the moon appearing over the eastern mountain.

38.

38.

Gajjantisvā’sanisu parito niccharantīsu jātu

Vijjummālāsu ca galagalāyantiyā vuṭṭhiyāhaṃ,

Saññibhuto nanu khaphasamāpattiyā santavitto

Nā’ssosiṃ bho sutikaṭuravaṃ nāddasaṃ rūpavāha; ()

At the end of that night, the householder, a man of great means, having prepared in abundance hard and soft foods, very sweet, and also tender pork infused with rich essence, informed the King of Dhamma: 'Venerable sir, it is time; the meal is ready.'

39. [O 0.0663]

39.

Vuttaṃ sutvā’matarasahīraṃ uddharitvāna dhīmā

Saddhābījaṃ panihita kamathā’ḷārakālāmakhette,

Yebhuyyenā’samacupasame siṅgīvaṇṇe pasanno

Datvā buddhaṃ saraṇa magamā sāṭakaṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ; ()

Hearing the words, the nectar-like essence, the wise one, having drawn it forth, established the seed of faith. Though formerly content in the field of Āḷāra Kālāma, he was now greatly pleased with the incomparable peace of the Golden-Hued One. Having given a golden-hued robe, he went to the Buddha for refuge.

40.

40.

Tattaṅgārodaramiva tamaṅgīrasaṅgopanītaṃ

Vatthaṃ vītaccika mabhinavaṃ siṅgivaṇṇaṃ rarāja,

Pacchā paccuttariya kakudhāsindhu majjhogahetvā

Ambāraññaṃ tahi mavatarī sakyasiho sasaṅgho; ()

The new, stainless, golden-hued cloth, brought to the Aṅgīrasa who was like a cauldron of hot coals, shone. Afterwards, having crossed the Kakudhā river, the Lion of the Sakyans, with the Saṅgha, then descended into the mango grove.

41.

41.

Saṅghāṭiṃ patthariya sahasā cundatherena mañce

Paññattasmiṃ sapadi samadhiṭṭhāya vuṭṭhānasaññaṃ,

Accadhāyā’dhikakilamatho so sato sampajañño

Pāde pādaṃ bhavabhayabhido sīhaseyyaṃ akāsi; ()

The saṅghāṭi having been spread hastily by the elder Cunda on the prepared bed, the breaker of the fear of becoming at once resolved upon the perception of rising. Then, mindful and fully aware, having overcome extreme weariness, he assumed the lion's posture, placing one foot upon the other.

42. [O 0.0664]

42.

Āmantetvā niravadhidayo thera mānandanāmaṃ

Dve me laddhā samasamaphalā piṇḍapātā visiṭṭhā,

Sandeho yo karabhavi siyā cundakammāraputta-

Sse’vaṃ vatvā pariharatu tañcāha me accayena; ()

He of boundless compassion, having addressed the elder named Ānanda, said: 'Two alms-offerings I have received are of equal result and pre-eminent. Should any remorse arise for Cunda the smith's son, you are to dispel it by speaking thus after my passing.'

43.

43.

Tamhā khīṇāsavaparivuto bhuripañño hirañña-

Vatyā najjā vijanapavanaṃ pārime tirabhāge,

Phullaṃ sālabbana mavasarī kosiṇārāna maggaṃ

Mallānaṃ so suravanasiriṃ rājadhānyā’vidūre; ()

From there, he of great wisdom, surrounded by those with extinguished outflows, descended into the blossoming Sāl-grove of the Mallas, a place of divine beauty on the far bank of the Hiraññavatī river, on the road to Kusinārā, not far from their capital.

44. [O 0.0665]

44.

Ānandenā’ nadhivaravaco coditeno’ pacāre

Paññantasmiṃ tathaṇayamakassālarukkhantarāḷe

Mañce paññāsatiparimukho uttarādhānasīse

Katvā pādoparipada manuṭṭhānaseyyaṃakāso ()

Urged by the Teacher's unsurpassed words, on a bed prepared by Ānanda in the space between the twin sāla trees, the Blessed One, with his head to the north, placed one foot upon the other and assumed the posture from which he would not rise again, with mindfulness established before him.

45.

45.

Sitacchāyā vigaḷitarajodhūsarā sabbaphāli-

Phullā bhantī jaṭitaviṭapakkhandhamūlā’ ññamaññaṃ,

Saṅkiṇṇālī sapadi yamakassālasālā visālā

Dissante’vaṃ vakulatilakā’sokacampeyyasākhī; ()

With cool shade, free from dust and pollen, all in full bloom and shining, their matted branches, trunks, and roots intertwined—thus appeared the vast twin sāla trees. Crowded together, the branches of the bakula, tilaka, asoka, and campaka trees were also seen.

46.

46.

Naccaṃ gītaṃ vividhaturiyaṃ vattate’dāni dibbaṃ

Dibbaṃ cuṇṇaṃ malayajamayaṃ dibbamandāravāni,

Passā’nandabbikacayamakassālapupphānya’kāle

Samūjāye’vahi bhagavato antalikkhā patanti; ()

See, Ānanda! Now divine dancing, singing, and various musical instruments are taking place. Divine sandalwood powder, divine mandārava flowers, and the flowers of the twin sāla trees, blossoming out of season, fall from the sky for the veneration of the Blessed One.

47. [O 0.0666]

47.

Ete brahmāmaranaraphaṇī cāmaracchattahatthā

Mālāmālāguḷaparimalaṇḍupadīpaddhajehi,

Channaṃ tāḷāvacarabhajitaṃ maṅgalāgārabhutaṃ

Jātikkhettaṃ nanu bhagavato kevalaṃ pūjanāya; ()

These Brahmās, devas, humans, and nāgas, with whisks and parasols in hand, honor him with garlands, perfumed powders, lamps, and banners. Resounding with music, having become a house of auspiciousness, is not this sacred site of the Blessed One indeed solely for worship?

48.

48.

Ānande’vaṃ satipi bhagavā tāvatā sakkatovā

Sammā tesaṃ nacagarukato namānito pūjitovā,

Yo kho dhammaṃ carati samaṇo’ pāsako vā’nudhammaṃ

Bhatyā so maṃ paramavidhānā kamānaye pūjayeti; ()

Ānanda, even so, the Blessed One is not thereby truly honored, respected, venerated, or worshipped. Whoever, whether a monk or a lay follower, lives in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing rightly, that one honors, respects, and venerates me with the highest form of worship.

49. [O 0.0667]

49.

Amhe tasmātiha paṭipadaṃ suṭṭhu dhammānudhammaṃ

Sampādemā’tya’vaca muni vo sikkhitabbañhi evaṃ,

Dhammāssāmiṃ sapadi purato vījamāno samāno

Hatthicchāpo yathariva ṭhīto theranāgo’pavāno; ()

Therefore, the Sage declared: 'We should practice well, in accordance with the Dhamma. Indeed, you must train yourselves in this way.' At that moment, the elder Upavāna stood fanning the Lord of Dhamma from the front, just like a young elephant.

50.

50.

Mallānaṃ kho nagaravarato yāvatā sāladāyaṃ

Rāsibhūtā’surasuravarabrahmarājūhi yasmā,

Daṭṭhuṃ buddhaṃ dasabaladharaṃ khittavālaggakoṭi-

Mattaṭṭhāne dasadasahi vā natthya’phuṭṭhappadeso; ()

From the excellent city of the Mallas all the way to the sāla grove, asuras, excellent devas, and Brahmā kings were gathered in heaps to see the Buddha, the possessor of the ten powers; because of this, there was no place untouched, not even for the space of a hair's breadth.

51.

51.

Kandantīnaṃ pakiriya sake kesapāse ca bāhā

Paggaṇahitvā sirasi pathavisaññinīdevatānaṃ,

Jhāyantīnaṃ bhuviparipatantīna mujjhāyinīnaṃ

Dento’kāsaṃ apanayi parañceḷhakeno’pavānaṃ; ()

Of the earth-deities who were weeping, scattering their tresses, raising their arms to their heads, lamenting, falling upon the ground, and complaining—to give them space, the Blessed One had the elder Upavāna moved aside.

52. [O 0.0668]

52.

Saṅkhārānaṃ khayavaya manāgāmino vītarāgā

Devabrahmā sumariya yathevi’ndakhīlācalaṭṭhā,

Nāmhe bhante’tarahī viya vo accayenātya’vocuṃ

Passissāmā’yati miga manobhāvanīyepi bhikkhū; ()

The devas and Brahmās who were non-returners, free from passion, stood firm and unmoving like Indra's pillar, reflecting on the destruction and passing away of all formations. They said: 'Venerable Sirs, we are not like the others at the time of your passing.'

53.

53.

Jātaṭṭhānappabhutika midhānandaṭhānaṃ catukkaṃ

Puññakkhettaṃ bhuvi bhagavato sabbhisaṃvejaniyaṃ,

Addhā saddhāvisadahadayā sādhavo cārikāyaṃ

Āhiṇḍantā pavurakusalaṃ tatrapatvā viṇanti; ()

Ānanda, these four places—the birthplace, the place of enlightenment, the place of the first turning of the wheel of Dhamma, and the place of final Nibbāna—are fields of merit of the Blessed One in the world, inspiring reverence in the virtuous. Indeed, the faithful with clear hearts, virtuous ones wandering on pilgrimage, having arrived there, accumulate excellent merit.

9 54. [O 0.0669]

9 54.

Puṭṭhassevaṃ kathamapi mayaṃ mātugāmesu bhante

Vattissāmā’tyamitamatimā’ nandatherassa’bhāsi,

Tannijjhānaṃ tadabhilapanaṃ mākarothāti tumhe

Evaṃsante satiparimukhā hotha chadvārarakkhā; ()

When asked by the elder Ānanda, 'Venerable Sir, how are we to conduct ourselves with regard to women?', the one of boundless wisdom replied: 'Do not gaze at them, do not converse with them. This being so, establish mindfulness and be guardians of the six sense-doors.'

55.

55.

Puṭṭhassevaṃ maya mutusamuṭṭhānarūpāvasiṭṭhe

Vatteyyāmhe tavanirupame rūpakāye kathannu,

Mākho tumhe bhavatha munino dehapūjāvidhāne

Sakhyāpārā upari ghaṭathā’hā’savānaṃ khayeti; ()

When asked, 'How should we conduct ourselves towards your incomparable physical body, this remaining form?' the Sage replied: 'Do not be occupied with the rites of honoring the Sage's body. Friends, you should strive for the ultimate goal, the destruction of the outflows.'

56.

56.

Saṃvijjante bhagavati idhānanda bhīyyopasannā

Rūpībrahmāmarapabhutayo khattiyabrāhmaṇā ye,

Sakkaccaṃ te yathariva janā cakkavattissarīre

Sabyāpārā naraharisariropahāre siyunti; ()

Ānanda, there are many devoted khattiyas, brahmins, Rūpa Brahmās, devas, and others here. They will diligently and reverently attend to the rites for the body of the Lion of Men, just as people do for the body of a wheel-turning monarch.

57. [O 0.0670]

57.

Cattāro me bahujanahitā buddhapaccekabuddhā

Yasmā maggapphalasukhamudā sāvakā cakkavattī,

Rājā pūjāvidhisumahiyā honti thūpārahe’va

Tasmā thūpo mamapi bhavatā’nandasiṅghāṭakamhi; ()

Four are for the welfare of many and worthy of a stūpa to be greatly honored with offerings: Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, disciples rejoicing in the bliss of path and fruit, and wheel-turning monarchs. Therefore, Ānanda, a stūpa for me should also be made at a crossroads.

58.

58.

Evaṃ vutte sariya tamurotomaribhūtasoko

Therānando pavisiya nirālambadhammo vihāraṃ,

Ālambitvā vilapiya bahuṃ aggalatthambhasīse

Satthā sekhe kaḷitakaruṇāpāṅgabhaṅgo parodi; ()

When this was said, the elder Ānanda, his sorrow like a spear in his breast, feeling unsupported, entered the monastery. Leaning against the crossbar of the door, he wept profusely. The Teacher, casting a compassionate glance upon the trainee, called out to him.

59. [O 0.0671]

59.

Āmantetvā tamanadhivaro puñchamakānassudhāraṃ

Theraṃ mākhovilapi ala mānanda māsoci hevaṃ,

Saṅkhārānaṃ kathamiha labhe niccataṃ nibbikāraṃ

Akkhātaṃ me nanu piyajanabbippayogo siyāti; ()

The Unsurpassed One, calling to the elder who was wiping away his stream of tears, said: 'Enough, Ānanda, do not weep, do not grieve thus. How, in this world, could permanence or an unchanging nature be found in conditioned things? Has it not been declared by me that there must be separation from all that is dear and beloved?'

60.

60.

Mettāpubbena hi cirataraṃ kāyakammena vācā-

Kammenā’yaṃ guṇamaṇimanokammunā bhikkhave maṃ;

Sakkaccaṃ sannicitakusalopaccupaṭṭhāsi tasmā

Ātāpī so tvamasi nipapako hesi khīṇāsavoti; ()

Indeed, for a long time, with loving-kindness as the foremost, by bodily action, by verbal action, and by mental action, O monks, this Ānanda, this jewel of virtue, attended to me carefully, having accumulated merit. Therefore, you are ardent, you are faultless, you will be one with destroyed taints.

61. [O 0.0672]

61.

Chāyāmaññe cira manucaraṃ seyyathā’nandabhikkhū-

Paṭṭhāko me bhavati sutavā nāgatātitakānaṃ,

Sambuddhānaṃ bhagavata mupaṭṭhāyakā ce’tadaggā

Iccā’he’tapparamasamaṇāyeva hessantya’hesuṃ; ()

Just as the learned monk Ānanda has been my attendant, following me for a long time like a shadow, so too were the attendants of the Blessed Buddhas of the past, and so will be for those of the future, the foremost among them. Thus he said: 'Indeed, they were and will be the foremost among ascetics.'

62.

62.

Saṃvaṇṇesi niravadhiguṇo ukkhipanto’va meruṃ

Saṅkhobhento viya jalanidhiṃ pattharanto’va bhumiṃ,

Vitthārento viya ravipathaṃ saṅghamajjhe ṭhitassa

Ānandassu’ttaritaraguṇaṃ abbhutaccherabhūtaṃ; ()

He of boundless virtues praised the wondrous and marvelous, ever-increasing virtues of Ānanda, who stood in the midst of the Saṅgha—praising as if lifting Mount Meru, as if stirring the ocean, as if spreading out the earth, as if expanding the path of the sun.

63.

63.

Hitvā sākhānagara manalaṃjaṅgalaṃ issarānaṃ

Vāsaṭṭhānaṃ taditarapuraṃ sabbasampattisāraṃ,

Patvā rājaggahapabhutikaṃ nātha nibbāyatūti

Evaṃ vutte muni ravaca māhevamānandavoca; ()

'Lord, may the Blessed One not attain final Nibbāna in this wattle-and-daub town, this town in the middle of the jungle, this branch-town! Let the Lord attain final Nibbāna in another great city, a dwelling place of the powerful, the essence of all prosperity, such as Rājagaha!' When this was said, the Sage replied: 'Ānanda, do not say so!'

64. [O 0.0673]

64.

Pubbe dibbopamasukha vidhā’nanda’haṃ cakkavatti-

Rājā hutvā cira manubhaviṃ dhammiko dhammarājā,

Mallānaṃ kho tadahani kusāvatya’yaṃ rājadhāni

Āsi lakkhivasati ralakārājadhānī’va phītā; ()

Formerly, I, Ānanda, having been a wheel-turning king, a righteous king, a king of righteousness, enjoyed divine-like happiness for a long time. Indeed, at that time, this Kusāvatī was the royal capital of the Mallās, like Alakā, a dwelling place of fortune, flourishing and prosperous.

65.

65.

Gāmakkhette jitaripuraṇo kosiṇārāna masmiṃ

Sālāraññe jinakarivaro mārakaṇṭhiravena,

Yāme ajjāhani rajaniyā pacchime haññate’ti

Vāseṭṭhānaṃ pahiṇi yatimārocanatthaṃ tamatthaṃ; ()

In this Sāl-grove of the Kusinārā Mallas, in this village territory, the Victor over enemy cities, the foremost elephant among conquerors, declared with a voice like a lion to Māra: 'In the last watch of this very night, the final passing will occur.' The Sage then sent a messenger to the Vāseṭṭhas to inform them of this matter.

66. [O 0.0674]

66.

Santhāgāre mahatiparisā kiñcikammaṃ paṭicca

Rāsibhūtā yativaravacocoditā mucchitāsi,

Uyyānaṃ te pavisiya tadā mallaputtā ca mallā

Vyāpajjiṃsū kasiranikarāvārapāre nimuggā; ()

In the assembly hall, a great gathering, having assembled concerning some matter, was urged by the words of the noble ascetic and swooned. Then, having entered the park, the Malla princes and the Mallas were overcome, submerged in the shoreless ocean of a mass of misery.

67.

67.

Yaṃnūnāhaṃ narapatikulaṃ ekamekaṃ gahetvā

Vandāpeyyaṃ caraṇakamaladvanda maṅgīrasassa,

Iccānando yati sapariso puttadārehisaddhiṃ

Itthannāmo paṇamati jinaṃ mallarājāti vatvā; ()

'What if I were to take each royal family one by one and have them pay homage to the pair of lotus feet of the Angirasa?' Thus Ānanda, the ascetic, had them pay homage, saying: 'A Malla ruler of such-and-such a name, with his retinue, together with his sons and wives, bows to the Jina.'

68.

68.

Mallānañcāhariya paṭhameyeva yāme rajanyā

Vandāpesi sakalaparisaṃ tenupāyena buddhaṃ,

Sutvā vidvā bhagavata manuṭṭhānaseyyappavattiṃ

Sāḷāraññaṃ avasari paribbājako yo subhaddo; ()

And having brought the Mallas, in the very first watch of the night, he had the entire assembly pay homage to the Buddha by that means. Having heard the news of the Blessed One’s final reclining, the wise wanderer Subhadda approached the Sāla grove.

69. [O 0.0675]

69.

Okāsaṃ me dadatha samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pucchanāya

Kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajahitu midhānandapatto hamasmi,

Vutte satthā kilamati alaṃhāvuso mā vihaññi

Vatvā’nando bhagavati dayācodito vārayī taṃ; ()

'Grant me an opportunity to question the ascetic Gotama. I have come here, Ānanda, to abandon a matter of doubt.' Ānanda replied, 'Enough, friend, do not trouble the Teacher; the Blessed One is weary.' Having said this, urged by compassion for the Blessed One, Ānanda prevented him.

70.

70.

Laddhokāso dasabaladayājālabaddho subhaddo

Aññāpekho pavisiya tahiṃ tabbihesānapekkho,

Pañhaṃ pucchi tadupanayane kovido’bhāsidhammaṃ

Vitthārento ariyavinaye puggale suppatiṭṭhe; ()

Having obtained the opportunity, Subhadda, bound by the net of compassion of the Ten-Powered One, seeking higher knowledge and disregarding the trouble, entered there. Skilled in its presentation, he asked a question. The Teacher then spoke the Dhamma, expounding in detail on persons well-established in the noble discipline.

71. [O 0.0676]

71.

Pabbajjitvā bhagavati sayaṃ bhikkhubhāvābhisitto

Saṅkhārānaṃ khayavaya matho bhāvayitvā subhaddo,

Viddhaṃsetvā sakalakalusaṃ satthupaccakkhabhuto

Unnādetvā parisamarahaṃ pacchimosāvakosi; ()

Having gone forth under the Blessed One, Subhadda was himself consecrated into the state of a bhikkhu. Then, having cultivated the destruction and passing away of formations and having shattered all defilements in the very presence of the Teacher, he became an Arahant, the last disciple, causing the assembly to resound.

72.

72.

Paññatto yo bhavati vinayo desito yoca dhammo

So vo satthā paramasaraṇo’tyā’ha me accayena,

There bhikkhū taditaravasī gāravaṃ voharantu

Bhante vatvā pariharatha vo sādarāsappatissā; ()

'The Discipline that has been laid down and the Dhamma that has been taught, that will be your Teacher and supreme refuge after my passing,' he said. 'O bhikkhus, let there be mutual respect among you. Saying "Bhante," you should conduct yourselves with reverence and deference.'

73.

73.

Paccakkho no bhavi dasabalo pucchituṃ sammukhā taṃ

Nāsakkhimhā mayamidamitī māhuvatthānutāpā,

Mutte tuṇhībhavi vasigaṇokiñci buddhecadhamme

Saṅghe magge vimati yadivo bhikkhave pucchathāti; ()

'Lest you have remorse later, thinking: "The Teacher was present before us, yet we were not able to question the Ten-Powered One face to face." O bhikkhus, if you have any doubt concerning the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, or the Path, ask now!' When this was said, the assembly of self-controlled ones remained silent.

74. [O 0.0677]

74.

Yasmā khandhe pajahati jino bhikkhave bhandadāni

Āmantemī niyatabhadurā sabbasaṅkhāradhammā,

Sampādethā’tya’mitamatimā appamādena tumhe

Pabyākāsi bhagavata mayaṃ pacchimāhotivācā; ()

'Now indeed, O bhikkhus, I exhort you: all conditioned phenomena are subject to decay. Strive on with diligence!' Thus declared the Blessed One, he of immeasurable wisdom. This was his final utterance.

75.

75.

Rūpārūpāvacarakiriyajjhānasaññānirodha-

Saṅkhātā yā navavidhasamāpattiyo tā’nulomaṃ,

Nissīmamhonidhinibhaguṇo mārasaṅgāmasūro

Buddho nārāyanabaladharo so samāpajji tāva; ()

Then the Buddha—hero in the battle with Māra, wielder of the strength of Nārāyaṇa, whose virtues are like the boundless ocean—entered in forward order the ninefold attainments: the jhānas of the form and formless spheres, and the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.

76. [O 0.0678]

76.

Taṃ taṃ jhānaṃ muni paṭisamāpajjamāno nirodhā

Sammā paccuṭṭhahiya paṭhamajjhānavosāna māpa,

Taṃ taṃ jhānaṃ punaranusamāpajjamāno catuttha-

Rūpajjhānu’ṭṭhahiya vigatāsesasaṅkhāradhammo; ()

The Sage, emerging from the attainment of cessation and entering each jhāna in reverse order, came down to the first jhāna. Then, entering each jhāna again in forward order and emerging from the fourth form-jhāna, all his conditioned phenomena ceased.

77.

77.

Snehaparikkhayajāto

Pajjoto viya tilokamaṇipajjoto,

Buddhonirupadhisesa-

Parinibbutiyā sayambhu parinibbāyi; ()

Just as a lamp is extinguished from the exhaustion of its fuel, so the Buddha, the jewel-lamp of the three worlds, the Self-Awakened One, was utterly extinguished with the Nibbāna-element that is without remaining substrate.

78. [O 0.0679]

78.

Sampati devamanussa-

Pajāya saddhiṃ parodamānāya bhusaṃ,

Sokeni’va saṅkampi

Sahassarāvena’yaṃ mahāpathavī; ()

At that moment, as the populace of devas and humans wept exceedingly, this great earth trembled with a thousand roars, as if overcome with grief.

79.

79.

Vipphuritavijjurāji-

Daṇḍāhatameghadundubhīphalitā’suṃ,

Kadalivanaṃ viya nāgo

Nippīḷesi asesalokaṃ soko; ()

Streaks of lightning flashed, the cloud-drums thundered as if struck, and rain burst forth. Like an elephant crushing a banana grove, grief oppressed the entire world without remainder.

80.

80.

Jātikkhettaṃ khettaṃ

Viya sambādhaṃ chaṇehi tesaṃtesaṃ,

Vijanokāsā’ kāsā

Loke maṅgalanimittajātaṃ jātaṃ; () (Yamakabandhanaṃ)

The field of birth is like a field crowded with their festivals; lonely places became open space. In the world, a host of auspicious signs arose.

Itimedhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadānanidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santike nidāne tathāgata parinibbānappavatti paridīpo ekūnatiṃsatimo saggo.

Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, the illumination of the events of the Tathāgata’s Parinibbāna, in the Proximate Section of the Jinavaṃsadīpa—a source of delight to the hearts of all poets—composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda.

Parinibbute [O 0.0681] bhagavati sahaparinibbānā brahmāsahampati imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi.

When the Blessed One attained Parinibbāna, at that very moment Brahmā Sahampati uttered this verse.

Sabbevanikkhipissanti bhūtā loke samussayaṃ

Yathā etādiso satthā loke appavipuggalo,

Tathāgato balappatto sambuddho parinibbutoti;

All beings in the world will surely lay down the body, when even such a Teacher, a person without peer in the world, the Tathāgata, endowed with the powers, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has attained Parinibbāna.

Parinibbute bhagavati sahaparinibbānāsakko devānamindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi.

When the Blessed One attained Parinibbāna, at that very moment Sakka, lord of the devas, uttered this verse.

Aniccā vatasaṅkārā uppāda vayadhammino,

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti tesaṃvūpasamo sukhoti;

Impermanent, indeed, are conditioned things, their nature is to arise and pass away. Having arisen, they cease; their stilling is bliss.

Parinibbute bhagavati sahaparinibbānā āyasmā anuruddho imā gāthāyo abhāsi.

When the Blessed One attained Parinibbāna, at that very moment the Venerable Anuruddha uttered these verses.

Nāhuassāsapassāso ṭhita cittassa tādito

Anejāsanti mārabbha sokālamakarī muni,

Asallīnena cittena vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi

Pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ vimokkho cetaso ahūhi;

There was no more in-breathing or out-breathing for him of steadfast mind. The sage, unshakable, intent on peace, made his end. With a mind unshrinking he endured all feelings; like the extinguishing of a lamp was the liberation of his heart.

Parinibbute bhagavati sahaparinibbānā āyasmā ānando imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi.

When the Blessed One attained Parinibbāna, at that very moment the Venerable Ānanda uttered this verse.

Tadāsiyaṃ hiṃsanakaṃ tadāsilomahaṃsanaṃ,

Sabbākāravarūpete sambuddhe parinibbuteti;

Then there was terror, then there was hair-raising awe, when the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with all the foremost qualities, attained Parinibbāna.

1.

1.

Lokattayekanayanomunikhippameva

Paggayhamuddhanibhuje parinibbutoti,

Kandiṃsu tāva vilapiṃsu vivaṭṭayiṃsu

Āvaṭṭayiṃsu papatiṃsu mavītarāgī; ()

When the Sage, the one eye for the three worlds, attained Parinibbāna, those not yet free from passion wept and lamented. Raising their arms to their heads, they rolled back and forth and fell to the ground.

2. [O 0.0682]

2.

Assāsayaṃ vasigaṇaṃ samalaṃ sasokaṃ

Ratyāvasesa matha dhammakathāya thero,

Taṃ vītināmayi niruddhatamo’nuruddho

Ānandatherasuhado hadayaṅgamāya; ()

Then the Elder Anuruddha, for whom darkness was dispelled, comforted the sorrowful, tear-stained assembly of self-controlled ones, and passed the remainder of the night with a heart-captivating Dhamma talk for his friend, the Elder Ānanda.

3.

3.

Mallāna magganagaraṃ kusiṇāra middhaṃ

Ārocanāya parinibbutabhāva massa,

Ānandathera maniruddhayaso sarīro

Pāhesi attadutiyaṃ anuruddhathero; ()

Then the Elder Anuruddha, of unimpeded fame, sent the Elder Ānanda with a companion to the prosperous city of Kusinārā, the chief city of the Mallas, to announce the fact of the Blessed One's Parinibbāna.

4.

4.

Mallā tadatthapasutā samayena tena

Yatrā’bhisannipatitā patimattayanti,

Theropana’ttadutiyo tamupecca santhā-

Gāraṃ tamattha mabhivedayi sokadīno; ()

At that time, the Mallas were assembled in the council hall, deliberating on that very matter. The Elder, with his companion, approached that assembly hall and, afflicted with sorrow, announced the news.

5. [O 0.0683]

5.

Therassa tassa suniyamakma samallaputtā

Mallā samallasuṇisā bhuvika mallachāyā,

Kandiṃsu tāva papatiṃsu pariddaviṃsu

Dhammillavellitabhujā’hatasokasallā; ()

Hearing the words of that Elder, the Mallas, with their sons, their daughters-in-law, and their young women, being struck by the dart of sorrow, wept, fell down, and lamented, with dishevelled hair and flailing arms.

6.

6.

Nānāvidhāni turiyāni sugandhamālaṃ

Ādāya pañcasatadussayugāni mallā,

Yenā’si tassasugatassu’tujaṃ sarīraṃ

Taṃ sāḷadāya mupavattana mosariṃsu; ()

Taking various kinds of musical instruments, fragrant garlands, and five hundred pairs of cloths, the Mallas proceeded to the Upavattana Sāla grove, where the physical body of the Sugata lay.

7.

7.

Te gandhadhūpakusumehi ca naccagīta-

Vajjehi chattamaṇivijanicāmarehi,

Celabbitāna navamaṇḍalamāḷakādiṃ

Katvāna chāhamakariṃsu sarīrapūjaṃ; ()

With perfumes, incense, and flowers, with dance, song, and music, with parasols, jeweled fans, and yak-tail whisks, having made a new pavilion with awnings, decorated platforms, and so forth, they performed homage to the body for six days.

8. [O 0.0684]

8.

Pamokkhamallapurisā’ṭṭhanahātasīsā

Gandhodakena sunivatthasupārutattā,

Muttāmaṇīhi khacitāya tathāgatassa

Gattaṃ suvaṇṇasivikāya niropitaṃ taṃ; ()

Eight foremost Malla men, with bathed heads, anointed with fragrant water, well-clothed and well-covered, placed that body of the Tathāgata upon a golden palanquin inlaid with pearls and gems.

9.

9.

Cāletu mappamapi sattamavāsaramhi

Pucchiṃsu thera manuruddha masayha kinti,

So dibbacakkhumatiyā’mitadevatānaṃ

Pabyākari parivitakka mavecca thero; ()

On the seventh day, being unable to move it even slightly, they asked the Elder Anuruddha, 'Why is this so difficult?' That Elder, having understood with the wisdom of his divine eye the intention of the innumerable deities, explained their deliberation.

10.

10.

Nissesamānusikadibbamahāmahehi

Taṃviggahaṃ bhagavato’bhimahīyamānaṃ,

Ukkhippa tāsamanuvattakamakallabhūpā

Gantvāna uttaradisāya purassu’dīciṃ; ()

While that body of the Blessed One was being honored with all human and divine great honors, the prompt kings, following the will of the deities, lifted it up and, proceeding by the northern direction, went to the east of the city.

11. [O 0.0685]

11.

Majjhenamajjha kamahinībharu muttarena

Dvārena tassanagarassa pavesayitvā,

Sutvāna bandhulapajāpatimallikā taṃ

Dvāre ṭhitā’thanavakovidhānabbayāya; ()

Having made it enter that city by the northern gate and proceed through the very middle, then Mallikā, the wife of Bandhula, having heard of it, stood at the gate, skilled in new forms of lamentation.

12.

12.

Dhotāya gandhasalilena mahālatābya-

Bhusāya sattaratanehi samujjalāya,

Aṅgīrasassa satapuññavīlāsacittaṃ

Chādesi gatta matulaṃ kaḷitāvakāsā; ()

She covered the incomparable body of Aṅgīrasa with the Mahālatā adornment—which was washed with fragrant water, radiant with the seven kinds of gems, and exquisitely depicted a display of a hundred merits—leaving no space uncovered.

13.

13.

Mallāna magganagarassa puratthimāyaṃ

Saṃvijjate makuṭabandhanacetiyaṃ yaṃ,

Dehaṃ tilokasaraṇassa puratthimena

Dvārena nikkhamiya tatra samappayiṃsu; ()

To the east of the Mallas' capital city, there is the cetiya named Makuṭabandhana. Having carried the body of the refuge of the three worlds out through the eastern gate, they laid it there.

14. [O 0.0686]

14.

Sā yāvasandhisamalā nagarī tadāni

Mandāravehi pihitā’bhavi channumattaṃ,

Pucchiṃsu satthu paṭipajjana mattabhāve

Ānandathera matha bhumibhujā kathanti; ()

Then that city, even to its very drains, was covered knee-deep with Mandārava flowers. The rulers then asked the Elder Ānanda how they should proceed with regard to the Teacher's body, and he told them.

15.

15.

Dehe yatheva paṭipajjati cakkavatti-

Rañño tatheva paṭipajjatha buddhadehe,

Iccāha so bhagavato’tujarūpakāyaṃ

Te veṭhayuṃ ahatakāsikasāṭakehi; ()

'As one treats the body of a wheel-turning king, so you should treat the body of the Buddha.' Thus he said. They wrapped the Blessed One's body, whose form was beyond decay, in new Kāsī cloths.

16.

16.

Kappāsapaṭṭavihatehipi veṭhayiṃsu

Katvāna pañcasatadussayugehi evaṃ,

Pakkhippa telaparipuṇṇasuvaṇṇadoṇyā

Aññā’yasāya paṭikujjiya doṇiyā te; ()

They also wrapped it with teased cotton wool, and having done so with five hundred pairs of cloths, they placed it in a golden trough filled with oil and covered it with another trough made of iron.

17. [O 0.0687]

17.

Gattaṃ jinassa citakaṃ katacittakammaṃ

Mālālatāvilasitaṃ satahatthamuccaṃ,

Vīsādhikaṃ agarucandanadāruka puṇṇaṃ

Āropayiṃsu siriyā jitavejayantaṃ; ()

They placed the Victor's body upon a pyre, which was adorned with artistry, embellished with garlands and vines, a hundred cubits high, filled with wood of aloe and sandalwood, and which in its splendor surpassed Vejayanta.

18.

18.

Pāvāya mallanagaraṃ kusiṇāranāmaṃ

Gantā mahāpabhutikassapatheranāgo,

Bhikkhūhi pañcasatikehi pathokkamitvā

Rukkhassa mūla mupagamma khaṇaṃ nisīdi; ()

The great and powerful Elder Kassapa, a true nāga, traveling from Pāvā to the Malla city named Kusinārā with five hundred monks, stepped aside from the path, approached the foot of a tree, and sat down for a moment.

19.

19.

Addhānamagga mathakho paṭipajji tamhā

Mandāravaṃ kusuma maññataro gahetvā,

Ājīvako ta mahipassiya kassapākhyo

Jānāsi gotama manantajinantyapucchi; ()

Then a certain Ājīvaka, holding a Mandārava flower, was traveling along the high road from that place. Seeing him, the one named Kassapa asked, 'Do you know of Gotama, the infinite Victor?'

20. [O 0.0688]

20.

Āmāvuso bhagavato parinibbutassa

Hontya’jja santadivasāti tatomayedaṃ,

Mandāravaṃ kusuma māharitanti vutte

Kandiṃsu keci vilapiṃsu avītarāgā; ()

'Yes, friend, today is the seventh day since the Blessed One's Parinibbāna. That is why I have brought this Mandārava flower.' When this was said, some of those not freed from passion wept and lamented.

21.

21.

Tāya’cchi bhikkhuparisāya subhaddabuḍḍha-

Pabbajjito sapadi satthari baddhavero,

Yo dubbaco yati mahāsamaṇena tena

Muttā mayaṃhi yadupaddutakāyavācā; ()

In that assembly of monks was one Subhadda, who had gone forth in old age and who harbored enmity toward the Teacher. He at once said, 'We are freed from that great ascetic, by whom we were oppressed in body and speech.'

22.

22.

Icchāma yaṃja maya midānikaroma taṃyaṃ

Necchāma’dāni nakaroma mayaṃ tatomā,

Sovittha mācavilapittha’ lamāvusoti

Vatvā pahāra madadī jinadhammacakke; ()

'Now we shall do what we desire, and what we do not desire, we shall not do. Therefore, friends, enough! Do not grieve, do not lament!' Having said this, he struck a blow against the Victor's Wheel of Dhamma.

23. [O 0.0689]

23.

Mallā narindamakuṭaṅakkitapādapīṭhā’-

Limpetu massa caturo cita mappasayha,

Pucchiṃsu thera manuruddha mi’tabruvi so

Patte’dha pajjalati kassapatherasīhe; ()

Four Malla chieftains, whose footstools were marked by the crowns of kings, being unable to light the pyre, asked the Elder Anuruddha. He replied, 'It will ignite only when the lion-like Elder Kassapa has arrived here.'

24.

24.

Dhammāgadena hatasokahadehi yena

Bhikkhūhi satthucitako vasikassapavho,

Teno’pasaṅkami subhaddakathaṃ sasīse

Sukkhāsanī’vu’rasi satti’va maññamāno; ()

That master, the one named Kassapa, by whom the sorrow in the hearts of the monks was dispelled with the medicine of the Dhamma, approached the Teacher's pyre, regarding the words of Subhadda as a dry thunderbolt upon his head or a spear in his chest.

25.

25.

Katvā padakkhiṇa madhiṭṭhahi so catuttha-

Jjhānuṭṭhito bhagavato citakaṃ tivāraṃ,

Baddhañjalī sirasi theravarassa bhetvā

Taṃ supakpatiṭṭhitapadāni patiṭṭhahiṃsu; ()

Having arisen from the fourth jhāna, he circumambulated the Blessed One's pyre three times and made a determination. For that foremost elder with hands joined in reverence at his head, the pyre split open, and the well-established feet of the Buddha appeared.

26. [O 0.0690]

26.

Therāsahassa karatāmarasehi satthu

Pādaṃsumāli vihitāhinipaccakāro,

Omujji gandhavitakāparasāgaramhi

Lokoca tappabhava sokaghanandhakāre; ()

A thousand elders, with hands like lotuses, paid great homage to the Teacher's radiant feet. And the world was immersed in an ocean of sublime thoughts, and in the dense darkness of sorrow born from that event.

27.

27.

Therenacāhinamite citako samantā

Sampajjalittha sayamevu’tujattabhāve,

Daḍḍhe jinassa masivā napichārikāsi

Sārīrikaṭṭhīvisaro’bhayathāvasiṭṭho; ()

When the Elder had paid homage, the pyre blazed up by itself on all sides, by its own inherent nature. When the Conqueror's body was burnt, there was neither soot nor ash; only the collection of bodily relics remained, of two kinds.

28.

28.

Satteva nābhivakiriṃsu lalāṭagīvā

Dhātvakkhakaṭṭhi munino catudantadhātū,

Siddhatthakhaṇḍakatataṇḍulamuggamattā

Sesā pabhāyapi tidhā pakiriṃsu dhātu; ()

Seven relics of the Sage did not scatter: the four canine teeth, the two collarbones, and the forehead bone. The remaining relics, the size of mustard seeds, broken rice grains, or mung beans, were scattered in three grades.

29. [O 0.0691]

29.

Nibbāpayiṃsu citakānala mantalikkhā

Nikkhamma cāmaramanohara nīradhārā,

Sāḷaddumehi salilāni tathā samantā

Mallā sugandhaparivāsitavārināpi; ()

Streams of water, as lovely as yak-tail whisks, emerged from the sky and extinguished the pyre's fire. Likewise, water from the sāla trees, and the Mallas all around with fragrant scented water, also extinguished it.

30.

30.

Olambamānamaṇidāmasuvaṇṇadāmaṃ

Cittabbitānamathabandhiyamallabhūpā

Katvā sugandhaparibhaṇḍa muḷārasanthā-

Gāre susanthariya kojavakambalāni; ()

Then the Malla kings, in the noble assembly hall, tied up beautiful awnings with hanging garlands of gems and gold, made fragrant arrangements, and spread out fine woolen blankets.

31.

31.

Taṭṭhānato kamakuṭabandhananāmasāḷaṃ

Yāvañjasaṃ rajatakañcanatoraṇehi,

Lājādinā kadalipuṇṇaghaṭehi dīpa-

Dhūpaddhajehi parito patimaṇḍayitvā; ()

Having decorated the path all the way from that place, the Makuṭabandhana shrine, with silver and golden arches, and all around with parched grain, banana trees, full pots, lamps, incense, and flags,

32. [O 0.0692]

32.

Taṃ satthudhātuparipuṇṇa suvaṇṇadoṇiṃ

Mallāna maggapura māhariyu’ssavehi,

Setātapattalasite sarabhāsanamhi

Muttāmaṇīhi khacite tahi mappayitvā; ()

The Mallas carried that golden urn, completely filled with the Teacher’s relics, to their capital city with festivals. Having placed it there on a splendid throne, shaded by a white canopy and inlaid with pearls and gems, they paid homage.

33.

33.

Kumbhena kumbha mupahacca gaḷaṃ gaḷena

Cakkena cakka mupahacca bhujaṃ bhujena,

Rakkhaṃ vidhāya caturaṅginiyā samantā

Senāya hemakavacehi gavacchikaṃva; ()

Pot against pot, neck against neck, wheel against wheel, and arm against arm, they arranged a guard on all sides with the fourfold army, like a lattice-work of golden armor.

34.

34.

Katvevameva dhanurāvaraṇañca satti-

Hatthehi pañjara manantajinassadhātū,

Sammānayiṃsu sumahiṃsu susādhukīḷaṃ

Kīḷiṃsu sattadivasaṃ sahanāgarehi; ()

Having thus made a barrier of bows and a cage of spears held in hand, they honored and paid homage to the relics of the boundless Victor. For seven days, they and the citizens celebrated with excellent festivities.

35. [O 0.0693]

35.

Sutvāna bhupati tamattha majātasattu

Satthāhi khattiyakulappabhavo ahampi,

Sārīrabhāga marahāma mayampi tasmā

Pāhesi dūta matha mallanarādhipānaṃ; ()

Having heard of this matter, King Ajātasattu sent a messenger to the Malla lords, saying: 'The Teacher was of the warrior caste, and so am I. Therefore, I too am worthy of a portion of the bodily relics!'

36.

36.

Vesālikā pacuralicchavibhubhujā ca

Sakyādhipā kapilavatthupurādhivāsī,

Bhūpā’llakappavijite bulayāca rāma-

Gāmamhi koliyamahīpatayo tatheva; ()

And the many Licchavi rulers of Vesālī, the Sakyan lords dwelling in the city of Kapilavatthu, the Buli rulers in the territory of Allakappa, and likewise the Koliyan kings in the village of Rāma—

37.

37.

Yo veṭhadīpanagare dharaṇīsuro so

Pāveyyakā ca mahipā pahiṇiṃsu tesaṃ;

Paccekadūtapurise caturaṅginīhi

Senāhi tepi nivutā’bhimukhībhaviṃsu; ()

The brahmin of the city of Veṭhadīpa and the kings of Pāvā sent their respective messengers to them; they too, surrounded by their fourfold armies, advanced to confront them.

38. [O 0.0694]

38.

Āgamma yena bhagavā sayameva gāma-

Kkhetto’pavattanavane parinibbuto no,

Dassāma no’ti jinadhātulavampi mallā

Pāhesu munnatimanā paṭisāsanāni; ()

Having come to where our Blessed One, self-awakened, attained final Nibbāna in the Upavattana grove, in the vicinity of the village, the Mallas, with proud minds, sent back replies, saying: 'We will not give even a particle of the Victor's relics.'

39.

39.

Sā rājadhāni nijarājapurakkhatāhi

Saṅgāmasūracaturaṅginivāhinīhi,

Yuddhāya baddhakalahāhi khaṇaṃjagāma

Velātivattapalayambudhinibbisesaṃ; ()

That royal city, with its heroic fourfold armies led by its own kings, intent on conflict for the sake of war, in an instant became indistinguishable from a cataclysmic ocean overstepping its bounds.

40. [O 0.0695]

40.

Yo doṇabhusurasudhī bhavi jambudīpe

Rājūhi pūjitapado sunisammakārī,

So doṇagajjanamakā kaparisaṃ vinento

Dvebhāṇavāramita māhavakeḷisajjaṃ; ()

The wise brahmin Doṇa, whose feet were honored by kings in Jambudīpa and who acted with careful consideration, that Doṇa, while taming the assembly, roared like a thundercloud, speaking for the length of two recitations regarding the impending great sport of battle.

41.

41.

Sutvā’nusāsana mathācariyassa tassa

Sabbe samagganiratā vasudhādhināthā,

Atthāya no vibhajathā’ti samena tumhe

Dhātūna maṭṭhapaṭiviṃsaka mabruviṃsu; ()

Having heard the instruction of that teacher, all the lords of the earth, delighting in harmony, said: 'For our benefit, you divide the relics equally.' Thus they spoke to him who was to divide the relics into eight portions.

42.

42.

Khīṇāsavo hi sarabhū citakena gīvā-

Dhātuṃ samāhariya lokahitāya yattha,

Laṅkāya bhāti mahiyaṅgaṇathūparājā

Tasmiṃ samappayi subhe maṇithūpagabbhe; ()

Indeed, Sarabhū, one whose influxes were destroyed, having taken the neck-relic from the pyre for the welfare of the world, placed it in a beautiful jeweled stūpa-chamber where the great Mahiyangana Thūpa shines in Laṅkā.

43. [O 0.0696]

43.

Khemavhayo citakato vasi vāmadāṭhā-

Dhātuṃ samaggahiya’ dāsi kaliṅgarañño,

Doṇodvijo bhariya dhātuvibhāgasajjo

Veṭhantare nidahi dakkhiṇadantadhātuṃ; ()

The master named Khema took the left canine-tooth relic from the pyre and gave it to the king of Kaliṅga. The brahmin Doṇa, while preparing the division of the relics, hid the right tooth-relic inside his turban.

44.

44.

Dāṭhaṃ jaṭārajatacetiyagaṃ dvijassa

Taṃ dakkhiṇakkhaka mapāhari devarājā,

Doṇo suvaṇṇamayadoṇimavāpuritvā

Tesaṃ vibhajja samabhāgamadāsidhātu; ()

The tooth relic of the brahmin went to the silver cetiya of the matted-hair ascetic. The king of the devas carried away the right collar-bone. Doṇa, having filled a golden measuring vessel, divided the relics and gave them out in equal portions.

45.

45.

Te bhubhujā sakasakevisaye vidhāya

Sampūjayiṃsu jinadhātunidhānathūpe

Aṅgāra māhariya moriyakhattiyā’tha

Doṇopi hemamayakumbha makaṃsu thupe; ()

Those kings, having established stūpas enshrining the relics of the Victor in their own respective domains, paid homage. Then the Moriya khattiyas, having taken the embers, built a stūpa, and Doṇa also built a stūpa over the golden urn.

46. [O 0.0697]

46.

Disvāna tassapamahāvasi tatthatattha

Dhātvantarāya matha gaṇhiya rāmagāme,

Aññatra doṇa mitadhātu majātasattu-

Rañño thiraṃ nidahituṃ padadāsi dhātu; ()

Seeing danger to the relics in various places, then, having taken the relics at Rāmagāma—except for the relics measured by the doṇa—King Ajātasattu gave the relics to be firmly enshrined.

47.

47.

Aṭṭha’ṭha vaḍḍhitakaraṇḍakathūpagabbhe

Pakkhippabhumipati dhātumahānidhānaṃ,

So theranāgasaraṇo pavidhāsi vāḷa-

Saṅghāṭayanta miha yojayi devarājā; ()

The lord of the earth, who had taken refuge in the Elder Nāga, deposited the great treasure of relics in a stūpa-chamber with caskets increased eightfold. He arranged a mechanism of vicious interlocking swords; here the king of the devas also assisted.

48.

48.

Rājā asokavidito sirijambudīpe

Tamhā samāhariya satthu sarīradhātu,

Kārāpayī caturasitisahassathūpe

Dhīmā mahindavasi dīpamimaṃ tadā’pa; ()

King Asoka, renowned in glorious Jambudīpa, having collected the Teacher's bodily relics from there, caused eighty-four thousand stūpas to be built. The wise master Mahinda then reached this island.

49. [O 0.0698]

49.

Devānamādipiyatissanarādhipena

Thūpe vidhāya jinadhātacihapattamattā,

Vitthāritā paṇihitā jayabodhisākhā-

Vāmetarakkhakasilāmayapattadhātu; ()

By the king of men, Devānampiyatissa, having made a stūpa and enshrined a bowl-measure of the Victor's relics, the victorious Bodhi-branch was established and spread, along with the right collar-bone and the stone bowl-relic.

50.

50.

Nattā pana’ssa abhayo jalituggatejo

Yo duṭṭhagāmini raṇambudhipāragāmī,

Rājā’nurādhanagare nagarādhirāje

Katvāna laṅkamakalaṅkamakāsirajjaṃ; ()

His grandson, Abhaya, with blazing, exalted power, who was Duṭṭhagāmiṇī, a crosser of the ocean of battle, became king in Anurādhapura, the sovereign city; having made Laṅkā stainless, he ruled the kingdom.

51.

51.

Laṅkaṅganāya kucamaṇḍalanibbisesaṃ

Sovaṇṇamāli matulaṃ ratanujjalantaṃ,

So thuparāja makari thira mappayitvā

Dhātuppabandha mabhinimmitabuddharūpaṃ; ()

He made that king of stūpas, the incomparable Suvaṇṇamāli, glittering with jewels, like a breast-ornament for the lady Laṅkā. Having established it firmly, he arranged a series of relics and fashioned Buddha-images.

52. [O 0.0699]

52.

Sārīrikehi’tarathupavarehi laṅkā-

Bhumitthi moḷimaṇi kañcanamālināma

Saggāpavaggasukhado vara thūparājā

So yāva dhātuparinibbutiyā vibhātu; ()

Among the bodily relics and other excellent stūpas, that excellent king of stūpas named Kañcanamāli is the crest-jewel of the lady that is the land of Laṅkā. Giver of the bliss of heaven and liberation, may it shine until the final passing away of the relics.

53.

53.

Iddhānubhāva madhikicca jinassa dhātu-

Kāyo’pahārarahito garukāraṭhānaṃ,

Patvā tahiṃtahi mathantaradhānakāle

Yo saṅkamissati’ha kañcanamālithupaṃ; ()

By the majestic power of the Victor, the relic-body, which is free from harm and a place for reverence, having come from here and there, will assemble here at the Kañcanamāli stūpa at the time of its disappearance.

54.

54.

So nāgadīpamupagamma tatovidhātu-

Lokā ca nāgabhavanā tidasālayamhā,

Nikkhamma nimmita nirūpamabuddharūpo

Rāsi bhavissati sumaṇḍita bodhimaṇḍe; ()

Having gone to Nāgadīpa, and then emerging from the relic-stūpa there, from the nāga-abode, and from the realm of the gods, it will form an incomparable Buddha-image and become a single mass at the beautifully adorned Bodhimaṇḍa.

55. [O 0.0700]

55.

Buddhānubhāvapabhavā’bhinavaggijālā-

Mālāhi pajjalitadhātumayattabhāve,

Tāvānu’mattamapi dissati nāvasesaṃ

Katvāna dhātuparinibbuti hessateva; ()

Arising from the Buddha’s power, with garlands of fresh flames, the relic-body will burn brightly, leaving not even a particle remaining to be seen; thus the final passing away of the relics will surely occur.

56.

56.

Buddhāpadāna marahādiguṇavadātaṃ

Bhatyā punappuna mimaṃ sarataṃ sataṃ bho,

Cittaṃ kilesapariyuṭṭhita mujjubhūtaṃ

Addhā sudhantakanakaṃva visuddhimeti; ()

O good people, for those who recollect again and again with devotion this life-story of the Buddha, purified by the qualities of Arahantship and so on, their minds, though beset by defilements, having become upright, will surely attain purity like well-refined gold.

57.

57.

Cittojutāyapi vitakkavicāradhammā

Vattanti satthuguṇasañcayagocarā’tha,

Saṃjāyate pavurapīti ca kāyacitta-

Passaddhi niddarathatāya sukhaṃ samādhi; ()

With uprightness of mind, thoughts and reflections occur having the accumulation of the Teacher’s virtues as their object; then excellent joy arises, and tranquility of body and mind, happiness, and concentration, leading to freedom from distress.

58. [O 0.0701]

58.

Gambhīratāya tadadhīnaguṇaṇṇavassa

Niddhutanīvaraṇato pavivekabhūtaṃ,

Chāyetha jhānamupacāra mathā’dhigacche

Tappādakaṃ ariyamga phakhalañca yogī; ()

Due to the depth of that ocean of qualities upon which it depends, and from the dispelling of the hindrances, having become secluded, the yogī might attain the shadow of jhāna, that is, access concentration, and then attain the noble path and its fruit which have that as their basis.

59.

59.

Tassā’ticārucaritassaraṇānuyutto

Hotevava satthari sagāravasapakpatisso,

Saddhindriyādi pariṇāmagato’dhigacche

Pītippamodabahulo kusalo’bhisandaṃ; ()

Being devoted to the recollection of his exceedingly lovely conduct, having reverence and deference towards the Teacher, one attains the maturing of the faculties of faith and so on, and, abounding in joy and gladness, a wholesome increase.

60.

60.

Satthussa cetiyagharaṃva tadattabhāvo

Pūjāraho ca bhayabheravadukkhasayho,

Lajji ca bhīru labhate sahavāsasaññaṃ

Saggāpavaggavibhavassa bhaveyya bhāgī; ()

That person's being becomes worthy of offerings like a shrine-house of the Teacher, and able to endure fear, terror, and suffering. Being modest and conscientious, one obtains the perception of dwelling together with the Teacher and would become a partaker in the glory of heaven and liberation.

61. [O 0.0702]

61.

Laṅkāya lakkhapatigāmavaramhi khettā-

Rāmādhipena guṇabhusaṇabhusitena,

Vikhyātanimmalayasovisarena valli-

Gāmubbhavena parisāvacarakkhamena; ()

By the lord of Khettārāma in the excellent village of Lakkhapatigāma in Laṅkā, one who was adorned with the ornament of virtue, renowned for his stainless and widespread fame, born in Valligāma, and patient with his assembly;

62.

62.

Therenu’pāyacaturena bhadattasaṅghā-

Nandābhidhena garunā garubhāvagena,

Sissoraso’panayanena nijaṃva nettaṃ

Rakkhaṃ vidhāya mabhivuddhiya mappito yo; ()

By the elder skilled in means, named the venerable Saṅghānanda, a teacher of weighty character; I am he who, protected like his own eye and entrusted for my development, was initiated as his own spiritual son.

63.

63.

Yo jīvitampi nirapekkhiya tambapaṇṇī-

Dīpaṃ tivāra mavatiṇṇa mimaṃ vasīhi,

Muttāmaṇīhi khacitena namahagghasiddhagī-

Caṅgoṭakena mahituṃ jinadantadhātuṃ; ()

He who, a master of self-control, disregarding even his life, descended to this island of Tambapaṇṇī three times to honor the Victor's tooth-relic with a priceless casket worthy of siddhas, inlaid with pearls and gems.

64. [O 0.0703]

64.

Sikkhāgaruṃ vajiranāma vihārasāmiṃ

Rājādhirājagurulañchadharaṃ yatindaṃ,

Katvānu’pajjhamupasampādamāpa dhamma-

Majjhetu motariya rammamarammaraṭṭhaṃ; ()

Having made the lord of ascetics, Vajiranāma—master of the monastery, bearer of the insignia of the teacher to the king of kings, and a teacher of the training—his preceptor, he obtained higher ordination and went down to the delightful land of the Marammas to study the Dhamma.

65.

65.

Saṃvaḍḍhitaṃ pitupadādhigatena meṇḍuna

Raññā pasīdiya kusaggadhiyā sakāya,

Sissaṃ asesapariyattidharassa ñeyya-

Dhammābhivaṃsaviditassa’pi saṅgharañño; ()

Having been nurtured by the king, who was pleased with my sharp intellect, I became a pupil of the Saṅgharāja, known as Ñeyyadhammābhivaṃsa, a master of the entire scriptures.

66.

66.

Saṃjayuttabhāṇakakumārabhivaṃsanāmaṃ

Rājādhirājagarulañchadharaṃ sudhīraṃ,

Therāsabhaṃ supaṭipattigaruṃ garuṃ yo

Nissāya dhammavinaye paṭutaṃ jagāma; ()

Relying on that teacher, the very wise Saṃjayuttabhāṇakakumārabhivaṃsa, a bull among elders who bore the insignia of the teacher to the king of kings and was respected for his good practice, I attained skill in the Dhamma and Vinaya.

67. [O 0.0704]

67.

Lakkhīsare moraṭunāmapure suramme

Jātena issarajanāyananamhi jātyā,

Vassaṭṭhatiṃsaparimāṇavayoguṇena

Pāsāṇadūrapuragocaragāmikena; ()

By one born in the beautiful city of Moraṭu, endowed with fortune, of noble lineage, at the age of thirty-eight, a resident of the village within the domain of Pāsāṇadūrapura;

68.

68.

Tenā’bhayādikaruṇāratanābhidhānā-

Rāmādhipena gaṇvācakābhāvagena,

Saṃsuddhabuddhaguṇādīpanatapparena

Saṃsārasāgarasamuttaraṇāsayena; ()

By him, named Abhayādikaruṇāratana, the lord of the Rāma monastery, who is without the status of a group-teacher, intent on illuminating the completely pure qualities of the Buddha, with the intention of crossing over the ocean of saṃsāra;

69.

69.

Pītippamodajananaṃ samaṇena medhā-

Nandābhidhena kavinā kavikuñjarānaṃ,

Ādiccabandhujinarājaguṇappabandha-

Suddhāpadānaparidīpakathāsarīraṃ; ()

This work, generating joy and delight, was composed by the monk named Medhānanda, a poet pre-eminent among poets. It is the body of the discourse illuminating the pure life stories of the Jina-King, the Kinsman of the Sun;

70. [O 0.0705]

70.

Saddānusāsani’tihāsanighaṇṭuchando-

Laṅkārasāra mabhidhammakathāgabhīraṃ,

Saggāpavaggasukhadaṃ samatiṃsasaggaṃ

Vyākhyāsameta manurūpa padappayogaṃ; ()

Profound in the essence of grammar, history, lexicon, prosody, and rhetoric; deep in the discourse of the Abhidhamma; bestowing the bliss of heaven and liberation; comprising thirty chapters, complete with commentary and the fitting use of words;

71.

71.

Dvisahassabandhasamākulaṃ jinavaṃsadīpamanākulaṃ

Racitaṃ samāpa samāpanaṃ paramaṃpabandhasiromaṇiṃ,

Subhamāghamāsikavāsare nirupaddavena tathāgate

Parinibbute dvisahassasaṭṭhicatussatodayahāyate; ()

The composition of the Jinavaṃsadīpa—that supreme crest-jewel of treatises, free from confusion and comprising two thousand verses—was brought to completion without any obstacle on an auspicious day in the month of Māgha, in the year 2460 after the Tathāgata’s Parinibbāna.

Iti medhānandābhidhānena yatinā viracite sakalakavijana hadayānandadāna nidāne jinavaṃsadīpe santikenidāne bhagavato dhātuparinibbānappavattiparidīpo tiṃsatimosaggo.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, the 'Elucidation of the Occurrence of the Complete Extinction of the Blessed One's Relics,' in the Santikenidāna section of the Jinavaṃsadīpa—the source that bestows joy upon the hearts of all poets—composed by the ascetic named Medhānanda.

Sātireko santikenidānabhāgo tatiyo.

The third section, the Santikenidāna, with its supplement.
